STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.claim: Most of 4:1–36, 4:127–130, and 4:176 is legislative, as are its instructions for conduct in war and peace.
STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.anchor: Most of the first part (vv. 1–36, 127–30, 176) is legislative in nature, as is the section dealing with war and peace

SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.claim: A mubtadaʾ and its predicate are two necessary parts; neither can replace the other.
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.anchor: وهما ما لا يغنى واحد منهما عن الآخر ولا يجد المتكلم منه بدا

SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.claim: A verb likewise requires its subject noun, just as the initial noun requires what is predicated of it.

SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.claim: Particles such as kāna and layta also require a following complement; a noun's initial state is mubtadaʾ until a governing word changes its case.
SIBAWAYH:وهمامالايغنىواحدمنهماعنالآخرولا.anchor: ومما يكون بمنزلة الابتداء قولك كان عبد الله منطلقا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.claim: A vessel's contents may be accusative, genitive directly, or introduced by من; the accusative treats the material as what the vessel contains.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.anchor: هذا راقود خلا وعليه نحى سمنا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.claim: Material nouns such as طين name a substance rather than an adjective; they may be a circumstantial accusative or a predicate, but وصف خز is bad.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.anchor: الطين اسم وليس مما يوصف به

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاراقودخلاوعليهنحىسمنا.claim: A material noun after a governing expression follows noun case behavior; جبتك خزا is a حال, while جبتك خز is predicated of the mubtadaʾ.

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r1.claim: Compared with the parallel in 2:83, this verse repeats ب before ذي القربى because it addresses this community, where kin deserve greater attention; repetition adds emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r1.anchor: وذلك لأنها في حق هذه الأمة فالاعتناء بها أكثر

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r2.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads إحسان in the nominative as subject with the preceding prepositional phrase as predicate; the statement expresses a command, like فصبر جميل in 12:18.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة " إحسان " بالرفع، على أنه مبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r3.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r3.claim: The majority’s genitive الجار ذي القربى means a neighbor related by blood; الجار الجنب is a neighbor distant in lineage.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r3.anchor: المراد به القريب النسب، وبالجار الجنب البعيد النسب

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r4.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r4.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran interprets الجار ذي القربى as the nearby neighbor; Ibn ʿAtiyya calls this wrong because it combines ال with annexation, which should instead be جار ذي القربى.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r4.anchor: وعن ميمون بن مهران: " والجار ذي القربى أريد به الجار القريب "

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r5.claim: The author salvages Maymun’s sense by making ذي القربى an appositive with an omitted annexed noun, “neighbor of a kin-neighbor,” as in the cited Talha and علم الكبيرة examples.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r5.anchor: على حذف مضاف أي: والجار جار ذي القربى

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r6.claim: Some read الجار ذا القربى in the accusative; al-Zamakhshari parses it as an اختصاص construction, like الصلاة الوسطى in 2:238.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r6.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: " والجار ذا القربى " نصبا. وخرجه الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r7.claim: جنب is an adjective on فعْل like ناقة سرح, invariant across gender and number; some speakers inflect it, as with شلل.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r7.anchor: يستوي فيه المفرد والمثنى والمجموع مذكرا ومؤنثا

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r8.speaker: عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r8.claim: Asim reads الجنب with fatḥa on jim and a still nūn; it is an adjective meaning “neighboring,” like رجل عدل.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r8.anchor: وعن عاصم: " والجار الجنب " بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r9.claim: جنب derives from being at a side; its alif reflects wāw in تجاوروا and جاورته, it pluralizes as جيرة and جيران, and جنابة means distance, as the poem and 14:35 illustrate.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36/r9.anchor: لأن الإنسان يترك جانبا، ومنه: واجنبني وبني

SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r1.claim: In بالصاحب بالجنب, ب may mean “in” or retain its ordinary sense; the author prefers the ordinary sense, and either way it modifies الصاحب as a circumstantial phrase with an omitted governor.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن تكون بمعنى " في ". والثاني: أن تكون على بابها

SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r2.claim: ما ملكت أيمانكم may refer to owned kinds other than enslaved men and women, with ما used for types as in 4:3.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يريد غير العبيد والإماء

SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, ما encompasses all animals a person owns; ما is used because rational and nonrational kinds are mixed.
SAMIN-DURR:4:36#2/r3.anchor: وأن يكون أريد جميع ما ملكه الإنسان من الحيوانات

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r1.claim: Worship God without associating anything with Him, since worship of another alongside Him corrupts one's worship.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r1.anchor: أي لا تعبدوا معه غيره، فإن ذلك يفسد عبادته.

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r2.claim: God enjoined His worship and kindness to parents; in 17:23, qaḍā likewise means commanded and enjoined.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r2.anchor: المعنى أوصاكم الله بعبادته، وأوصاكم بالوالدين إحسانا، وكذلك قوله تعالى: (وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا). لأن معنى قضى ههنا أمر ووصى.

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r3.speaker: بعض النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r3.claim: Some grammarians parse iḥsānan as an accusative verbal noun governed by an omitted command, as in ḍarban Zaydan.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r3.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين (إحسانا) منصوب على وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا. كما تقول: ضربا زيدا، المعنى اضرب زيدا ضربا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r4.claim: God commands kindness to kin after parents, and likewise to orphans, the poor, and all groups named.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r4.anchor: أمر الله بالإحسان إلى ذوي القربى بعد الوالدين. و (اليتامى) في موضع جر. المعنى وباليتامى والمساكين أوصاكم أيضا

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r5.claim: The near neighbor is close to you and known to you, as you are known to him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r5.anchor: أي الجار الذي يقاربك وتعرفه ويعرفك.

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r6.claim: Al-jār al-junub means a distant neighbor.

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r7.speaker: علقمة
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r7.claim: ʿAlqama's verse uses janābah for distance, supporting the meaning of al-jār al-junub.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r7.anchor: قال علقمة: فلا تحرمني نائلا عن جنابة. . . فإني امرؤ وسط القباب غريب

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r8.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r8.claim: Some identify the companion at one's side as a traveling companion.

ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r9.claim: The son of the road is a guest who must be hosted and helped to reach his destination.
ZAJJAJ:v2p49/r9.anchor: الضيف يجب قراه، وأن يبلغ حيث يريد.

ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r1.claim: Show kindness to those under one's authority; mā is coordinated with the preceding objects of kindness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r1.anchor: أي وأحسنوا بملك أيمانكم، موضع ما عطف على ما قبلها.

ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r2.speaker: النبي
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r2.claim: The Prophet's final counsel was prayer and care for those held in one's right hands.
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r2.anchor: وكانت وصية النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عند وفاته: " الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم ".

ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r3.claim: Mukhtāl describes an arrogant, conceited, boastful, foolish person.

ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r4.claim: Arrogant people disdain poor relatives and neighbors and so fail to treat them well; this explains the warning.
ZAJJAJ:v2p50/r4.anchor: وإنما ذكر الاختيال في هذه القصة. لأن المختال يأنف من ذوي قراباته إذا كانوا فقراء، ومن جيرانه إذا كانوا كذلك، فلا يحسن عشرتهم.

ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n46/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n46/r1.claim: The word shay’an makes shirk broader than worshipping other deities: it includes assigning divine or quasi-divine powers to people or objects not viewed as deities, such as saint-worship.
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n46/r1.anchor: is not confined to a worship of other "deities", but implies also the attribution of divine or quasi-divine powers

ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r1.claim: “Your own people” means someone from your own community, not an actual relative, since near of kin were already mentioned; the other neighbor is from another community.
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r1.anchor: the expression "your own people" (dhu l-qurba) refers to the community and not to one's actual relatives

ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r2.speaker: the Prophet
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r2.claim: The Prophet stressed believers’ moral duty to neighbors regardless of faith, summarized by the instruction to do good to one’s neighbor; Asad cites Bukhari, Muslim, and other compilations.
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n47/r2.anchor: The Prophet often stressed a believer's moral obligation towards his neighbours, whatever their faith

ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r1.speaker: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and other Companions
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r1.claim: Companions identified “the friend by your side” as one's wife or husband.
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r1.anchor: According to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and other Companions, "the friend by your side" (as-sahib bi'l-janb) is one's wife or husband (Tabari).

ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r2.claim: In this context, those whom one's right hand possesses are enslaved people of either sex.
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r2.anchor: By "those whom you rightfully possess" (lit., "whom your right hands possess") are meant, in this context, slaves of either sex.

ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r3.claim: Because freeing a slave is the best good one can do for them, the command elliptically calls for emancipation; 2:177 and 9:60 explicitly make freeing people a zakah objective.
ASAD-NOTES:4:36#n48/r3.anchor: Since this verse enjoins the "doing of good" towards all people with whom one is in contact, and since the best that can be done to a slave is to free him, the above passage calls, elliptically, for the freeing of slaves (Manar V, 94).

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r1.claim: “Shayʾan” can be a direct object forbidding worship of any thing, or an absolute object forbidding any degree of shirk; the author intends both readings, including subtle shirk.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r1.anchor: كلمة (شيئا) تحتمل المعنيين أي لا تشركوا بالله شيئاً من الأشياء ولا شيئاً من الشرك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r1.claim: In ولا تشركوا به شيئاً, شيئاً may be a direct object meaning any thing worshipped, or an absolute object meaning any form of shirk.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r1.anchor: وعنده يُعرب مفعول به أو لا تشركوا به شيئاً من الشرك لأن الشرك أنواع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r2.claim: He takes both senses together: do not associate any object or any degree of shirk with God, including subtle forms of shirk.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r2.anchor: نهانا سبحانه عن الشرك به شيئاً من الأشياء أو شيئاً من الشرك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r3.claim: The absolute object may be represented by several substitutes, including an adjective, pronoun, or ordinary concrete noun.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r3.anchor: المفعول المطلق المصدر ينوب عنه أشياء كثيرة فقد تنوب عنه صفته والضمير والمصدر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r4.claim: As an example, سكيناً in طعنه سكيناً is an absolute object standing for the instrument, meaning he stabbed him with a knife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r4.anchor: طعنه سكيناً عند النحاة هو مفعول مطلق بمعنى طعنه بسكين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r6.claim: When only one sense is intended, the Qur'an can specify it, as in 18:110; wording open to several senses instead gives broader meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r6.anchor: ولو أراد تعالى التحديد والتخصيص بمعنى واحد لفعل كما في قوله تعالى (ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا)

IBNMAJAH:1625/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:1625/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:1625/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that during his final illness the Prophet repeatedly urged care for prayer and those under one's right hand, until he could barely speak.
IBNMAJAH:1625/r1.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي مَرَضِهِ الَّذِي تُوُفِّيَ فِيهِ

IBNMAJAH:2697/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:2697/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:2697/r1.claim: Anas reports that prayer and care for those under one's right hand made up most of the Prophet’s counsel as he was dying.
IBNMAJAH:2697/r1.anchor: كَانَتْ عَامَّةُ وَصِيَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ حَضَرَتْهُ الْوَفَاةُ

IBNMAJAH:2698/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:2698/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNMAJAH:2698/r1.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet’s final words urged observance of prayer and care for those under one's right hand.
IBNMAJAH:2698/r1.anchor: كَانَ آخِرُ كَلاَمِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r1.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r1.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim alone reads al-janb with fatḥa on jīm and sukūn on nūn; others read both with ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r1.anchor: قال أحمد: روى أبو زيد سعيد بن أوس الأنصاري عن المفضل عن عاصم: والجار الجنب [النساء/ 36] بفتح الجيم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses the near neighbor as a relative and the distant neighbor as a stranger; janāba means distance, as ʿAlqama’s poem shows.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: والجار ذي القربى: القريب، والجار الجنب: الغريب

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r3.claim: Al-Fārisī gives two analyses: janb means a side, with an elided ‘possessor of’ phrase, or an adjective meaning one separated from relatives; both yield a stranger neighbor.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: قوله تعالى: والجار الجنب، يحتمل معنيين: أحدهما: أن يريد الناحية

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r4.claim: The side sense is supported by the rajaz ‘people are janb and the ruler is janb’; poems by al-Aʿshā and another poet support the sense of distance from kin.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r4.anchor: قال الراجز : الناس جنب والأمير جنب

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r6.claim: The companion by one’s side is a traveling companion who stays and lodges beside one.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p157/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: والصاحب بالجنب: الذي يصاحبك في سفرك، فيلزمك

NASHR:v2p248/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p248/r14.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p248/r14.claim: Yaʿqūb assimilates in والصاحب بالجنب as does Abū ʿAmr in the large-assimilation chapter.
NASHR:v2p248/r14.anchor: مذهب يعقوب في إدغام والصاحب بالجنب كأبي عمرو من باب الإدغام الكبير

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r1.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r1.claim: Qatada and Mujahid define the near neighbor as a neighbor who is also a relative.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r1.anchor: عن قتادة وعن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ والجار ذي القربى ﴾ قالا هو جارك وهو ذو قرابتك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r2.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r2.claim: Qatada and Mujahid define the distant neighbor as a neighbor from another people or community.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r2.anchor: ﴿ والجار الجنب ﴾ جارك من قوم آخرين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r3.claim: Qatada and Mujahid identify the companion by one’s side as one’s travel companion.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r4.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r4.claim: Qatada and Mujahid define the wayfarer as a traveler passing by.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p159/r4.anchor: ﴿ وابن السبيل ﴾ الذي يمر عليك وهو مسافر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r1.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says the companion by one’s side is one’s travel companion.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله تعالى ﴿ والصاحب بالجنب ﴾ قال الرفيق في السفر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r2.claim: Ibrahim offers a different referent for the companion by one’s side: a wife.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p160/r2.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم عن إبراهيم هي المرأة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:693/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:693/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:693/r1.claim: Ali reports that near the Prophet's death he urged care for prayer, zakat, and those under one's care, echoing the verse's charge concerning those whom one's right hand possesses.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:693/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، قال: أمرني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن آتيه بطبق يكتب فيه ما لا تضل أمته

MUSNAD-AHMAD:12169/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12169/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12169/r1.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet's recurring deathbed counsel stressed prayer and kindness toward those under one's care, matching the verse's concern for those one possesses.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12169/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن أنس قال: كانت عامة وصية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين حضره الموت

MUSNAD-AHMAD:26483/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26483/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26483/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that among the Prophet's last counsels were repeated injunctions to prayer and to those under one's care, consonant with the verse's instruction.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26483/r1.anchor: عن سفينة، مولى أم سلمة عن أم سلمة، قالت: كان من آخر وصية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:26657/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26657/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26657/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that the dying Prophet kept repeating the injunctions to pray and attend to those under one's care, recalling the verse's latter duty.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26657/r1.anchor: عن أبي الخليل، عن سفينة، مولى أم سلمة، عن أم سلمة، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين حضر

MUSNAD-AHMAD:26684/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26684/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26684/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet's main deathbed counsel was prayer and those under one's care, echoing this verse's injunction.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26684/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: حدث سفينة، مولى أم سلمة، عن أم سلمة، زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان عامة وصية نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:26727/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26727/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26727/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that as he was dying, the Prophet repeatedly urged prayer and care for those under one's authority, as in the verse.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:26727/r1.anchor: عن أبي الخليل، عن سفينة، مولى أم سلمة، عن أم سلمة، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال وهو في الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r1.claim: Al-jār is someone living near you; its alif derives from wāw, as shown by jāwartu, and its plurals are jīrān and jīra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r1.anchor: الجار: القريب المسكن منك، وألفه منقلبة عن واو لقولهم: جاورت، ويجمع على جيران وجيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r2.claim: Al-janb means distant, and janāba is distance; the cited verse of poetry uses janāba in that sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r2.anchor: والجنب: البعيد. والجنابة البعد قال: فلا تحرمني نائلا عن جنابة ... فإني امرؤ وسط القباب غريب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r3.claim: Al-janb derives from ijtināb, leaving something to one side; ajnibnī means keep me far away, and janb is an adjective on the pattern of sarḥ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607#2/r3.anchor: وهو من الاجتناب، وهو أن يترك الرجل جانبا. وقال تعالى: واجنبني أي بعدني، وهو وصف على فعل كناقة سرح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r9.claim: After male responsibility toward wives, grounded in God's preference and men's spending, the verse explains that men also owe benevolence to parents and all the other listed groups; ethical duties extend beyond one's wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r9.anchor: أنه تعالى لما ذكر أن الرجال قوامون على النساء بتفضيل الله إياهم عليهن، وبإنفاق أموالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r10.claim: The call to single out God in worship opens this passage because worship is the foundation from which righteous deeds follow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r10.anchor: وافتتح التوصل إلى ذلك بالأمر بإفراد الله تعالى بالعبادة، إذ هي مبدأ الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r11.claim: The verse parallels the Israelite covenant in 2:83, with similar commands to worship God and treat parents well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r11.anchor: ونظير: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله وبالوالدين إحسانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r12.claim: Unlike the parallel at 2:83, this verse repeats the preposition ب before ذو القربى, intensifying the emphasis on kin, orphans, and the poor; Abū Ḥayyān links the greater emphasis to this community's special honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r12.anchor: وإعادة الباء تدل على التوكيد والمبالغة، فبولغ في هذه الآية لأنها في حق هذه الأمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r13.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r13.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblā reads إحسان in the nominative, parsing it as subject and predicate while retaining the imperative force of a command in a declarative form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p630/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: وبالوالدين إحسان بالرفع، وهو مبتدأ وخبر فيه ما في المنصوب من معنى الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة وابن زيد ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatāda, Ibn Zayd, Muqātil, and others say the near-kindred neighbor is related by blood and the distant neighbor has no kinship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ومجاهد، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وقتادة، وابن زيد، ومقاتل في آخرين: هو الجار القريب النسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r2.speaker: بلعاء بن قيس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r2.claim: The poet Bulʿāʾ b. Qays attests الجار الجنب as a neighbor who is not kin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r2.anchor:
وقال بلعاء بن قيس:
لا يجتوينا مجاور أبدا ... ذو رحم أو مجاور جنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r3.speaker: نوف الشامي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r3.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī takes the near neighbor to be a Muslim and the distant neighbor a Jew or Christian: Islamic kinship contrasts with religious foreignness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r3.anchor: وقال نوف الشامي: هو الجار المسلم. والجار الجنب هو: الجار اليهودي، والنصراني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r4.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r4.claim: A group interprets the two neighbors spatially: one lives close by, the other farther away, deriving the distinction from the report about giving a gift to the neighbor nearest one's door.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة، هو الجار القريب المسكن منك، والجنب هو البعيد المسكن منك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r5.claim: A report says someone with two neighbors asked which should receive a gift; the Prophet said the one whose door is nearer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r5.anchor: إن لي جارين فإلى أيهما أهدي؟ قال: «إلى أقربهما منك بابا»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r6.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r6.claim: Maymūn b. Mihrān says the phrase means the neighbor who is close; Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that this reading combines the definite article with an annexation improperly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r6.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران: والجار ذي القربى أريد به الجار القريب. قال ابن عطية: وهذا خطأ في اللسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reconciles Maymūn's interpretation by taking ذي القربى as an appositive after an omitted جار: 'the neighbor, neighbor of kin'; he supports such ellipsis with poetic and Arabic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r7.anchor: ويمكن تصحيح قول ميمون على أن لا يكون جمعا بين الألف واللام والإضافة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r8.claim: Junub means distant and is so named because of distance from kinship; a verse uses عن جنابة in this sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r8.anchor: والجنب: هو البعيد، سمي بذلك لبعده عن القرابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r9.claim: Four definitions of neighborhood are given: co-residence in a district or city, forty homes in every direction (attributed to al-Awzāʿī), hearing the call to prayer, or hearing the iqāma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r9.anchor: والمجاورة مساكنة الرجل الرجل في محلة، أو مدينة، أو كينونة أربعين دارا من كل جانب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r10.claim: A report says the Prophet ordered a caller to announce that forty houses count as neighbors and that one whose neighbor is unsafe from his harms will not enter Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p631/r10.anchor: وروى في ذلك حديثا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام «أمر مناديه ينادي: «ألا إن أربعين دارا جوار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r1.claim: A poetic address calls a woman a neighbor and says she is divorced, illustrating the neighboring relationship the passage treats.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r2.claim: A reading with ذا in the accusative is parsed by al-Zamakhsharī as specification, like the accusative الصلاة الوسطى at 2:238, emphasizing the neighbor's dual claim of proximity and kinship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r2.anchor: وقرىء: والجار ذا القربى. قال الزمخشري: نصبا على الاختصاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r3.speaker: عاصم في رواية المفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r3.claim: In al-Mufaḍḍal's transmission, ʿĀṣim reads الجار الجنب with fatḥa on jīm and sukūn on nūn; it means the distant neighbor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية المفضل عنه: والجار الجنب بفتح الجيم وسكون النون، ومعناه البعيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r4.speaker: أعرابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r4.claim: A Bedouin defines the distant neighbor as someone who comes and settles wherever your eye happens to fall on him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r4.anchor: وسئل أعرابي عن الجار الجنب فقال: هو الذي يجيء فيحل حيث تقع عينك عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take the companion at one's side as a fellow traveler.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وابن جبير، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والضحاك: هو الرفيق في السفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r6.speaker: علي وابن مسعود والنخعي وابن أبي ليلى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r6.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, al-Nakhaʿī, and Ibn Abī Laylā identify the companion at one's side as one's wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r6.anchor: وقال علي وابن مسعود والنخعي، وابن أبي ليلى: الزوجة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says it is someone who comes by and spends time with you so that you may benefit him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو من يعتريك ويلم بك لتنفعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī broadens the phrase to anyone beside you: a travel companion, adjacent neighbor, study or trade partner, or seatmate in an assembly or mosque; each companionship creates a right to observe and a reason for kindness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هو الذي صحبك بأن حصل يجنبك إما رفيقا في سفر، وإما جارا ملاصقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r9.claim: Mujāhid also says it is a companion in travel or at home; another view specifies a righteous companion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: هو الذي يصحبك سفرا وحضرا. وقيل: الرفيق الصالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān refers readers to his earlier explanation of ابن السبيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r11.claim: One view uses ما for rational beings by category, as in 4:3; another says it is broader than من and includes all owned animals, enslaved humans and other animals alike.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r11.anchor: قيل: ما وقعت على العاقل باعتبار النوع كقوله تعالى: فانكحوا ما طاب لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r12.claim: Because owned animals outnumber enslaved people, the command to show kindness covers every owned person and animal; several hadiths in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere commend kindness to slaves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r12.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى بالإحسان إلى كل مملوك من آدمي وحيوان غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r13.speaker: سهل التستري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r13.claim: Sahl al-Tustarī reads the near neighbor inwardly as the heart, distant neighbor as the self, companion at one's side as the intellect guiding adherence to Sunna and law, and wayfarer as obedient limbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r13.anchor: ومن غريب التفسير ما نقل عن سهل التستري قال: الجار ذو القربى هو القلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r14.claim: Mukhtāl is arrogant; fakhūr boasts of his merits to exalt himself over people. These traits lead one to neglect the needy people listed in the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r14.anchor: الاختيال وهو التكبر، والفخر هو عد المناقب على سبيل التطاول بها والتعاظم على الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r15.speaker: أبو رجاء الهروي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r15.claim: Abū Rajāʾ al-Harawī says a bad master is invariably arrogant and boastful, while one who mistreats parents is tyrannical and wretched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r15.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء الهروي: لا تجد سيىء الملكة إلا وجدته مختالا فخورا، ولا عاقا إلا وجدته جبارا شقيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes the arrogant person as a conceited, ignorant boaster who refuses to honor relatives, companions, and slaves, and does not welcome or attend to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p632/r16.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والمختال التياه الجهول الذي يتكبر عن إكرام أقاربه وأصحابه ومماليكه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p635/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p635/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p635/r18.claim: If linked to the preceding phrase, the passage addresses believers: show kindness to those named, since God dislikes arrogance, pride, miserliness, urging it, and concealing provision.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p635/r18.anchor: أحسنوا أيها المؤمنون إلى من سمى الله،

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r1.claim: This new instruction follows counsel to spouses on kind treatment and resolving discord; it reinforces marital rights and teaches good dealings with all classes of people.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r1.anchor: مسوق للإرشاد إلى خلال مشتملة على معالي الأمور إثر إرشاد كل من الزوجين إلى المعاملة الحسنة وإزالة الخصومة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r2.claim: God's rights are placed first because they are the greatest foundation; that order also signals the high standing of the duties listed after them.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r2.anchor: وقدم الأمر بما يتعلق بحقوق الله تعالى لأنها المدار الأعظم وفي ذلك إيماء أيضا إلى ارتفاع شأن ما نظم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r3.claim: Worship is the utmost degree of submission.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r4.claim: شيئا may be a direct object, with indefinite tanwin generalizing the prohibition to anything whatsoever, idol or otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r4.anchor: و ( شيئا ) إما مفعول به أي لا تشركوا به شيئا من الأشياء

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r5.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r5.claim: Isam al-Din takes the tanwin as belittling: associating even a contemptible thing with God's limitless greatness merits severe rebuke.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r5.anchor: واختار عصام الدين كونه للتحقير ليكون فيه توبيخ عظيم أي لا تشركوا به شيئا حقيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r6.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r6.claim: He argues that relating a contingent being to the Necessary is more remote than relating nonexistence to existence, since nonexistence is the possibility of existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r6.anchor: ونسب الممكن إلى الواجب أبعد من نسبة المعدوم إلى الموجود إذ المعدوم إمكان الموجود

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r7.claim: Alternatively شيئا is a verbal noun: associate nothing with God, whether openly or secretly.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r7.anchor: وإما مصدر أي لا تشركوا به عز شأنه من الإشراك جليا أو خفيا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r8.claim: The ban may follow because worship as total submission cannot be directed to one who has a partner, or to rebuke people for missing that implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r8.anchor: للنهي عن الإشراك فيما جعله الشرع علامة نهاية الخضوع أو للتوبيخ بغاية الجهل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r9.claim: Al-Alusi says the clearer reading is that the prohibition commands sincerity, restating worship as worshipping God alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r9.anchor: ولعل الأوضح أن يقال : إن هذا النهي إشارة إلى الأمر بالإخلاص

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r10.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r10.claim: The Imam explains the sequence as a general command covering heart and bodily acts followed by its specific core, monotheism, without which God accepts no deed; it is coordination of the specific with the general.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r10.anchor: إلى أن سبحانه أمر أولا بما يشمل التوحيد وغيره من أعمال القلب والجوارح ثم أردفه بما يفهم منه التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r11.claim: The phrase means and treat both parents well: the preposition may modify an omitted verb or the verbal noun; it is fronted for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r11.anchor: أي وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا فالجار متعلق بالفعل المقدر وجوز تعلقه بالمصدر وقدم للاهتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r12.claim: أحسن takes باء, إلى, or لام; one view allows باء only when the verb conveys affection.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r12.anchor: وأحسن يتعدى بالباء وإلى واللام وقيل : إنما يتعدى بالباء إذا تضمن معنى العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r13.claim: Kindness includes serving parents, not raising one's voice or speaking harshly, meeting their needs, and supporting them within one's means.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r13.anchor: أن يقوم بخدمتهما ولا يرفع صوته عليهما ولا يخشن في الكلام معهما ويسعى في تحصيل مطالبهما

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r14.claim: ذو القربى means a relative, such as a brother, uncle, maternal uncle, or their children.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r14.anchor: أي بصاحب القرابة من أخ وعو وخال وأولاد كل نحو ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r15.claim: The preposition is repeated here, unlike al-Baqara, because this is counsel to this community and is therefore emphasized; the earlier instruction addressed the Children of Israel.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28/r15.anchor: وأعيد الباء هنا ولم يعد في البقرة قال في البحر : لأن هذا توصية لهذه الأمة فاعتني به وأكد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r1.claim: The orphans and poor in this phrase are those outside one's family.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r2.claim: One reading of near neighbor is a neighbor close by location.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, near neighbor is also connected by kinship or religion, while the distant neighbor has no kinship or is an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالجار ذي القربى من له مع الجوار قرب واتصال بنسب أو دين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r4.claim: A report through Abu Nuaym and al-Bazzar, which al-Alusi says is weak, assigns three rights to the kin Muslim neighbor, two to a Muslim neighbor without kinship, and one to a non-Muslim neighbor from the People of the Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r4.anchor: أخرج أبو نعيم والبزار من حديث جابر بن عبدالله وفيه ضعف قال : قال رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r5.speaker: عبدالله بن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r5.claim: Al-Bukhari's Adab collection reports Ibn Umar repeatedly telling his servant to give meat to their Jewish neighbor, citing the Prophet's teaching that Gabriel kept urging care for neighbors until he thought they would inherit.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج البخاري في الأدب عن عبدالله بن عمر أنه ذبحت له شاة فجعل يقول لغلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r6.claim: The customary understanding of neighborhood determines who counts as a neighbor.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن مبنى الجوار على العرف

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan defines a neighbor as extending forty houses in front, behind, to the right, and to the left; a similar report is attributed to al-Zuhri.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن كما في الأدب أنه سئل عن الجار فقال : أربعين دارا أمامه وأربعين خلفه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.claim: Another view defines the neighbor's distance as forty cubits.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.claim: Aisha asked which of two neighbors should receive a gift; the Prophet said to choose the one whose door is nearer.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.anchor: فعن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : قلت : يا رسول الله إن لي جارين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.claim: A variant reads الجار ذي القربى in the accusative, meaning and I single out the near neighbor, highlighting the neighbor's right.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.anchor: وقرئ والجار ذي القربى بالنصب أي وأخص الجار وفي ذلك تنبيه على عظم حق الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.speaker: أبو شريح الخزاعي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.claim: The two Sahih collections transmit Abu Shurayh's report from the Prophet: whoever believes in God and the Last Day should treat his neighbor well.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.anchor: وقد أخرج الشيخان عن أبي شريح الخزاعي أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : من كان يؤمن

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for two meanings of the companion at one's side: a travel companion or someone who relies on you and seeks your aid.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.anchor: وهو الرفيق في السفر أو المنقطع إليك يرجو نفعك ورفدك وكلا القولين عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r13.claim: Another interpretation is a companion in a good undertaking such as learning, trade, a craft, or travel; some include anyone who sits beside one in a mosque, gathering, or other brief companionship, a view praised for its breadth.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : الرفيق في أمر حسن كتعلم وتصرف وصناعة وسفر وعدوا من ذلك من قعد بجنبك في مسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r14.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r14.claim: Ali says the companion at one's side is one's wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r14.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه الصاحب بالجنب المرأة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r15.claim: The prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element serving as a circumstantial modifier of الصاحب, governed by the estimated verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r15.anchor: والجار متعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من الصاحب والعامل فيه الفعل المقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r16.claim: Ibn al-sabil means a traveler or guest.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r17.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r17.claim: Muqatil identifies those possessed by the right hand as male and female slaves.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r18.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r18.claim: Ahmad and al-Bayhaqi transmit from Anas that the Prophet's final counsel repeatedly included prayer and those under one's authority, even as his speech failed near death.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r18.anchor: فقد أخرج أحمد والبيهقي عن أنس قال : كان عامة وصية رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم حين حضره الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r19.claim: The required degree of kindness to these various groups differs according to what suits each one.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r19.anchor: ثم الإحسان إلى هؤلاء الأصناف متفاوت المراتب حسبما يليق بكل وينبغي

ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r20.claim: Mukhtal means arrogant and conceited, disdaining relatives and neighbors and ignoring them.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p28#2/r20.anchor: أي ذا خيلاء وكبر يأنف من أقاربه وجيرانه مثلا ولا يلتفت إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r1.claim: Fakhur is someone who vaunts his merits over others with pride.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r2.claim: The warning that God does not love the arrogant explains the preceding commands to kindness.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r3.speaker: ثابت بن قيس بن شماس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r3.claim: Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh report that Thabit ibn Qays wept after hearing the verse and fearing its warning; he loved fine appearance, even in his sandal strap. The Prophet reassured him that beautifying one's mount and belongings is not arrogance, which is rejecting truth and belittling people.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p29/r3.anchor: أخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه عن ثابت بن قيس بن شماس قال : كنت عند رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r1.claim: Worship God by turning toward Him and becoming annihilated in Him; do not associate anything imagined as existent, since nothing besides Him truly exists.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r1.anchor: مما تحسبونه شيئا وليس بشئ إذ لا وجود حقيقة لغيره سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r2.claim: The parents allegorically are spirit and soul, between which the heart is born; receive effusion from the spirit and submit to it, while purifying the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r2.anchor: الروح والنفس اللذين تولد بينهما القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r3.claim: Close kin signify people sharing one's original preparedness and spiritual affinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r3.anchor: وهم من يناسبكم بالاستعداد الأصلي والمشاكلة الروحانية

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r4.claim: Orphans are prepared souls cut off from the spirit's light by veiling; the needy are worshippers without a share in gnosis, stilled from spiritual travel.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r4.anchor: المستعدين المنقطعين عن نور الأب وهو الروح بالاحتجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r5.claim: The near neighbor is close in spiritual station, the distant neighbor far from it, and the companion beside one at the same station.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r5.anchor: ( والجار ذي القربى ) القريب من مقامك بالسلوك ( والجار الجنب ) البعيد عن مقامك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r6.claim: The wayfarer is a traveler estranged from the self's abode who has not yet attained a station; those possessed are affiliated through love and will.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r6.anchor: أي السالك المتغرب عن مأوى النفس الذي لم يصل إلى مقام بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p36/r7.claim: Alternatively, the parents are shaykhs; a disciple honors them through obedience and following their commands because they know how to treat hearts and prescribe only what pleases God.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r1.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r1.claim: Junayd said his Lord commanded him one thing and al-Sari another, so he put al-Sari's command first; he attributed what he found to al-Sari's blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره : أمرني ربي أمرا وأمرني السري أمرا فقدمت أمر السري

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r2.claim: The near neighbor can be the speaking, knowing, passionate celestial spirit, nearest to all things and colored by God's light; kindness frees it from nature and human appetites for its flight toward witnessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r2.anchor: بالروح الناطقة العارفة العاشقة الملكوتية التي خرجت من العدم بتجلي القدم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r3.claim: The distant neighbor can be the bodily form that bears the spirit; kindness to it means weaning its limbs from the breast of desires.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r3.anchor: بالصورة الحاملة للروح والإحسان إليها أن تفطم جوارحها من رضع ضرع الشهوات

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r4.claim: The companion beside one can be the heart on the unseen journey; kindness means freeing it from temporal things and directing its longing toward the Merciful's beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r4.anchor: وهو القلب الذي يصحبك في سفر الغيب والإحسان إليه أن تفرده من الحدثان

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r5.claim: Alternatively, the companion is the commanding self, which should be restrained by servitude and burned by love.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو النفس الأمارة وفي الخبر أعدى عدوك نفسك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r6.claim: A report calls the self between one's sides one's most hostile enemy; the passage uses it to support the allegorical reading of the companion as the commanding self.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r6.anchor: وفي الخبر أعدى عدوك نفسك التي بين جنبيك والإحسان إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r7.claim: The wayfarer can signify the complete saint, continually moving from the light of acts to attributes and then to essence; kindness means concealing his secret and obeying him.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r7.anchor: بالولي الكامل فإنه لم يزل يتنقل من نور الأفعال إلى نور الصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r8.speaker: بعض العارفين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r8.claim: Some knowers interpret close kin as related immaterial beings, orphans as spiritual faculties, and the needy as psychical faculties including the outer senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r8.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : وإن شئت أولت ( ذا القربى ) بما يتصل بالشخص من المجردات

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r9.speaker: بعض العارفين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r9.claim: In an alternative mapping by some knowers, the near neighbor is intellect, the distant neighbor imagination, and the companion is desire and will.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r9.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : وإن شئت أولت ( ذا القربى ) بما يتصل بالشخص من المجردات

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r10.speaker: بعض العارفين
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r10.claim: Some knowers map the wayfarer to thought and owned persons to acquired dispositions that generate virtuous actions; the author says the field of allegory is wide.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r10.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : وإن شئت أولت ( ذا القربى ) بما يتصل بالشخص من المجردات

ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r11.claim: The conceited wayfarer is one who boasts of spiritual states and stations, remaining veiled by his own perception of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p37/r11.anchor: ( إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا ) يسعى بالسلوك في نفسه ( فخورا ) بأحواله ومقاماته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r1.claim: Worship God means affirm His oneness and obey Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {واعبدوا الله} أي: وحدوه وأطيعوه، {ولا تشركوا به شيئا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r2.claim: In the report from Muʿādh, the Prophet says God's right is that people worship Him without associating anything; their right, if they do so, is that He not punish them, but he tells Muʿādh not to publicize this lest they rely on it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210/r2.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه قال: كنت رديف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r1.claim: The command means treating parents with goodness, kindness, and affection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r2.claim: It means doing good to one's relatives.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says he and the sponsor of an orphan will be together in Paradise like the index and middle fingers, held slightly apart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r3.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم] (4) "أنا وكافل اليتيم في الجنة هكذا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says one who strokes an orphan's head for God's sake earns a good deed for every hair touched, and one who cares for an orphan joins him in Paradise like two fingers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p210#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من مسح رأس يتيم لم يمسحه إلا لله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r1.claim: The near neighbor is one related by kinship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {والجار ذي القربى} أي: ذي القرابة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r2.claim: The distant neighbor is someone without kinship ties to you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r2.anchor: {والجار الجنب} أي: البعيد الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r3.claim: Asked which of two neighbors should receive a gift, ʿĀʾisha is told to give the one whose door is closer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r3.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: يا رسول الله إن لي جارين فإلى أيهما أهدي؟ قال: "إلى أقربهما منك بابا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r4.claim: The Prophet urges believers not to dismiss any kindness, including a cheerful greeting or adding water to stew and sharing it with neighbors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تحقرن من المعروف شيئا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r5.claim: The Prophet says Gabriel continued urging him to care for the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would inherit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Qatāda, and others identify the companion at one's side as a travel companion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.anchor: يعني: الرفيق في السفر، قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وجماعة وعكرمة وقتادة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.speaker: علي وعبد الله والنخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.claim: ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, and al-Nakhaʿī identify the companion at one's side as one's wife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.anchor: وقال علي وعبد الله والنخعي: هو المرأة تكون معه إلى جنبه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج وابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd say this is someone who accompanies you hoping to benefit from you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وابن زيد: هو الذي يصحبك رجاء نفعك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.claim: One view identifies the son of the road as a traveler because he stays on the road.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.anchor: قيل: هو المسافر لأنه ملازم للسبيل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.claim: Most commentators identify the son of the road as a guest.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.anchor: والأكثرون: على أنه الضيف، أخبرنا الأستاذ الإمام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.claim: The Prophet links faith in God and the Last Day with honoring one's neighbor and guest, and with speaking good or remaining silent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي شريح الخزاعي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليحسن إلى جاره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.claim: The Prophet sets a guest's entitlement at a day and night, hospitality at three days, and anything beyond that as charity; a guest must not overstay and distress the host.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي شريح الكعبي، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليكرم جاره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r1.claim: The phrase means enslaved people, whom one should treat well.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وما ملكت أيمانكم} أي: المماليك أحسنوا إليهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that during his illness the Prophet kept urging prayer and care for those under one's authority, repeating it as his tongue could barely speak.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r2.anchor: عن سفينة، عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول في مرضه: "الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r3.claim: Abū Dharr recounts the Prophet correcting his insult of a man's non-Arab mother: enslaved people are brethren, must be fed and clothed like their owners, not overworked, and helped if burdened.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r3.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: رأيت عليه بردا وعلى غلامه برد، فقلت:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r4.claim: The Prophet says a person guilty of bad treatment of those under his authority will not enter Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p212/r4.anchor: عن أبي بكر رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يدخل الجنة سيئ الملكة"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r1.claim: مختال is arrogant; فخور is someone who boasts falsely over others out of pride.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r1.anchor: المختال: المتكبر، والفخور: الذي يفتخر على الناس بغير الحق تكبرا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r2.claim: This warning follows the listed rights because pride makes an arrogant person withhold others' rights.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r2.anchor: ذكر هذا بعدما ذكر من الحقوق، لأن المتكبر يمنع الحق تكبرا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r3.claim: The Prophet recounts a man who strutted in two cloaks, admired himself, and was swallowed by the earth, where he remains convulsing until the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r3.anchor: عن همام بن منبه، قال: أنا أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "بينما رجل يتبختر في بردين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r4.claim: The Prophet says God will not look on the Day of Resurrection at a person who drags his garment out of arrogance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p213/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا ينظر الله يوم القيامة

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r1.claim: Worship God without associating an idol or anything else with Him, whether association is overt or subtle.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r1.anchor: صنما أو غيره، أو شيئا من الإشراك جليا أو خفيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r2.claim: The command means to treat both parents well.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r3.claim: The phrase means people connected by kinship.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r4.claim: The near neighbor may be one whose dwelling is near, or one connected by kinship or religion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r4.anchor: أي الذي قرب جواره. وقيل الذي له الجوار قرب واتصال بنسب أو دين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r5.claim: The phrase is also read in the accusative as a special construction to exalt the neighbor’s right.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r6.claim: The distant neighbor is one who lives far away, or one with no kinship to the listener.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r6.anchor: البعيد، أو الذي لا قرابة له.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r7.claim: The Prophet describes three neighbors: one with rights of neighborhood, kinship, and Islam; one with neighborhood and Islam; and a non-Muslim from the People of the Book with neighborhood alone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r7.anchor: فجار له ثلاثة حقوق: حق الجوار، وحق القرابة،

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r8.claim: The companion at one’s side may be a partner in learning, work, craft, or travel, or a wife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r8.anchor: الرفيق في أمر حسن كتعلم وتصرف وصناعة وسفر، فإنه صحبك

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r9.claim: The wayfarer may be a traveler or a weak person.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r10.claim: Those whom the right hands own are enslaved men and women.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r11.claim: God dislikes the arrogant person who turns away from relatives, neighbors, and companions, and boasts over them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:36/r11.anchor: متكبرا يأنف عن أقاربه وجيرانه وأصحابه ولا يلتفت إليهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r1.claim: After repeated counsel toward piety, justice, and beneficence, including marital kindness, this verse renews the sura's opening call to piety; its syntax can also connect to the command to seek God's bounty in 4:32.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r1.anchor: الوصايا من أولها إلى هنا بنتيجة التقوى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r2.claim: Worship means obeying the wholly perfect God, unlike anything else, with unalloyed obedience, humility, and submission through keeping commands and avoiding prohibitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r2.anchor: الذي له الكمال كله فلا يشبهه شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r3.claim: Because God is self-sufficient, He accepts only sincere worship; the prohibition reinforces the exclusive devotion implied by worshipping Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r3.anchor: ولما كان سبحانه غنيا لم يقبل إلا الخالص

BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r4.claim: After faith and the higher rank of ihsan in worship, the command turns to ihsan in human stewardship, beginning with parents who were the means of one's existence; their kindness is paired with God's oneness.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p254/r4.anchor: فصار المأمور بذلك مخلصا في عبادته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r1.claim: Kinship ties are a central concern of the sura, so this command details and reinforces its opening counsel; the repeated preposition underscores relatives' added right through closeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r1.anchor: قال مفصلا لما ذكر أول السورة تأكيدا له

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r2.claim: Orphans and the poor merit care even without known kinship; both are weak, and the orphan comes first because youth leaves the child unable to meet needs or seek help.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r2.anchor: أي وإن لم تكن رحمهم معروفة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r3.claim: A related neighbor has two rights; an unrelated neighbor still deserves care because of daily proximity and the harm a bad neighbor can cause. He quotes a supplication seeking refuge from a bad resident neighbor, unlike a nomadic one who moves.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r4.claim: The companion at one's side is someone close and associated through a matter that prolongs companionship.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r4.anchor: الملاصق المخالط في أمر من الأمور الموجبة لامتداد العشرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r5.claim: The wayfarer is a traveler made vulnerable by distance from home, few helpers, and loneliness.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r6.claim: Those under one's ownership means male and female slaves, and treating them well is a great act of obedience.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r7.claim: He quotes a report that the Prophet's final words concerned prayer and those owned by one's right hand; no grading or source is supplied here.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r7.anchor: آخر ما تكلم به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة وماملكت أيمانكم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r8.claim: Mukhtal is conceited, proud of appearance and gifts, contemptuous of others, ashamed of poor relatives, and unwilling to help weak neighbors; fakhuur excessively boasts and shuns the poor.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p255/r8.anchor: متكبرا معجبا بنفسه متزينا بحليته مرائيا بام آتاه الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r1.claim: The people of truth are one soul: their bodies and numbers differ, but the unity of their faith is undiminished.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r1.anchor: مؤمنان معدود ليك إيمان يكى جسم شان معدود ليكن جان يكى والحاصل أن أهل الحق كلهم نفس واحدة

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r2.claim: Worship includes every action and omission performed solely because God commands it, encompassing both heart and bodily acts.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r2.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن كل فعل وترك يؤتى به بمجرد أمر الله تعالى بذلك وهذا يدخل فيه جميع أعمال القلوب وجميع أعمال الجوارح

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r3.claim: Shirk means associating anything with God, including idols, manifest shirk such as unbelief, and hidden shirk such as showing off.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r3.anchor: من الأشياء صنما أو غيره أو شيئا من الإشراك جليا وهو الكفر أو خفيا وهم الرياء

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r4.claim: The preposition bi means toward, as in 12:100; parents come first because they have the greatest human claim, requiring service, gentle speech, attention to needs, and support within one’s means.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r4.anchor: فالباء بمعنى إلى كما في قوله : {وقد أحسن بى} (يوسف : 100)

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r5.claim: Treat relatives such as siblings, uncles, and maternal uncles with kinship and compassion when prosperous, and care and spend well on them when poor.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r5.anchor: وبصاحب القرابة من أخ أو عم أو خال أو نحو ذلك بصلة الرحم والمرحمة إن استغنوا والوصية وحسن الإنفاق إن افتقروا

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r6.claim: Care for orphans by spending in their best interests or, as their guardian, managing their property.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r6.anchor: بإنفاق ما هو أصلح لهم أو بالقيام على أموالهم إن كان وصيا

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r7.claim: Help the poor with charity, alms, food, or a kind response.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r7.anchor: بالمبار والصدقات وإطعام الطعام أو بالرد الجميل

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r8.claim: The near neighbor is either someone close in residence or a neighbor connected by kinship or religion.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r8.anchor: أي الذي قرب جواره أو الذي له مع الجوار اتصال بنسب أو دين

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r9.claim: The Prophet says few fulfill a neighbor’s rights: enrich a poor neighbor, lend when asked, congratulate good fortune, console misfortune, visit illness, and attend the funeral.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r9.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "والذي نفسي بيده لا يؤدي حق الجار إلا من رحم الله

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r10.claim: The distant neighbor is either far away or unrelated by kinship.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r10.anchor: أي : البعيد أو الذي لا قرابة له

BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r11.claim: The Prophet divides neighbors into one with three rights of proximity, kinship, and Islam; one with proximity and Islam; and a non-Muslim neighbor with the right of proximity alone.
BURSEVI:v2p162#2/r11.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : "الجيران ثلاثة فجار له ثلاثة حقوق حق الجوار وحق القرابة وحق الإسلام

BURSEVI:v2p163/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r1.claim: The companion at one’s side includes a partner in study, work, craft, or travel, and even someone who briefly sits beside one in a mosque or gathering.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r1.anchor: أي : الرفيق في أمر حسن كتعلم وتصرف وصناعة وسفر فإنه صحبك وحصل بجانبك

BURSEVI:v2p163/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r2.claim: Even a slight companionship creates a right to be cared for and remembered, and should become a reason to do good.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r2.anchor: من أدنى صحبة التأمت بينك وبينه فعليك أن ترعى ذلك الحق ولا تنساه وتجعله ذريعة إلى الإحسان

BURSEVI:v2p163/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r3.claim: The son of the road is a traveler away from home and property, or a guest who has come to stay.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r3.anchor: هو المسافر الذي سافر عن بلده وماله والإحسان بأن تؤويه وتزوده أو هو الضيف الذي ينزل عليك

BURSEVI:v2p163/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r4.claim: A guest has a right to hospitality for three days; more is charity, and the guest may not remain until the host makes him leave.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r4.anchor: وحقه ثلاثة أيام وما زاد على ذلك فهو صدقة ولا يحل له أن يقيم عنده حتى يخرجه

BURSEVI:v2p163/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r5.claim: Treat enslaved men and women well: train them, do not overburden them or make them work all day, speak gently, and provide needed food and clothing.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r5.anchor: من العبيد والإماء والإحسان إليهم بأن يؤدبهم ولا يكلفهم ما لا طاقة لهم ولا يكثر العمل لهم طول النهار

BURSEVI:v2p163/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v2p163/r6.claim: Some say every animal is in one’s care, and kindness appropriate to it is a great act of obedience.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم كل حيوان فهو مملوك والإحسان إليه بما يليق به طاعة عظيمة

BURSEVI:v2p163/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r7.claim: The arrogant look down on relatives, neighbors, and companions and ignore them; the boastful brag inappropriately and fail to fulfill others’ rights.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r7.anchor: أي متكبرا يأنف من أقاربه وجيرانه وأصحابه ولا يلتفت إليهم {فخورا} بما لا يليق

BURSEVI:v2p163/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes boastfulness here as failing to thank God for His blessings.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r8.anchor: ويقال فخورا في نعم الله لا يشكر

BURSEVI:v2p163/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r9.speaker: الله
BURSEVI:v2p163/r9.claim: In a divine address to Moses, God says that those who reject contentment with His decree, gratitude for blessings, patience in trials, and acceptance of provision should worship another lord; worship and gratitude sustain mercy, rainfall, and forbearance toward deniers.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r9.anchor: قال الله تعالى لموسى عليه السلام : (يا موسى إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني وحدي

BURSEVI:v2p163/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163/r10.claim: True worship is serving God alone through His commands and prohibitions, without worshipping worldly or afterlife rewards; seek the Master for His own sake, renounce both realms, and submit to destiny with gratitude and patience.
BURSEVI:v2p163/r10.anchor: واعلم أن العبادة أن تعبد الله وحده بطريق أوامره ونواهيه ولا تعبد معه شيئا من الدنيا والعقبى فإنك لو عبدت الله خوفا من شيء أو طمعا في شيء

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r1.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r1.claim: A gnostic poem says to erase the self through la ilaha: its negation severs attachment to all else, carries the seeker from annihilation to subsistence, and frees the self for intimacy with God.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r1.anchor: نقد هستي محو كن در "لا اله"

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r2.claim: Kindness is a divine quality, while wrongdoing belongs to the human self; the servant’s good deeds come from God, as 32:7, 12:53, and 4:79 indicate.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r2.anchor: لأن الإحسان صفات الله تعالى لقوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r3.claim: Servitude requires turning wholly toward God and away from all else; by taking on divine qualities, one is annihilated through Him and remains through Him, beneficent toward parents and others without shirk or showing off.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r3.anchor: فإذا حصل المقصود ووصل العابد إلى المعبود فحينئذ يصح منه بالوالدين إحسانا

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r4.claim: The warning follows because arrogance and pride are qualities of the self, which does not love God but desires worldly ornaments and what satisfies its own appetite.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r4.anchor: لأن الاختيال والفخر من أوصاف النفس والله تعالى لا يحب النفس ولا أوصافها لأن النفس لا تحب الله ولا المحبة من أوصافها

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says shirk is more hidden in a human being than an ant crawling on a smooth rock on a dark night.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r5.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "الشرك أخفى في ابن آدم من دبيب النملة على الصخرة الصماء

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r6.claim: Serving a created being out of fear of harm or hope for benefit is practical shirk; the poem warns that a path away from God makes even one’s prayer rug liable to the fire.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r6.anchor: ومن خدم مخلوقا خوفا من مضرته أو طمعا في منفعته فقد أشرك عملا :

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r7.claim: Deeds done without seeking God’s face are nullified and become scattered dust, as stated in 25:23.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r7.anchor: يعني الأعمال التي عملوها لغير وجه الله أبطلنا ثوابها وجعلناها كالهباء المنثور

BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r8.claim: A man told the Prophet he gave charity seeking God’s face but also liked being praised; the cited answer is 18:110, which commands righteous work without associating anyone in worship.
BURSEVI:v2p163#2/r8.anchor: وجاء رجل إلى النبي عليه السلام فقال : يا رسول الله إني أتصدق بالصدقة فالتمس بها وجه الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r1.claim: The Prophet says a God-fearing caretaker of an orphan, whether related to him or not, will be in Paradise alongside him, gesturing with two fingers.
