DURR-FULL:v2p528/r1.anchor: عن أم سعد بنت مرة الفهرية عن أبيها قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: أنا وكافل اليتيم له أو لغيره

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the near neighbor as one related to you and the remote neighbor as one with no kinship to you.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {والجار ذي القربى} يعني الذي بينك وبينه قرابة {والجار الجنب} يعني الذي ليس بينك

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r3.speaker: نوف الشامي
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r3.claim: Nawf al-Shami interprets the near neighbor as a Muslim and the remote neighbor as a Jew or Christian.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r3.anchor: عن نوف الشامي في قوله {والجار ذي القربى} قال: المسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r4.claim: The Prophet says whoever believes in God and the Last Day should treat the neighbor well.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r4.anchor: عن أبي شريح الخزاعي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليحسن إلى جاره

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r5.claim: Aisha says Gabriel continued advising the Prophet about neighbors until she thought they would be given inheritance rights.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r5.anchor: عن عائشة: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: ما زال جبريل يوصيني بالجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that a neglected neighbor will complain on Judgment Day that the person shut his door and withheld kindness.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: كم من جار متعلق بجاره يوم القيامة يقول: يا رب هذا أغلق بابه دوني

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r7.claim: A hadith warns that a person whose neighbor is not safe from his harm will not enter Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا يدخل الجنة من لا يأمن جاره بوائقه

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet condemned a woman for worship and charity coupled with verbal harm to neighbors, but praised a woman who performed obligations, gave modestly, and harmed no one; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قيل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن فلانة تقوم الليل وتصوم النهار وتفعل وتصدق وتؤذي جيرانها بلسانها

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r9.claim: When Aisha asked which of two neighbors should receive her gift, the Prophet directed her to the one whose door was nearer.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r9.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قلت: يا رسول الله إن لي جارين فإلى أيهما أهدي قال: إلى أقربهما منك بابا

DURR-FULL:v2p528/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra says one should give first to the nearer neighbor, not the more distant one.
DURR-FULL:v2p528/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: لا يبدأ بجاره الأقصى قبل الأدنى ولكن يبدأ بالأدنى قبل الأقصى

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r1.claim: Abu Umama says the Prophet kept advising about neighbors until he thought the neighbor would inherit.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوصي بالجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r2.claim: An unnamed Ansari saw Gabriel standing with the Prophet; the Prophet repeated Gabriel's advice about neighbors and said a greeting would have been returned.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r2.anchor: من طريق أبي العالية عن رجل من الأنصار قال: خرجت من أهلي أريد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فإذا به قائم ورجل معه

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r3.claim: The Prophet says whoever believes in God and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فلا يؤذ جاره

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra also reports Gabriel's repeated advice about the neighbor, which the Prophet thought might make neighbors heirs.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أوصاني جبريل بالجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r5.speaker: أبو لبابة
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r5.claim: Abu Lubaba transmits the Prophet's warning that no harm to a neighbor should be treated as insignificant.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r5.anchor: عن أبي لبابة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا قليل من أذى جاره

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r6.claim: The Prophet says adultery with a neighbor's wife is worse than with ten other women, and stealing from a neighbor is worse than stealing from ten other homes.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r6.anchor: عن المقداد بن الأسود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه: ما تقولون في الزنا

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the companion at one's side as a travel companion.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {والصاحب بالجنب} قال: الرفيق في السفر

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid likewise take the companion at one's side to mean a travel companion.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد مثله

DURR-FULL:v2p530/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the phrase can mean a companion at home, a travel companion, or one's wife who shares a bed.
DURR-FULL:v2p530/r9.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم {والصاحب بالجنب} قال: هو جليسك في الحضر ورفيقك في السفر

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r1.claim: In an unattributed report, the Prophet gives his companion the straight spearhead and keeps the crooked one, saying every companion is accountable for his companionship, even for an hour.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r1.anchor: فقال: كلا يا فلان إن كل صاحب يصحب صاحبا مسؤول عن صحابته ولو ساعة من نهار

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r2.claim: The Prophet says the best companions before God are those best to their companions, and the best neighbors are those best to their neighbors.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: خير الأصحاب عند الله خير هم لصاحبه وخير الجيران

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r3.claim: Ali interprets the companion at one's side as one's wife.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r3.anchor: عن علي في قوله {والصاحب بالجنب} قال: المرأة

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r4.claim: Ibn Masud likewise interprets the companion at one's side as one's wife.

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise interprets the companion at one's side as one's wife.

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r6.claim: Mujahid says those whom God placed in your care should receive good companionship; God enjoined all the groups named in the verse.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وما ملكت أيمانكم} قال: مما خولك الله فأحسن صحبته كل هذا أوصى الله به

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r7.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r7.claim: Muqatil identifies the phrase as male and female slaves and says God commands good treatment and fulfillment of their rights.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل {وما ملكت أيمانكم} يعني من عبيدكم وإمائكم يوصي الله بهم خيرا

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r8.claim: The Prophet calls enslaved people one's brothers: feed and clothe them as oneself, do not burden them beyond capacity, and help if overburdened.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r8.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن إخوانكم خولكم جعلهم الله تحت أيديكم فمن كان أخوه تحت يديه

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r9.claim: The Prophet advised kindness to enslaved people: feed and clothe them from what one uses and do not torture God's creatures.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوصي بالمملوكين خيرا ويقول: أطعموهم مما تأكلون

DURR-FULL:v2p531/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r10.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r10.claim: Abu al-Darda was seen wearing a cloak and white garment like those worn by his enslaved attendant.
DURR-FULL:v2p531/r10.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء أنه رؤى عليه برد وثوب أبيض وعلى غلامه برد وثوب أبيض

DURR-FULL:v2p535/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r1.speaker: أبو المتوكل الناجي
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda made his son face the enslaved woman he had slapped; when she forgave him, he witnessed her pardon and freed her for God's sake.
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r1.anchor: عن أبي المتوكل الناجي أن أبا الدرداء كانت لهم وليدة فلطمها ابنه يوما لطمة فأقعده لها

DURR-FULL:v2p535/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r2.speaker: أبو قلابة
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r2.claim: Abu Qilaba says Salman kneaded dough himself because he had sent the servant on an errand and did not want to burden her with two tasks.
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r2.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال: دخلنا على سلمان وهو يعجن

DURR-FULL:v2p535/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses mukhtal as arrogant and fakhur as boasting about what one received without thanking God.
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا} قال: متكبرا {فخورا} قال: بعدما أعطي

DURR-FULL:v2p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r4.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that on Judgment Day Hell will seize arrogant tyrants and vainglorious boasters from the gathered people with its tongue.
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إذا جمع الله الناس في صعيد واحد يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v2p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r5.claim: The Prophet distinguishes jealousy in a genuinely suspicious case from groundless jealousy, and permits swagger in battle or charity while condemning prideful or oppressive swagger.
DURR-FULL:v2p535/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن عتيك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن من الغيرة ما يحب الله ومنها ما يبغض الله

DURR-FULL:v2p536/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p536/r1.speaker: جابر بن سليم الهجيمي
DURR-FULL:v2p536/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet taught the greeting “السلام عليكم,” instructed that the izar end above the ankles, urged small acts of kindness and cheerful greetings, and counseled against returning insults; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v2p536/r1.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والحاكم وصححه عن جابر بن سليم الهجيمي قال: أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p536/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p536/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v2p536/r2.claim: Abu Dharr names three beloved people: the slain, patient fighter, one enduring a harmful neighbor, and a late-night traveler who rises to purify himself; God dislikes the arrogant, the boastful miser, and the boastful, oath-selling merchant. Al-Hakim authenticated it.
DURR-FULL:v2p536/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في الشعب عن مطرف بن عبد الله قال: قلت لأبي ذر

DURR-FULL:v2p537/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r1.claim: Abu Dharr completes the list of those God dislikes with the merchant who sells while swearing oaths repeatedly.

DURR-FULL:v2p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء الهروي
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r2.claim: Abu Raja says people who mistreat slaves are arrogant boasters, while those disobedient to parents are domineering and wretched; al-Awwam ibn Hawshab transmits the same report.
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي رجاء الهروي قال: لا تجد سيء الملكة إلا وجدته مختالا فخورا

DURR-FULL:v2p537/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r3.speaker: رجل من بلجيم
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r3.claim: An unnamed man of Baljim reports the Prophet's advice: do not let the izar trail, since trailing it expresses arrogance and God does not love arrogance.
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r3.anchor: عن رجل من بلجيم قال: قلت: يا رسول الله أوصني قال: إياك وإسبال الإزار

DURR-FULL:v2p537/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r4.speaker: ثابت بن قيس بن شماس
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r4.claim: Thabit feared that his love of beautiful clothes and sandal straps meant pride. The Prophet reassured him that grooming one's mount and gear is not pride; pride is spurning truth and belittling people, and said Thabit was among Paradise's people.
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r4.anchor: عن ثابت بن قيس بن شماس قال: كنت عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v2p537/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r5.speaker: سمرة بن فاتك
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r5.claim: Samura reports the Prophet praised him as an excellent young man if only he trimmed his forelock and hitched up his waist garment.
DURR-FULL:v2p537/r5.anchor: عن سمرة بن فاتك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: نعم الفتى سمرة لو أخذ من لمنة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains worshipping God as affirming His oneness.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : اعبدوا الله اي : وحدوا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r2.claim: The Prophet instructed his followers not to associate anything with God, even if they were burned, cut apart, or crucified.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r2.anchor: عن سلمة بن شريح ، عن عبادة بن الصامت قال : اوصانا رسول الله ، بسبع خصال الا تشركوا بالله شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r3.claim: Maqatil ibn Hayyan says kindness to parents means fulfilling the rights God has commanded regarding them.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قول الله تعالى : وبالوالدين احسانا فيما امركم به من حق الوالدين

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r4.claim: Maqatil ibn Hayyan explains “those of kinship” as relatives.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r4.anchor: عن بكير بن معروف ، عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : وبذي القربى يعني : القرابة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet through Ali says there is no orphan status after puberty.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r5.anchor: عن النزال ، عن علي ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انه قال : لا يتم بعد الحلم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says an orphan’s status ends when sound judgment is discerned, quoting the criterion in 4:6.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r6.anchor: كتب نجدة إلى ابن عباس ، ساله عن اليتيم : متى ينقضي يتمه ؟ فقال : اكتب يا يزيد

IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r7.claim: The Prophet says the poor person is not one who goes around begging and receives a morsel or two; the truly poor person refrains from asking and is overlooked.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p947/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ليس المساكين بالطواف ، ولا بالذي

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the near neighbor as one related to you; Mujahid, Ikrima, Maimun ibn Mihran, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, Maqatil ibn Hayyan, and Qatada are also reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : والجار ي القربى يعني : الذي بينك وبينه قرابة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r2.claim: Ali and Ibn Masud identify the near neighbor as one’s wife; Hasan and Said ibn Jubayr are also reported to hold this view.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r2.anchor: عن جابر ، عن عامر قال : قال علي وابن مسعود : والجار ذي القربى : المراة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r3.speaker: نوف
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r3.claim: Nawf identifies the near neighbor as a Muslim.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r3.anchor: عن نوف والجار ذي القربى قال : المسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the distant neighbor as someone with no kinship to you; several other authorities are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : والجار الجنب : الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r5.claim: Mujahid gives another explanation of the distant neighbor: your travel companion, sharing your overnight lodging and close company.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r5.anchor: قال : قال ابن جريج ، عن سليم هو أبو عبيد الله انه سمع مجاهدا يقول في : الجار الجنب قال : هو رفيقك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r6.speaker: نوف
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r6.claim: Nawf identifies the distant neighbor as a Jew or Christian.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r6.anchor: عن أبي اسحاق ، عن نوف قال : الجار الجنب قال : اليهودي والنصراني

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r7.speaker: علي وعبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r7.claim: Ali and Abdullah identify the companion at one’s side as one’s wife; reports from Ibn Abi Layla, Ibrahim al-Nakhai, Hasan, and Said ibn Jubayr also agree in one narration.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r7.anchor: عن علي وعبد الله في قوله : والصاحب بالجنب قالا : هي المراة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas gives another explanation of the companion at one’s side: a companion or associate.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p948/r8.anchor: عن علي ، عن بن عباس قوله : والصاحب بالجنب قال : الرفيق

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r1.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r1.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima identify the companion at one’s side as a travel companion; Qatada is also reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة في قوله : والصاحب بالجنب قال : هو الرفيق في السفر

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r2.claim: Mujahid describes the travel companion as someone whose lodging, food, and journey are shared with yours.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد والصاحب بالجنب : الرفيق في السفر ، منزلة منزلك ، وطعامه طعامك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the companion as someone sitting with you at home or traveling alongside you.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r3.anchor: عن زيد ابن اسلم ، قوله : والصاحب بالجنب قال : هو جليسك في الحضر

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr identifies the companion at one’s side as a righteous companion.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : والصاحب بالجنب قال : الرفيق الصالح

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the wayfarer as a poor guest who lodges among Muslims; Said ibn Jubayr is reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وابن السبيل قال : هو الضيف الفقير الذي ينزل بالمسلمين

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r6.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r6.claim: Qatada and Mujahid identify the wayfarer as a traveler passing by; Hasan, Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, Maqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Dahhak are also reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، وعن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد : وابن السبيل قال : هو الذي يمر عليك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r7.claim: Mujahid says a stranded traveler has a right to zakat even if wealthy; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Zuhri, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabi ibn Anas are also reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : وابن السبيل قال : لابن السبيل حق في الزكاة ، وان كان غنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r8.claim: Mujahid says those under one’s care are a gift from God whose company should be treated well; God enjoined all the listed duties.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : وما ملكت ايمانكم قال : ما خولك الله فاحسن صحبته ، كل هذا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r9.claim: Maqatil ibn Hayyan says the phrase means male and female slaves, whose prescribed rights should be fulfilled and who should be treated well.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p949/r9.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قوله : وما ملكت ايمانكم يعني : من عبيدكم وامائكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r1.claim: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet counted the conceited boaster among those God dislikes, citing this verse; he also names the conceited person who reminds others of favors.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r1.anchor: قال : اجل فلا اخا لك ، اكذب على خليلي ثلاثا ؟ قلت من الثلاثة الذي يبغض ؟ قال : المختال الفخور

IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r2.claim: The Prophet warned a man from Balhajim against letting his garment trail, since doing so is vanity and God dislikes vanity.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r2.anchor: عن رجل من بلهجيم قال : قلت يا رسول الله اوصني ، قال : اياك واسبال الازار ؛ فان اسبال الازار من المخيلة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r3.speaker: العوام بن حوشب
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r3.claim: Al-Awwam ibn Hawshab observes that people who treat those under their authority badly are usually conceited and boastful, and cites this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p950/r3.anchor: عن العوام بن حوشب قال : انك لا تكاد تجد سيء الملكة الا وجدته مختالا فخورا ثم قرا : وما ملكت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r1.claim: In the cited poetic verse, the main purpose is boasting that the group die in battle by the sword; the poet then presents this as a habitual trait, not exaggeration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r1.anchor: فإن الغرض الأهم هو التمدح بأنهم يقتلون في الحرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r2.claim: “Shayʾan” can be the object of “tushrikū”: make nothing worshipped a partner, as in the cited verse from al-Jinn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r2.anchor: أي لا تجعلوا شريكا شيئا مما يعبد كقوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r3.claim: Alternatively, “shayʾan” is an emphatic cognate accusative: do not commit shirk at all, even a slight amount, as in the cited verse from al-Maʾida.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r4.claim: Placing the command to treat parents well immediately after worship emphasizes their status; the author links the order to the commands in Luqman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r4.anchor: اهتمام بشأن الوالدين إذ جعل الأمر بالإحسان إليهما عقب الأمر بالعبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r5.claim: The object governed by “iḥsānan” is brought forward for emphasis, not restriction, because benevolence is prescribed toward everything.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r5.anchor: ولذا قدم معمول ( إحسانا ) عليه تقديما للاهتمام إذ لا معنى للحصر هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r6.claim: The verbal noun “iḥsānan” stands in place of a verb.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r7.claim: Here “iḥsān” takes the preposition bāʾ because it includes the sense of birr: respectful treatment and honoring a person; financial benefit instead takes ilā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p49/r7.anchor: وعندي أن الإحسان إنما يعدى بالباء إذا أريد به الإحسان المتعلق بمعاملة الذات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r1.claim: Orphans and the poor are singled out for care because both groups are weak and lack anyone to support them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r2.claim: The near-related neighbor is a neighbor belonging to one’s tribe; the distant neighbor is a stranger who has settled among the tribe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r2.anchor: الجار النسيب من القبيلة ، وب { الجار الجنب } الجار الغريب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r3.claim: “Al-junub” means distant, from janib (“side”); Ibn ʿAshur analyzes it as an adjective on faʿl, while noting a competing verbal-noun analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r3.anchor: فهو جنب ، أي بعيد ، مشتق من الجانب ، وهو وصف على وزن فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r4.claim: Some take “junub” as a verbal noun, which explains why it does not agree in form with the word it describes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو مصدر ، ولذلك لم يطابق موصوفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r5.claim: A line by Balaʿa ibn Qays contrasts a relative neighbor with a strange, non-tribal neighbor, supporting Ibn ʿAshur’s interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r5.anchor: قال بلعاء بن قيس : لا يجتوينا مجاور أبدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r6.claim: ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada’s phrase “from estrangement” likewise uses janāba for being a stranger or outsider.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r6.anchor: ويشهد لهذا المعنى قول علقمة بن عبدة في شعره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r7.claim: Some interpret the near and distant neighbors as those close to or far from one’s home; Ibn ʿAshur rejects this because qurba is not used for spatial proximity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r7.anchor: وهذا بعيد ، لأن القربى لا تعرف في القرب المكاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r8.claim: Islam reinforces the Arabs’ established virtue of honoring neighbors and completes their noble character by commanding kindness to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r8.anchor: والعرب معروفون بحفظ الجوار والإحسان إلى الجار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r9.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet said Gabriel kept advising him about the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would be made an heir; al-Bukhari records it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r9.anchor: ففي ( البخاري ) عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r10.speaker: أبو شريح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r10.claim: Abu Shurayh reports the Prophet’s repeated oath that a person whose neighbor is not safe from his harms does not truly believe; al-Bukhari records it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r10.anchor: وفيه عن أبي شريح : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج وهو يقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r11.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r11.claim: Aisha asked which of her two neighbors should receive a gift, and the Prophet told her to choose the one whose door was nearer; al-Bukhari records it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r11.anchor: وفيه عن عائشة ، قلت : ( يا رسول الله إن لي جارين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r12.speaker: رسول الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r12.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr to add water to broth and share it considerately with his neighbors; Muslim records the report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r12.anchor: وفي ( صحيح مسلم ) : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي ذر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r13.speaker: ابن شهاب والأوزاعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r13.claim: Ibn Shihab and al-Awzaʿi define the neighbor’s range as forty houses in every direction; a hadith is also reported for this limit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r13.anchor: فقال ابن شهاب ، والأوزاعي : أربعون دارا من كل ناحية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r14.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r14.claim: No fixed boundary for neighborliness is transmitted from Malik.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r14.anchor: وليس عن مالك في ذلك حد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r15.claim: The scope of neighborliness is best left to what people customarily recognize.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p50/r15.anchor: والظاهر أنه موكول إلى ما تعارفه الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r1.claim: The companion at one’s side is someone who stays nearby: a guest, a travel companion, or anyone visiting in hope of receiving help.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r1.anchor: هو المصاحب الملازم للمكان ، فمنه الضيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies the companion at one’s side as one’s wife.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r3.claim: “Ibn al-sabīl” is a traveler passing through without intending to settle; “ibn” conveys association, and the road is imagined to have cast him toward the people as its child.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r3.anchor: فابن السبيل هو الذي لازم الطريق سائرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r4.claim: The traveler merits care because he is vulnerable, has few supporters, and cannot readily learn the circumstances of an unfamiliar people and place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r4.anchor: والوصاية به لأنه ضعيف الحيلة ، قليل النصير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r5.claim: Enslaved people merit special care because slavery leaves them needy and weak, with their masters blocking routes to freedom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r5.anchor: لأن العبيد في ضعف الرق والحاجة وانقطاع سبل الخلاص من سادتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r6.claim: The closing clause is a summative censure of traits that commonly obstruct kindness to the named groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r6.anchor: تذييل لجملة الأمر بالإحسان إلى من سماهم بذم موانع الإحسان إليهم الغالبة على البشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r7.claim: Ikhtiyāl is arrogance, derived from khuyalāʾ; fakhūr is someone intensely boastful about what he has done.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r7.anchor: والاختيال : التكبر ، افتعال مشتق من الخيلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r8.claim: Both traits produce harshness and rudeness, opposed to the commanded kindness and to humility toward people thought unable to retaliate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r8.anchor: وكلا الوصفين منشأ للغلظة والجفاء ، فهما ينافيان الإحسان المأمور به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r9.claim: God’s lack of love here means withholding approval and nearness from the person described.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r9.anchor: ومعنى نفي محبة الله تعالى نفي رضاه وتقريبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r10.claim: The censure alludes to the roughness and harshness associated with polytheists and warns believers against retaining those former traits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p51/r10.anchor: وهذا تعريض بأخلاق أهل الشرك ، لما عرفوا به من الغلطة والجفاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r1.claim: The waaw joins this sentence to another sentence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r1.anchor: «الواو» لعطف جملة الكلام على جملة غيرها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r2.claim: ʿIbāda means humble submission through obedience; related words describe a marked road or branded camel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r2.anchor: والعبادة: التذلل بالطاعة، ومنه طريق معبد، وبعير معبد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r3.claim: Iḥsānan is an accusative verbal noun governed by an implied command; al-Ṭabarī's exhortative-accusative analysis is mistaken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r3.anchor: وإحسانا نصب على المصدر، والعامل فعل مضمر تقديره: وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r4.claim: Required parental duties include honoring and protecting them and supporting them if needy; other kindness, gentle treatment, and gracious speech are recommended.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r4.anchor: والقيام بحقوق الوالدين اللازمة لهما من التوقير والصون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r5.claim: Asked who most deserved good companionship, the Prophet named the mother three times, then the father; another version says to begin with the nearest kin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r5.anchor: حسب قوله عليه السلام للذي قال له من أبر؟ قال أمك قال ثم من؟ قال أمك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads إحسان in the nominative.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r7.claim: ذو القربى means a relative on either the father's or mother's side, and the command requires preserving kinship ties.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r7.anchor: هو القريب النسب من قبل الأب والأم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r8.claim: An orphan is one whose father has died before puberty; Arabic usage for someone whose mother died is metaphorical.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r8.anchor: واليتامى: جمع يتيم، وهو فاقد الأب قبل البلوغ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r9.claim: The needy meant here are indigent Muslims eligible for zakat who openly ask for help.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r9.anchor: والمساكين: المقترون من المسلمين الذين تحل لهم الزكاة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r10.claim: They identify the near neighbor as a relative and the distant neighbor as one with no kinship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r10.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وغيرهم: الجار ذو القربى هو الجار القريب النسب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r11.speaker: نوف الشامي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r11.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī takes the near neighbor as Muslim and the distant neighbor as Jewish or Christian: Islam is a bond of kinship, unbelief a distance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r11.anchor: وقال نوف الشامي: الجار ذو القربى هو الجار المسلم، والجار الجنب هو الجار اليهودي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r12.claim: Another group understands the terms spatially: the near neighbor lives close to you and the distant neighbor farther away.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r12.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الجار ذو القربى هو الجار القريب المسكن منك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r13.speaker: عائشة والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r13.claim: ʿĀʾisha asks which of two neighbors should receive her gift; the Prophet says to give to the one whose door is nearer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r13.anchor: قالت عائشة، يا رسول الله إن لي جارين، فإلى أيهما أهدي؟ قال إلى أقربهما منك بابا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r14.speaker: الأوزاعي وفرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r14.claim: Neighbor boundaries differ: al-Awzāʿī counts forty houses in each direction; another group counts those who hear the mosque's call to prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r14.anchor: فقال الأوزاعي: أربعون دارا من كل ناحية جيرة، وقالت فرقة: من سمع إقامة الصلاة فهو جار ذلك المسجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r15.claim: Another group calls anyone living with someone in the same quarter or city a neighbor; degrees vary, with a spouse the closest neighbor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r15.anchor: وقالت فرقة: من ساكن رجلا في محلة أو مدينة فهو جاره، والمجاورة مراتب بعضها ألصق من بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r16.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r16.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse calls a spouse the closest neighbor and uses الجيرة الخلط for closely associated neighbors.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p49#3/r16.anchor: أدناها الزوج كما قال الأعشى: [الطويل] أيا جارتي بيني وبعد ذلك الجيرة الخلط،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r1.claim: An unnamed poet's line evokes harm that breaks up closely associated neighbors, continuing the cited evidence about الجيرة الخلط.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r1.anchor: سائل مجاور جرم هل جنيت لها ... حربا تفرق بين الجيرة الخلط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports Maymūn ibn Mihrān's view that the phrase means the neighbor of one's relative; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it as bad Arabic because it combines the definite article with annexation, and says جار ذي القربى would be proper.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r2.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن ميمون بن مهران: أن الجار ذا القربى أريد به جار القريب، وهذا خطأ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r3.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read والجار ذا القربى, with الجار in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة «والجار ذا القربى» بنصب الجار،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r4.speaker: بعض الصحابة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r4.claim: Makki transmits from Ibn Wahb an unnamed Companion's view that الجار الجنب means a man's wife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r4.anchor: وحكى مكي عن ابن وهب أنه قال عن بعض الصحابة في الجار الجنب: إنها زوجة الرجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r5.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r5.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal transmits from ʿĀṣim a reading with fatḥa on jīm and a vowelless nūn in الجنب.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r5.anchor: وروى المفضل عن عاصم أنه قرأ «والجار الجنب» بفتح الجيم وسكون النون،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r6.claim: Here الجنب means distant; جنابة denotes distance, as al-Aʿshā's verse about visiting Ḥurayth from afar attests.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r6.anchor: والجنب في هذه الآية معناه. البعيد، والجنابة البعد، ومنه قول الشاعر وهو الأعشى:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r7.speaker: علقة بن عبدة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r7.claim: ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada also uses جنابة for distance in a verse asking not to be denied a gift while a stranger among the tents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r7.anchor: ومنه قول الآخر، وهو علقمة بن عبدة: [الطويل] فلا تحرمني نائلا عن جنابة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r8.claim: The word also relates to الاجتناب, leaving something to one side; an Arab described the neighbor as someone who settles wherever one's eye falls.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r8.anchor: وهو من الاجتناب، وهو أن يترك الشيء جانبا، وسئل أعرابي عن الجار الجنب، فقال: هو الذي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r9.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī treats جنب as an adjective, like ناقة أجد and مشية سجح, and derives ritual junub from this sense of distance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: جنب صفة كناقة أجد، ومشية سجح، وجنب التطهر مأخوذ من الجنب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r10.claim: They identify the companion at one's side as a travel companion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك: الصاحب بالجنب هو الرفيق في السفر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى وإبراهيم النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r11.claim: They identify the companion at one's side as one's wife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r11.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه، وابن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى وإبراهيم النخعي: الصاحب بالجنب الزوجة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the phrase to mean someone who visits and calls on you so that you can help him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو الرجل يعتريك ويلم بك لتنفعه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r13.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits a report in which the Prophet gives his companion the straight stick and keeps the crooked one, explaining that every companion is accountable for his companionship, even for an hour.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r13.anchor: وأسند الطبري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان معه رجل من أصحابه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r14.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r14.claim: All commentators take ابن السبيل to be a traveler on the road; the expression parallels ابن ماء for a bird that stays by water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r14.anchor: وقال المفسرون طرا: ابن السبيل هو المسافر على ظهر طريقه، وسمي ابنه للزومه له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r15.claim: The Prophet's saying that ابن زنى does not enter Paradise is explained as referring to someone who persists in the conduct and thereby deserves that attribution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p50/r15.anchor: ومنه قول النبي عليه السلام: «لا يدخل الجنة ابن زنى» أي: ملازمه الذي يستحق بالمثابرة عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r1.claim: Mujāhid interprets ابن السبيل as a person passing you while traveling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r1.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن مجاهدا فسره بأنه المار عليك في سفره،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r2.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r2.claim: Qatāda and others interpret ابن السبيل as a guest; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this and Mujāhid's passerby are effectively one view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r2.anchor: وأن قتادة وغيره فسره بأنه الضيف. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا كله قول واحد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r3.claim: What one's right hand possesses means enslaved people; possession is attributed to the hand because it conventionally grasps, dominates, and acquires.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r3.anchor: وما ملكت أيمانكم يريد العبيد الأرقاء، ونسب الملك إلى اليمين إذ هي في المعتاد جارحة البطش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r4.claim: Many well-known Prophetic reports enjoin good treatment of enslaved people, though Ibn ʿAṭiyya does not enumerate them here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r4.anchor: والعبيد موصى بهم في غير ما حديث يطول ذكرها، ويغني عن ذلك اشتهارها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r5.claim: Here denying divine love means withholding the effects of God's favor in the afterlife and praise in this life; it is love as an attribute of action, removed from the arrogant boaster.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r5.anchor: ومعنى لا يحب في هذه الآية لا تظهر عليه آثار نعمه في الآخرة ولا آثار حمده في الدنيا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r6.claim: خال الرجل يخول خولا means that a man acts arrogantly and admires himself; al-Ṭabarī cites a poem to attest the usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r6.anchor: يقال خال الرجل يخول خولا إذا تكبر وأعجب بنفسه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r7.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī's cited poem uses الخال as an arrogant person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r7.anchor: وأنشد الطبري: [المتقارب] فإن كنت سيدنا سدتنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r8.claim: The denial of love is a threat; arrogance and boasting are singled out because pride leads people to neglect those whom God commanded them to treat kindly, while conceit or miserliness obstructs that care.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r8.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ونفي المحبة عمن هذه صفته ضرب من التوعد، وخص هاتين الصفتين هنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r9.speaker: أبو رجاء الهروي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r9.claim: Abū Rajāʾ al-Harawī observes that poor treatment of dependents accompanies arrogance and boastfulness, while disobedience to parents accompanies tyranny and wretchedness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r9.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء الهروي: لا تجده سيء الملكة إلا وجدته مختالا فخورا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p51/r10.claim: Fakhr is counting one's merits in order to vaunt them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses worshipping God as affirming His oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ واعبدوا الله ﴾ قال ابن عباس وحدوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the wording urges people to show kindness to their parents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وبالوالدين إحسانا ﴾ قال الفراء أغراهم بالإحسان إلى الوالدين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عكرمة، الضحاك، قتادة، ابن زيد، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r3.claim: One interpretation is a neighbor to whom one is related by kinship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه الجار الذي بينك وبينه قرابة قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة وابن زيد ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r4.speaker: نوف الشامي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r4.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī interprets this as a Muslim neighbor, near in faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه الجار المسلم قاله نوف الشامي فيكون المعنى ذي القربى منكم بالإسلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r5.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r5.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal reports from ʿĀṣim a pronunciation with fatḥa on jīm and sukūn on nūn in al-junub.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r5.anchor: روى المفضل عن عاصم والجار الجنب بفتح الجيم وإسكان النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r6.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī analyzes the phrase as “the neighbor of the side,” with the genitive noun omitted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي المعنى والجار ذي الجنب فحذف المضاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عطاء، عكرمة، الضحاك، ابن زيد، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r7.claim: One interpretation of the neighbor is a stranger with no kinship to the person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه الغريب الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء وعكرمة والضحاك وابن زيد ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r8.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r8.claim: Another interpretation includes the neighbors on every side: right, left, in front, and behind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r8.anchor: والثاني أنه جارك عن يمينك وعن شمالك وبين يديك وخلفك رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r9.speaker: نوف الشامي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r9.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī says the phrase refers to a Jewish or Christian neighbor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r9.anchor: والثالث أنه اليهودي والنصراني قاله نوف الشامي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r10.speaker: علي، ابن مسعود، الحسن، إبراهيم النخعي، ابن أبي ليلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r10.claim: One interpretation of the companion at one's side is one's wife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r10.anchor: أحدها أنه الزوجة قاله علي وابن مسعود والحسن وإبراهيم النخعي وابن أبي ليلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك، السدي، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r11.claim: Another interpretation is a travel companion; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is reported to have held either of the first two views.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r11.anchor: والثاني أنه الرفيق في السفر قاله ابن عباس في رواية مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن قتيبة وعن سعيد بن جبير كالقولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r12.speaker: ابن جريج عن ابن عباس، عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r12.claim: A third interpretation is a companion generally, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and held by ʿIkrima.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r12.anchor: والثالث أنه الرفيق رواه ابن جريج عن ابن عباس وبه قال عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the companion as someone who stays close to you hoping for your goodwill.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r13.anchor: قال ابن زيد هو الذي يلصق بك رجاء خيرك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r14.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r14.claim: Muqātil says the companion is with you both at home and on a journey.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r14.anchor: وقال مقاتل هو رفيقك حضرا وسفرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r15.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier discussion of “the wayfarer” in al-Baqara.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p78/r15.anchor: وفي ابن السبيل أقوال قد ذكرناها في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r1.claim: The phrase means enslaved people; some exegetes also include domesticated animals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وما ملكت أيمانكم ﴾ يعني المملوكين وقال بعضهم يدخل فيه الحيوان البهيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the arrogant person as one who struts in his walk, and the boastful as one who prides himself over others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمحتال البطر في مشيته والفخور المفتخر على الناس بكبره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the boastful person recounts what God has given him but does not thank God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد هو الذي يعد ما أعطى ولا يشكر الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains al-mukhtāl as one characterized by vanity and pride.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r4.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة المختال ذو الخيلاء والكبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls the mukhtāl conceited, swaggering, and foolish; such a person scorns poor relatives and neighbors.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p80/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج المختال الصلف التياه الجهول وإنما ذكر الاختيال هاهنا لأن المختال يأنف من ذوي قراباته ومن جيرانه إذا كانوا فقراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r1.claim: God alone deserves worship and exclusive devotion because He is the Creator, Provider, and benefactor who continually favors His creatures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r1.anchor: يأمر تبارك وتعالى بعبادته وحده لا شريك له؛ فإنه هو الخالق الرازق المنعم المتفضل على خلقه في جميع الآنات والحالات، فهو المستحق منهم أن يوحدوه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r2.claim: The Prophet tells Muadh that God's right over His servants is that they worship Him without associating anything with Him; if they do, their right is that He not punish them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r2.anchor: كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ: "أتدري ما حق الله على العباد (6) ؟ " قال: الله ورسوله أعلم. قال: "أن يعبدوه ولا يشركوا به شيئا"،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r3.claim: God commands kindness to parents, who were the means by which a person passed from nonexistence into life; the Qur'an often joins devotion to God with kindness to parents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r3.anchor: ثم أوصى بالإحسان إلى الوالدين، فإن الله، سبحانه، جعلهما سببا لخروجك من العدم إلى الوجود، وكثيرا ما يقرن الله، سبحانه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r4.claim: The command extends kindness to male and female relatives; charity to a poor person is charity, while charity to kin is both charity and maintaining family ties.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r4.anchor: ثم عطف على الإحسان إلى الوالدين الإحسان (3) إلى القرابات من الرجال والنساء، كما جاء في الحديث:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r5.claim: Orphans have lost those who would manage their affairs and provide for them, so God commands people to treat them kindly and compassionately.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r5.anchor: واليتامى} وذلك لأنهم قد فقدوا من يقوم بمصالحهم، ومن ينفق عليهم، فأمر الله بالإحسان إليهم والحنو عليهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r6.claim: The poor are needy people without enough to meet their needs; they should be helped until their needs are met and hardship removed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p297#2/r6.anchor: وهم المحاويج من ذوي الحاجات الذين لا يجدون ما يقوم بكفايتهم، فأمر الله بمساعدتهم بما تتم به كفايتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، مجاهد، ميمون بن مهران، الضحاك، زيد بن أسلم، مقاتل بن حيان، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the listed early authorities identify the near neighbor as a relative and the distant neighbor as someone with no kinship to you.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {والجار ذي القربى} يعني الذي بينك وبينه قرابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r2.speaker: نوف البكالي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r2.claim: Nauf al-Bikali interprets the near neighbor as a Muslim and the distant neighbor as a Jew or Christian.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق عن نوف البكالي في قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} يعني المسلم {والجار الجنب} يعني اليهودي والنصراني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r3.speaker: علي وابن مسعود عن الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi reports from Ali and Ibn Masud that the near neighbor means a woman.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r3.anchor: وقال جابر الجعفي، عن الشعبي، عن علي وابن مسعود: {والجار ذي القربى} يعني المرأة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r4.claim: Mujahid also interprets the distant neighbor as a traveling companion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا في قوله: {والجار الجنب} يعني الرفيق في السفر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r5.claim: The Prophet says Gabriel repeatedly advised him about the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would be granted inheritance; Bukhari and Muslim include this report in their Sahih collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما زال جبريل يوصيني بالجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه". أخرجاه في الصحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r6.claim: A report from Abdullah ibn Amr repeats the saying about Gabriel's repeated counsel to the Prophet concerning neighbors; Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi transmit similar routes, and al-Tirmidhi grades one hasan gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما زال جبريل يوصيني بالجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r7.claim: The Prophet says the best companions to God are those best to their companion, and the best neighbors are those best to their neighbor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p298/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "خير الأصحاب عند الله خيرهم لصاحبه، وخير الجيران

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits the report that the best companions and neighbors are those who treat their companion and neighbor best, and grades it hasan gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r1.anchor: ورواه الترمذي عن أحمد بن محمد، عن عبد الله بن المبارك، عن حيوة بن شريح -به، وقال: [حديث] حسن غريب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r2.speaker: عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r2.claim: The Prophet says a person should not eat his fill while his neighbor remains hungry; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r2.anchor: قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي، حدثنا سفيان، عن أبيه، عن عباية بن رفاعة عن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يشبع الرجل دون جاره". تفرد به أحمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r3.speaker: المقداد بن الأسود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r3.claim: The Prophet says adultery with a neighbor's wife is worse than adultery with ten women, and theft from a neighbor worse than theft from ten homes; Ahmad alone reports it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r3.anchor: سمعت المقداد بن الأسود يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه: ["ما تقولون في الزنا؟ " قالوا: حرام حرمه الله ورسوله، فهو حرام إلى يوم القيامة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r4.claim: As corroboration, the Prophet names associating a partner with God, killing one's child for fear of sharing food, and adultery with a neighbor's wife among the gravest sins; this report is in both Sahih collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r4.anchor: وله شاهد في الصحيحين من حديث ابن مسعود: قلت: يا رسول الله، أي الذنب أعظم؟ قال: "أن تجعل لله ندا وهو خلقك".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r5.speaker: رجل من الأنصار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r5.claim: An Ansari says he saw the Prophet standing for a long time with a man, later identified as Gabriel; the Prophet says Gabriel kept advising him about neighbors until he thought they would inherit, and says Gabriel would have returned the greeting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p299/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية، عن رجل من الأنصار قال: خرجت من أهلي أريد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فإذا به قائم ورجل معه مقبل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r1.claim: A man from al-Awali sees Gabriel with the Prophet near the place where funeral prayers are held; Gabriel had so often advised kindness to neighbors that the man thought they would inherit. This route is unique and supports the earlier report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: جاء رجل من العوالي ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وجبريل عليه السلام يصليان حيث يصلى على الجنائز،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r2.claim: A report from Jabir divides neighbors into three: a non-Muslim without kinship has the neighbor's right; a Muslim has neighbor and Islam rights; a Muslim relative has those plus kinship, making the greatest claim. Al-Bazzar notes only Ibn Abi Fudayk is known to report from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Fudayl.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الجيران ثلاثة: جار له حق واحد، وهو أدنى الجيران حقا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r3.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r3.claim: When Aisha asks which of two neighbors should receive her gift, the Prophet tells her to give it to the one whose door is closer; Bukhari transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300/r3.anchor: عن عائشة؛ أنها سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: "إن لي جارين، فإلى أيهما أهدي؟ قال: "إلى أقربهما منك بابا".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r1.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r1.claim: Ali and Ibn Masud identify the companion at one's side as one's wife.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r1.anchor: قال الثوري، عن جابر الجعفي، عن الشعبي، عن علي وابن مسعود قالا هي المرأة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى وإبراهيم النخعي والحسن وسعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim reports a similar identification of the companion at one's side as the wife from these authorities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, and Qatada say the companion at one's side is a traveling companion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وقتادة: هو الرفيق في السفر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr specifies that the companion at one's side is a righteous traveling companion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو الرفيق الصالح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the term covers one's companion at home and one's companion on a journey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r5.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: هو جليسك في الحضر، ورفيقك في السفر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and a group identify the wayfarer as a guest.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r6.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وجماعة هو: الضيف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد وأبو جعفر الباقر والحسن والضحاك ومقاتل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r7.claim: These authorities say the wayfarer is someone passing through on a journey; Ibn Kathir calls this clearer, while allowing that both views coincide if guest means a passerby.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p300#2/r7.anchor: وهذا أظهر، وإن كان مراد القائل بالضيف: المار في الطريق، فهما سواء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r1.claim: The command concerning those under one's right hand is a charge to care for enslaved people, who are vulnerable and held in others' power.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r1.anchor: وصية بالأرقاء؛ لأن الرقيق ضعيف الحيلة أسير في أيدي الناس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r2.claim: The Prophet repeatedly urged prayer and care for those under one's right hand during his final illness, until his tongue could scarcely utter the words; Ibn Kathir calls this established.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r2.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جعل يوصي أمته في مرض الموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r3.claim: The Prophet called food given to oneself, one's child, wife, or servant charity; al-Nasa'i transmits the report and Ibn Kathir grades its chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r3.anchor: عن المقدام بن معد يكرب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما أطعمت نفسك فهو لك صدقة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r4.claim: When his steward had not fed the enslaved people, Abdullah ibn Amr ordered him to do so and cited the Prophet's warning that withholding their livelihood is sufficient sin; Muslim transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r4.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمرو أنه قال لقهرمان له: هل أعطيت الرقيق قوتهم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r5.claim: The Prophet says an enslaved person is owed food and clothing and should not be assigned work beyond capacity; Muslim transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r5.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "للمملوك طعامه وكسوته،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r6.claim: If a servant brings food, the Prophet advises sharing the meal or giving the servant a portion, since the servant endured its heat and preparation; Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r6.anchor: وعنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا أتى أحدكم خادمه بطعامه، فإن لم يجلسه معه، فليناوله لقمة أو لقمتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r7.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet calling servants one's brothers: feed and clothe them as oneself, do not overburden them, and assist if burdened; Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301/r7.anchor: وعن أبي ذر، رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "هم إخوانكم خولكم، جعلهم الله تحت أيديكم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r1.claim: The arrogant boaster is self-admiring and conceited, considers himself better than others, and is low before God and disliked by people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r1.anchor: أي: مختالا في نفسه، معجبا متكبرا، فخورا على الناس، يرى أنه خير منهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the arrogant one as conceited and the boaster as one who counts God's gifts while failing to thank Him, boasting of blessings with little gratitude.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد في قوله: {إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا} يعني: متكبرا {فخورا} يعني: يعد ما أعطي،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن واقد أبو رجاء الهروي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Waqid says bad treatment of those under one's authority accompanies arrogance and boastfulness, and filial disobedience accompanies tyrannical wretchedness; he cites 4:36 and 19:32.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن واقد أبي رجاء الهروي قال: لا تجد سيئ الملكة إلا وجدته مختالا فخورا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r4.speaker: العوام بن حوشب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab the same point about the arrogant boaster.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r4.anchor: وروى ابن أبي حاتم، عن العوام بن حوشب، مثله في المختال الفخور.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r5.claim: Abu Dharr confirms to Mutarrif that God hates the arrogant boaster and recites this verse as proof; Mutarrif had asked about a report that God loves three and hates three.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r5.anchor: قال مطرف: كان يبلغني عن أبي ذر حديث كنت أشتهي لقاءه، فلقيته فقلت: يا أبا ذر،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r6.claim: The Prophet counsels a man from Bahla against letting his garment trail, saying that trailing it is conceit and God does not love conceit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p301#2/r6.anchor: عن رجل من بلهجيم قال: قلت يا رسول الله، أوصني. قال: "إياك وإسبال الإزار، فإن إسبال الإزار من المخيلة،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r1.speaker: مشايخنا
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r1.claim: The author's teachers say Ali's arbitration was correct; Ali had cited a precedent against the Kharijites about the two arbiters.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r1.anchor: وقد قال مشايخنا: إن ما فعله (عليه السلام) عين الصواب؛

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r2.claim: When Qurans were raised, division emerged in Ali's army and he feared for his life, so arbitration was permissible and even obligatory.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r2.anchor: لأنه لما رفع المصاحف وظهرت الفرقة في عسكره وخاف على نفسه جاز له التحكيم، بل وجب،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r3.claim: Ali's arbitration is compared to the Prophet's agreement at Hudaybiyya and Hasan's peace as responses to circumstances.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r3.anchor: ولهذا صالح رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يوم الحديبية، وعلى هذا يحمل صلح الحسن (عليه السلام)،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r4.claim: Hasan made peace after being stabbed, when Ubayd Allah ibn Abbas sought safe conduct and the army fractured; this was concern for welfare.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r4.anchor: فإنه لما طعن واستأمن صاحب جيشه عبيد الله بن عباس، وتفرقت الكلمة في عسكره رأى الصلاح في الصلح،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r5.claim: God guides those who intend good to what is right, as in the promise to guide those who strive for Him.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن كل من يريد الخير وينويه فالله تعالى يوفقه للصواب والحق فلذلك قال تعالى:

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r6.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r6.claim: The common reading has ihsanan accusative, as an instruction to treat parents and the named groups well.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r6.anchor: قراءة العامة: إحسانا نصبا على معنى أحسنوا إليهم إحسانا،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r7.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Ablah reads ihsanun nominative, supplying that kindness to parents is obligatory.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r7.anchor: وعن ابن أبي عبلة بالرفع على تقدير: واجب الإحسان إليهما.

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r8.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r8.claim: The common reading coordinates the near neighbor with preceding objects.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r8.anchor: قراءة العامة: والجار ذي القربى عطفا على الكلام الأول

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r9.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r9.claim: Ibn Abi Ablah puts the neighbor and following terms in the accusative as an exhortation.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r9.anchor: عن ابن أبي عبلة، والجار وما يليه نصب على الإغراء.

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r10.speaker: الأعمش
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r10.claim: Al-A'mash reads al-janb with open jim and still nun; both forms are dialects.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r10.anchor: قراءة العامة: الجنب بضم الجيم والنون، وعن الأعمش: الجنب بفتح الجيم وسكون النون، وهما لغتان،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r11.claim: Jar is linked to turning or moving to a side; a neighbor is beside another, injustice deviates from right, and refuge asks God to turn one from hell.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r11.anchor: الجار أصله من العدول، جار أي عدل، وجاوره مجاورة وجوارا، وسمي الجار لعدوله إلى ناحيته في مسكنه،

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r12.claim: Janb means moving away; an unrelated neighbor is distant from kinship.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r12.anchor: وأصل الجنب التنحية، يقال: جنبت فلانا عن كذا فتجنب، أي نحيته فتنحى، ومنه: (واجنبني وبني)

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r13.claim: Mukhtal derives from imagining oneself; khayal likewise names an imagined image.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r13.anchor: والمختال: أصله التخيل وهو التصور، فالمختال لأنه يتخيل بخياله مزح النظر، ومنه الخيال؛

JISHUMI:v2p1550/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r14.claim: A fakhur counts advantages out of pride; one who counts them in gratitude is instead grateful.
JISHUMI:v2p1550/r14.anchor: والفخور هو: المعدد للمنافع كبرا وتطاولا، وهو من الفخر، والذي يعددها اعترافا بالنعمة هو: شكور.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r1.claim: The command means to treat one's parents excellently.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r2.claim: The near relatives include anyone related to you, such as a brother or uncle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r2.anchor: وبكل ما بينكم وبينه قربى من اخ أو عم أو غيرهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r3.claim: The first neighbor is close in location and the second farther away; another view takes the first as kin and the second as a non-relative, supported by Bal'a ibn Qays's verse contrasting a kinsman and a distant neighbor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r3.anchor: الذي قرب جواره ﴿ والجار الجنب ﴾ الذي جواره بعيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r4.claim: A reading puts ذا in the accusative as specification, emphasizing the neighbor's right because he has both neighborhood and kinship claims; the source compares the emphasis in 2:238.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r4.anchor: ( والجار ذا القربى ) نصبا على الاختصاص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r5.claim: The companion by one's side can be a travel companion, adjacent neighbor, study or work partner, or anyone in even brief close company; one must honor that bond through kindness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r5.anchor: هو الذي صحبك بأن حصل بجنبك إما رفيقا في سفر وإما جارا ملاصقا وإما شريكا في تعلم علم أو حرفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r6.claim: Another view identifies the companion by one's side as one's wife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#3/r6.anchor: فعليك ان ترعى ذلك الحق ولا تنساه وتجعله ذريعة إلى الإحسان وقيل الصاحب بالجنب المراة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r1.claim: The son of the road is a traveler stranded on the way; another view identifies him as a guest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r1.anchor: المسافر المنقطع به وقيل الضيف والمختال التياه الجهول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r2.claim: The arrogant boaster is a strutting fool who withholds generosity from relatives, companions, and servants and does not attend to them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r2.anchor: والمختال التياه الجهول الذي يتكبر عن إكرام أقاربه وأصحابه ومماليكه فلا يتحفى بهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r3.claim: A reading pronounces the jīm in الجنب with fatḥa and the nūn with sukūn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p541#4/r3.anchor: وقرىء ( والجار الجنب ) بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r1.claim: The injunction to treat parents well means to charge people to care for them graciously.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r2.claim: The kin are blood relatives among the people of family ties.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r2.anchor: هم قرابة النسب من ذوي الأرحام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r3.claim: An orphan is someone whose father has died before the person reaches puberty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r3.anchor: جمع يتيم وهو من مات أبوه لم يبلغ الحلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r4.claim: A miskin is someone overcome by the humiliation of poverty and need, and who presents himself as needy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r4.anchor: جمع مسكين وهو الذي قد ركبه ذل الفاقة والحاجة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid take the near neighbor as a neighbor related by blood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r5.anchor: أحدهما : بمعنى ذي القرابة والرحم وهم الذين بينك وبينهم قرابة نسب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r6.claim: A second interpretation is the neighbor near in Islam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r6.anchor: والثاني : يعني الجار ذي القربى بالإسلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid take the distant neighbor as one far from you in lineage and without kinship ties.
