MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r7.anchor: أحدهما : الجار البعيد في نسبه الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r8.claim: A second interpretation is a neighbor who is distant from you in religion and is a non-Muslim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنه المشرك البعيد في دينه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r9.claim: In Arabic, junub means distant; the ritually junub person is so called because he stays away from prayer until washing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r9.anchor: والجنب في كلام العرب هو البعيد , ومنه سمي الجنب لاعتزاله الصلاة حتى يغتسل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r10.speaker: الأعشى بن قيس بن ثعلبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r10.claim: Al-A'sha ibn Qays ibn Tha'laba's verse uses janāba for arriving from a distance, illustrating the sense of being apart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p484/r10.anchor: قال الأعشى بن قيس بن ثعلبة : أتيت حريثا زائرا عن جنابة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret the companion by one's side as a travel companion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه الرفيق في السفر , وهو قول ابن عباس , ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r2.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the companion by one's side as a man's wife, who is alongside him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنها زوجة الرجل التي تكون في جنبه , وهو قول ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the phrase as someone who stays close to you hoping to benefit from you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنه الذي يلزمك ويصحبك رجاء نفعك , وهو قول ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r4.claim: The Prophet says every person accompanying another is accountable for that companionship, even if it lasted only an hour of the day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r4.anchor: روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( كل صاحب يصحب صاحبا مسئول عن صحابته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r5.claim: The Prophet says the best companions with God are those best to their companions, and the best neighbors are those best to their neighbors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r5.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( خير الأصحاب عند الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r6.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r6.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Rabi' interpret the son of the road as a traveler passing through.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r6.anchor: أحدها : أنه المسافر المجتاز مارا , وهذا قول مجاهد , وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r7.speaker: الشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i interprets the phrase as someone who intends to travel but lacks the money for the journey.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r7.anchor: والثاني : هو الذي يريد سفرا ولا يجد نفقة , وهذا قول الشافعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the son of the road as a weak person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r8.anchor: والثالث : أنه الضعيف , وهو قول الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r9.claim: Sabil means road; a traveler is called the road's son as a water bird is called the son of water.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r9.anchor: والسبيل الطريق , ثم قيل لصاحب الطريق ابن السبيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r10.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r10.claim: An unnamed poet's image of the Pleiades above a traveler's head calls him an attached son of water, illustrating the expression.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p485/r10.anchor: وردت اعتسافا والثريا كأنها … على قمة الرأس ابن ماء ملحق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r1.claim: Those owned by one's right hand are enslaved people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r1.anchor: يعني المملوكين , فأضاف الملك إلى اليمين لاختصاصها بالتصرف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r2.claim: Ownership is attributed to the right hand because it is the means of control and disposal, like saying that one's mouth spoke or foot walked.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r2.anchor: فأضاف الملك إلى اليمين لاختصاصها بالتصرف كما يقال تكلم فوك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r3.claim: Mukhtāl is a person possessing khuyalāʾ, conceit or swagger.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r4.claim: The form is derived from the verb khāla, used for a man who acts proudly or conceitedly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r4.anchor: مفتعل من قولك : خال الرجل يخول خيلاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r5.speaker: العجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r5.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse calls the conceited person al-khāl, a garment of the ignorant, providing poetic evidence for the word.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r5.anchor: قال العجاج : والْخال ثوب من ثياب الجهال

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r6.claim: Fakhūr is someone who boasts over God's servants about the blessings and abundant provision God has granted him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p486/r6.anchor: والفخور : المفتخر على عباد الله بما أنعم الله عليه

MUQATIL:4:36/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:36/r1.claim: Worship God means affirm His unity; the People of Scripture worship Him without sincere devotion, so they are told not to associate any created thing with Him.
MUQATIL:4:36/r1.anchor: { واعبدوا الله } ، يعنى وحدوا الله، { ولا تشركوا به شيئا }؛ لأن أهل الكتاب يعبدون الله

MUQATIL:4:36/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:36/r2.claim: Goodness to parents means dutifulness, and goodness to relatives means maintaining family ties; charity is due to orphans and the needy.
MUQATIL:4:36/r2.anchor: { وبالوالدين إحسانا } ، يعنى برا بهما، { وبذي القربى } والإحسان إلى ذى القربى، يعنى صلته، { و } الإحسان إلى { واليتامى والمساكين }

MUQATIL:4:36/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:36/r3.claim: The near neighbor is a neighbor who is kin; the distant neighbor belongs to another people.
MUQATIL:4:36/r3.anchor: { والجار ذي القربى } ، يعنى جارا بينك وبينه قرابة، { والجار الجنب } ، يعنى من قوم آخرين،

MUQATIL:4:36/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:36/r4.claim: The companion by one's side is a companion in travel or at home; the son of the road is a guest who comes to stay and should be treated well.
MUQATIL:4:36/r4.anchor: { والصاحب بالجنب } ، يقول: الرفيق فى السفر والحضر، { وابن السبيل } ، يعنى الضيف ينزل عليك أن تحسن إليه،

MUQATIL:4:36/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r5.speaker: علي وعبدالله
MUQATIL:4:36/r5.claim: Ali and Abdullah interpret the companion by one's side as one's wife.
MUQATIL:4:36/r5.anchor: وعن على وعبدالله، قالا: { والصاحب بالجنب } ، المرأة، فأمر الله عز وجل بالإحسان إلى هؤلاء،

MUQATIL:4:36/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:36/r6.claim: Those held in one's right hand are servants and others in one's possession; they too are owed kindness.
MUQATIL:4:36/r6.anchor: { و } إلى { وما ملكت أيمانكم } من الخدم وغيره، وعن على وعبدالله، قالا: { والصاحب بالجنب } ،

MUQATIL:4:36/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:36/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:36/r7.claim: Mukhtāl means boastfully arrogant and fakhūr means prideful over God's blessings; such a person fails to receive God's gifts with gratitude.
MUQATIL:4:36/r7.anchor: { إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا } ، يعنى بطرا مرحا { فخورا } [آية: 36] فى نعم الله، لا يأخذ ما أعطاه الله عز وجل فيشكر.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r1.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r1.claim: A reported saying defines worship as keeping covenants, accepting what one has, guarding limits, and enduring loss.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r1.anchor: قيل العبودية أربعة الوفاء بالعهود والرضا بالموجود والحفظ للحدود والصبر على المفقود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r2.claim: The prohibition covers idols and anything else; the phrase may also use the verbal noun shirk.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r2.anchor: صنما وغيره ويحتمل المصدر أى إشراكا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r3.claim: Show parents kindness in speech and action, and support them financially when they need it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r3.anchor: وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا بالقول والفعل والانفاق عليهما عند الاحتياج

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r4.claim: Kinship includes anyone related to you, such as a brother or uncle.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r4.anchor: وبكل من بينكم وبينه قربى من أخ أو عم أو غيرهما

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r5.claim: The near neighbor may be near in residence; the distant neighbor may be a stranger, contrasted with a nearby kinsman.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r5.anchor: أى الذى جواره بعيدا والجار القريب النسيب والجار الجنب الأجنبى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r6.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r6.claim: Ali identifies the companion at one's side as one's wife.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r6.anchor: أى الزوجة عن على رضى الله عنه أو الذى صحبك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, the companion is anyone beside you as a travel partner, study partner, or neighbor in an assembly or mosque.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r7.anchor: أو الذى صحبك بأن حصل بجنبك إما رفيقا فى سفر أو شريكا فى تعلم علم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r8.claim: The wayfarer is a stranger or a guest.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r9.claim: Those under one's ownership are male and female slaves.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r10.claim: The arrogant person disdains relatives and neighbors and pays them no attention.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p221#3/r10.anchor: متكبرا يأنف عن قرابته وجيرانه فلا يلتفت إليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: A boastful person lists his merits out of pride; listing them as acknowledgment of God's gifts would instead be gratitude.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: يعدد مناقبه كبرا فإن عدها اعترافا كان شكورا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r1.claim: Scholars unanimously regard the verse as definitive, agreed upon, and unabrogated; the author says it is likewise in all scriptures and reason alone would recognize its authority.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r1.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أن هذه الآية من المحكم المتفق عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r2.claim: Worship is submission and need before the one with judgment and choice; God commands exclusive devotion, making the verse a foundation for cleansing deeds of ostentation and other impurities.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r2.anchor: وقد مضى معنى العبودية وهي التذلل والافتقار، لمن له الحكم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r3.claim: The author links sincerity to the warning that one hoping to meet the Lord must do good and associate no one in worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r3.anchor: فمن كان يرجو لقآء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r4.claim: The author cites the declaration that pure religion belongs to God alone.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r5.claim: The command to worship God is linked to the command to worship Him sincerely in religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r5.anchor: ومآ أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r6.speaker: بعض علمائنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r6.claim: Some scholars say purification for cooling or fasting to settle one's stomach does not fulfill worship if a worldly aim is mixed into devotion; God accepts only pure work.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r6.anchor: قال بعض علمائنا: إنه من تطهر تبردا أو صام محما لمعدته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r7.claim: An imam who senses someone entering during bowing should not wait, since waiting would make the bowing no longer solely for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r7.anchor: وكذلك إذا أحس الرجل بداخل في الركوع وهو إمام لم ينتظره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r8.claim: In a Muslim hadith qudsī, God says that whoever performs a deed while associating another with Him is left to that partner and the deed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r8.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r9.claim: Al-Dāraquṭnī reports sealed records presented on Judgment Day: God accepts only deeds intended for His sake, even though the angels had seen good in rejected deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r9.anchor: وروى الدارقطني عن أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r10.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس الفهري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r10.claim: A report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays al-Fihrī quotes the Prophet: God accepts only what is sincerely for Him, not what is split between Him, kin, or people's approval.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36/r10.anchor: وروي أيضا عن الضحاك بن قيس الفهري قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r1.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r1.claim: The scholars classify shirk as three forbidden degrees. The greatest is believing in a partner in divinity, the pre-Islamic form, warned against at 4:48.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r1.anchor: مسألة إذا ثبت هذا فاعلم أن علماءنا رضي الله عنهم قالوا: الشرك على ثلاث مراتب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r2.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r2.claim: The second degree is belief that another independently brings an act into existence, even without calling it a god; the scholars call the Qadariyya the community's Magians, and Ibn ʿUmar disavowed them in the Gabriel report.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r2.anchor: ويليه في الرتبة اعتقاد شريك لله تعالى في الفعل، وهو قول

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r3.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r3.claim: The third degree is ostentation: doing worship commanded for God for someone else. It invalidates deeds and is subtle; these verses and reports are cited to prohibit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r3.anchor: ويلي هذه الرتبة الإشراك في العبادة وهو الرياء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r4.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r4.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī explains in al-Riʿāya how ostentation corrupts deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد بن أبي فضالة الأنصاري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r5.claim: Ibn Mājah reports the Companion Abū Saʿīd ibn Abī Faḍāla: on Judgment Day, those who shared a deed intended for God with another should seek the other's reward, since God needs no partners.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r5.anchor: وفي سنن ابن ماجه عن أبي سعيد بن أبي فضالة الأنصاري

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r6.claim: The Prophet calls hidden shirk more fearful than the Antichrist: someone beautifies his prayer because another person is watching.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r7.speaker: شداد بن أوس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r7.claim: A report from Shaddād ibn Aws says the Prophet feared shirk for his community, meaning deeds for others and hidden desire, not worship of celestial bodies or idols; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmitted it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#2/r7.anchor: وفيه عن شداد بن أوس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r1.claim: Asked about hidden desire, the Prophet defines it as learning knowledge because one wants people to gather around him.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r1.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشهوة الخفية فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r2.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r2.claim: Sahl al-Tustarī's first kind of ostentation begins with acting for someone other than God while seeking to appear devout; he calls this hypocrisy and doubt in faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r2.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله التستري رضي الله عنه: الرياء على ثلاثة وجوه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r3.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r3.claim: Sahl's second kind begins sincerely for God, then gains energy when seen; if the person repents, he says all those deeds must be repeated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r3.anchor: والآخر يدخل في الشيء لله فإذا اطلع عليه غير الله نشط، فهذا إذا تاب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r4.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r4.claim: Sahl's third kind starts sincerely for God and ends in recognition and pleasure at praise; this is the ostentation God forbids.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r4.anchor: والثالث دخل في العمل بالإخلاص وخرج به لله فعرف بذلك ومدح عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r5.speaker: لقمان
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r5.claim: Luqmān tells his son that ostentation seeks the reward of deeds in this world, while the people worked for the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r5.anchor: قال لقمان لابنه: الرياء أن تطلب ثواب عملك في دار الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r6.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r6.claim: Sahl's remedy is to conceal deeds: perform what must be public sincerely, and prefer no one but God see what need not be shown.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r6.anchor: قيل له: فما دواء الرياء؟ قال كتمان العمل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r7.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r7.claim: Sahl says not to count a deed seen by other people as a true deed of devotion.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r7.anchor: قال: وكل عمل اطلع عليه الخلق فلا تعده من العمل.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r8.speaker: أيوب السختياني
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r8.claim: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī says no sensible person wants others to know where his deeds stand.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r8.anchor: وقال أيوب السختياني: ما هو بعاقل من أحب أن يعرف مكانه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r9.claim: Sahl's third kind is blameworthy when pleasure in praise seeks rank, affection, or material gain, because the heart delights in exposure even if it came after the deed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r9.anchor: إن كان سكونه وسروره إليهم لتحصل منزلته في قلوبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r10.claim: If God reveals a deed against the person's wishes, joy in God's favor is obedience, as the verse commands joy in His bounty and mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r10.anchor: فأما من أطلع الله عليه خلقه وهو لا يحب اطلاعهم عليه فيسر بصنع الله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r11.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r11.claim: Asked about a hadith of concealing a deed that pleases one when revealed, Sahl says the pleasure is gratitude that God made it known.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#3/r11.anchor: وقد سئل سهل عن حديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r1.claim: God pairs gratitude to parents with gratitude to Him; the author cites the command to thank God and one's parents.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r2.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says the Prophet taught that God's pleasure is in parents' pleasure and His anger in their anger.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r3.claim: The author says the discussion of relatives, orphans, and the poor has already appeared in Sūrat al-Baqara.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r4.claim: God commands preserving the neighbor, fulfilling the neighbor's rights, and respecting the neighbor's protected status, emphasizing the neighbor after parents and kin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r4.anchor: أما الجار فقد أمر الله تعالى بحفظه والقيام بحقه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ذي القربى is the close neighbor and الجنب the stranger; the author notes this is Arabic usage.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r6.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r6.claim: Lexicographers cite a poem using جنابة for distance and being a stranger, evidence for الجنب as a distant neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r6.anchor: وأنشد أهل اللغة: فلا تحرمني نائلا عن جنابة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r7.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r7.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse also uses عن جنابة for distance or being a stranger.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r7.anchor: وقال الأعشى: أتيت حريثا زائرا عن جنابة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r8.speaker: الأعمش والمفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash and al-Mufaḍḍal read الجار الجنب with fatḥa on jīm and a still nūn; related dialects mean having no kinship, with أجانب as plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والمفضل «والجار الجنب» بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r9.claim: Another analysis assumes an omitted noun: والجار ذي الجنب, the neighbor of the side or area.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r9.anchor: وقيل: على تقدير حذف المضاف، أي والجار ذي الجنب أي ذي الناحية.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r10.speaker: نوف الشامي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r10.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī identifies the close neighbor as Muslim and the distant neighbor as Jewish or Christian; the author says neighborly care is recommended for Muslims and non-Muslims alike, the correct view.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r10.anchor: وقال نوف الشامي: { والجار ذي القربى } المسلم { والجار الجنب } اليهودي والنصراني.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r11.claim: Neighborly kindness may mean material support or good companionship, refraining from harm, and defending the neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r11.anchor: والإحسان قد يكون بمعنى المواساة، وقد يكون بمعنى حسن العشرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r12.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r12.claim: In a Bukhārī report from ʿĀʾisha, the Prophet says Gabriel kept enjoining care for the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would inherit.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r12.anchor: روى البخاري عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r13.speaker: أبو شريح
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r13.claim: The Prophet swears three times that one whose neighbor is not safe from his harms lacks complete faith; this applies to every neighbor and requires avoiding harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#4/r13.anchor: وروي عن أبي شريح أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r1.claim: A prophetic report assigns three rights to a Muslim relative neighbor, two to a Muslim neighbor without kinship, and one to a non-Muslim neighbor: the right of neighborliness.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r1.anchor: الجيران ثلاثة فجار له ثلاثة حقوق وجار له حقان

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r2.claim: When ʿĀʾisha asked which of two neighbors should receive her gift, the Prophet told her to choose the one with the nearer door.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قلت يا رسول الله، إن لي جارين فإلى أيهما أهدي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r3.speaker: جماعة من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r3.claim: Some scholars take close and distant neighbors to mean those with near and far homes, using the gift report to support a neighbor's preemption right and the hadith about a neighbor's claim to adjoining property.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r3.anchor: فذهب جماعة من العلماء إلى أن هذا الحديث يفسر المراد من قوله تعالى: { والجار ذي القربى }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r4.claim: The author rejects that inference: ʿĀʾisha asked whom to gift first, and the Prophet prioritized the nearer door; the report also shows neighbor can mean more than an adjoining house.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r4.anchor: ولا حجة في ذلك، فإن عائشة رضي الله عنها إنما سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa denies preemption to a neighbor without shared wall or route if the adjoining neighbor relinquishes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r5.anchor: وقد خرج أبو حنيفة عن ظاهر هذا الحديث فقال: إن الجار اللصيق إذا ترك الشفعة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r6.speaker: عوام العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r6.claim: Most scholars say a bequest to neighbors includes adjoining and non-adjoining neighbors; Abū Ḥanīfa limits it to the adjoining neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r6.anchor: وعوام العلماء يقولون: إذا أوصى الرجل لجيرانه أعطى اللصيق وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي وابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r7.claim: Al-Awzāʿī and Ibn Shihāb define the neighborhood as forty houses in every direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r7.anchor: فكان الأوزاعي يقول: أربعون دارا من كل ناحية وقاله ابن شهاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r8.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet sent Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī to announce that forty houses count as neighbors and that none enters Paradise if a neighbor is unsafe from his harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r8.anchor: أن رجلا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني نزلت محلة قوم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r9.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib says anyone who hears the call to prayer is a neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r9.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: من سمع النداء فهو جار.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r10.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r10.claim: Another group defines a mosque's neighbor as anyone who hears the call to begin prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة: من سمع إقامة الصلاة فهو جار ذلك المسجد.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r11.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r11.claim: Another group says anyone sharing a quarter or city with a person is a neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#5/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة: من ساكن رجلا في محلة أو مدينة فهو جار.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r1.claim: The author links neighborhood to the verse saying the hypocrites would not remain in Medina except briefly, so their common residence counts as neighborliness.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r1.anchor: ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r2.claim: Neighbor relations have degrees, some closer than others; the nearest is one's wife, as the cited line calls her a neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r2.anchor: والجيرة مراتب بعضها ألصق من بعض، أدناها الزوجة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r3.claim: Muslim reports Abū Dharr's account of the Prophet advising him to add water to broth and look after his neighbors.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r3.anchor: ما رواه مسلم عن أبي ذر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r4.claim: Sharing food builds affection, good relations, and mutual help; cooking smells can distress neighbors and their hungry children, especially where the caregiver is poor or widowed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r4.anchor: فحض عليه السلام على مكارم الأخلاق لما يترتب عليها من المحبة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r5.claim: Sharing food prevents distress caused by cooking smells and children's hunger; the author mentions Jacob's separation from Joseph as similar sorrow.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r5.anchor: وكل هذا يندفع بتشريكهم في شيء من الطبيخ يدفع إليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r6.claim: The near neighbor is especially suited to a gift because each sees what enters and leaves the other's house and can respond quickly to unexpected needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r6.anchor: ولهذا المعنى حض عليه السلام الجار القريب بالهدية لأنه ينظر إلى ما يدخل دار جاره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r7.claim: Adding water is a tactful way to make generosity easy for a miser: water costs nothing, unlike extra meat.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r7.anchor: نبه بذلك على تيسير الأمر على البخيل تنبيها لطيفا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r8.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r8.claim: The cited couplet says the poet's cooking pot and his neighbor's are one, and it is raised to the neighbor before his own.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r8.anchor: ولقد أحسن القائل: قدري وقدر الجار واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r9.claim: A gift should be a customary amount, not a contemptibly small portion; if only a little is available, give it without disdain, and the recipient should accept it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#6/r9.anchor: ولا يهدي النزر اليسير المحتقر لقوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r1.claim: The Prophet tells believing women not to disdain giving a neighbor a gift, even a roasted sheep's hoof; Mālik transmits it in his Muwaṭṭaʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r1.anchor: أخرجه مالك في موطئه. وكذا قيدناه «يا نساء المؤمنات»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r2.claim: The author prefers the nominative يا نساء المؤمنات without annexation: the vocative يا أيها is omitted, النساء modifies أيها, and المؤمنات modifies النساء; the annexed reading is also reported but less common.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r2.anchor: وكذا قيدناه «يا نساء المؤمنات» بالرفع على غير الإضافة، والتقدير: يا أيها النساء المؤمنات

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r3.claim: The Prophet forbids preventing a neighbor from setting a beam in one's wall; Abū Hurayra threatens to cast the ruling among listeners. Variants include singular or plural خشبه and أكنافكم or أكتافكم.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r4.claim: The phrase لأرمين بها means that Abū Hurayra would throw the saying or case among them.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r5.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r5.claim: Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, and their companions read the beam report as recommending kindness, not imposing a duty, since property is forbidden without willing consent; they compare it to the recommendation not to bar a wife from the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r5.anchor: فذهب مالك وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهما إلى أن معناه الندب إلى بر الجار

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r6.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق وأبو ثور وداود بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Abū Thawr, Dāwūd, and hadith scholars hold allowing the beam obligatory; Abū Hurayra's insistence supports that he understood a duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأصحابه وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق وأبو ثور وداود بن علي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r7.claim: ʿUmar ruled that Muḥammad ibn Maslama must let al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Khalīfa's channel cross his land, even threatening to force him; Mālik transmits the ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r7.anchor: وهو مذهب عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه فإنه قضى على محمد بن مسلمة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r8.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r8.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues in al-Radd that Mālik recorded no Companion opposing ʿUmar and criticizes him for recording the ruling without adopting it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r8.anchor: وزعم الشافعي في كتاب «الرد» أن مالكا لم يرو عن أحد من الصحابة خلاف عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r9.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r9.claim: Abū ʿUmar rejects al-Shāfiʿī: Muḥammad ibn Maslama, the Anṣār, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf opposed ʿUmar in related watercourse disputes. With Companions divided, reason returns to the rule that Muslim property is inviolable without consent.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r9.anchor: قال أبو عمر: ليس كما زعم الشافعي لأن محمد بن مسلمة كان رأيه في ذلك خلاف رأي عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra's statement that he would cast the ruling among them indicates disagreement over whether the permission is obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#7/r10.anchor: ويدل على الخلاف في ذلك قول أبي هريرة: مالي أراكم عنها معرضين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r1.speaker: الأولون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r1.claim: The earlier jurists answer that a neighbor's use of an amenity does not violate the ban on taking property without consent: that concerns transfer and consumption, while the Prophet distinguished the rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r1.anchor: أجاب الأولون فقالوا: القضاء بالمرفق خارج بالسنة عن معنى قوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r2.claim: Malik reports that a judge in Medina named Abu al-Mutallib used to rule in favor of this neighbor's amenity right.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r2.anchor: وحكى مالك أنه كان بالمدينة قاض يقضي به يسمى أبو المطلب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r3.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r3.claim: A report attributed to Anas says that after a youth from their group died at Uhud, his mother praised him as destined for Paradise, and the Prophet warned that he might have spoken vainly or withheld harmless things.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r3.anchor: واحتجوا من الأثر بحديث الأعمش عن أنس قال: استشهد منا غلام يوم أحد فجعلت أمه تمسح التراب عن وجهه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r4.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r4.claim: Abu Umar says al-A'mash's hearing from Anas is not established, qualifying the report about the youth killed at Uhud.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r4.anchor: والأعمش لا يصح له سماع من أنس، والله أعلم. قاله أبو عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r5.claim: The Prophet's comprehensive list of a neighbor's rights includes lending, assistance, aid in need, visiting illness, attending burial, sharing joy and grief, sharing food discreetly, and avoiding harmful construction; only a few fulfill all these rights.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r5.anchor:
حديث
" معاذ بن جبل قال: قلنا يا رسول الله، ما حق الجار؟

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls the neighbor-rights narration comprehensive and حسن, while noting that its chain contains the disapproved narrator Abu al-Fadl Uthman ibn Matar al-Shaybani.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r6.anchor: هذا حديث جامع وهو حديث حسن، في إسناده أبو الفضل عثمان بن مطر الشيباني غير مرضي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r7.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r7.claim: The scholars hold that the injunctions to honor a neighbor are unrestricted and include a non-Muslim neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r7.anchor: قال العلماء: الأحاديث في إكرام الجار جاءت مطلقة غير مقيدة حتى الكافر كما بينا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r8.claim: When asked whether Muslims should feed polytheists from sacrificial meat, the Prophet said not to feed them from Muslims' sacrifices.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r8.anchor:
يا رسول الله أنطعمهم من لحوم النسك؟ قال:
" لا تطعموا المشركين من نسك المسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the prohibition may concern an obligatory sacrifice, whose performer may not eat from it or feed the wealthy; non-obligatory sacrifice may be given to protected non-Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#8/r9.anchor: يحتمل النسك الواجب في الذمة الذي لا يجوز للناسك أن يأكل منه ولا أن يطعمه الأغنياء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r1.claim: While distributing sacrificial meat, the Prophet told Aisha to begin with their Jewish neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r1.anchor: لعائشة عند تفريق لحم الأضحية: «ابدئي بجارنا اليهودي»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr was asked three times whether his household had sent meat to their Jewish neighbor; he cited the Prophet's teaching that Gabriel repeatedly urged care for neighbors until he thought they would inherit.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r2.anchor: وروي أن شاة ذبحت في أهل عبد الله بن عمرو فلما جاء قال: أهديتم لجارنا اليهودي؟ ثلاث مرات

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies the companion by one's side primarily as a travel companion, following Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r3.anchor: والأول أصح وهو قول ابن عباس وابن جبير وعكرمة ومجاهد والضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r4.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r4.claim: Ali, Ibn Masud, and Ibn Abi Layla interpret the companion by one's side as one's wife; al-Qurtubi prefers the travel-companion reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r4.anchor: وقال علي وابن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets the phrase as someone who keeps close company with a person in hope of benefiting from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r5.anchor: ابن جريج: هو الذي يصحبك ويلزمك رجاء نفعك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r6.claim: A report transmitted by al-Tabari describes the Prophet giving his straight walking stick to a companion and saying that everyone is answerable for the companionship of another, even for an hour in the day.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r6.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان معه رجل من أصحابه وهما على راحلتين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r7.speaker: ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r7.claim: Rabi'a says travel chivalry means sharing provisions, minimizing disagreement with companions, and joking often without disobeying God.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r7.anchor: وقال ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن: للسفر مروءة وللحضر مروءة فأما المروءة في السفر فبذل الزاد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r8.speaker: ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r8.claim: Rabi'a says the chivalry of settled life consists of frequent mosque attendance, Qur'an recitation, and many bonds of brotherhood for God's sake.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r8.anchor: وأما المروءة في الحضر فالإدمان إلى المساجد، وتلاوة القرآن وكثرة الإخوان في الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r9.speaker: بعض بني أسد وقيل حاتم الطائي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r9.claim: A poem attributed either to a man of Banu Asad or to Hatim al-Ta'i illustrates sharing one's mount and provisions with a companion and acknowledging the companion's contribution.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r9.anchor: ولبعض بني أسد وقيل إنها لحاتم الطائي: إذا ما رفيقي لم يكن خلف ناقتي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r10.claim: Although the travel companion is the preferred referent, al-Qurtubi says the verse's general wording can encompass all the reported kinds of companion.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r10.anchor: وقد تتناول الآية الجميع بالعموم. والله أعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r11.claim: Mujahid says the wayfarer is a traveler passing by; the word is related to the road because the traveler passes along and stays with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد: هو الذي يجتاز بك مارا. والسبيل الطريق فنسب المسافر إليه لمروره عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r12.claim: Kindness to a wayfarer includes giving help, offering hospitality, guiding the traveler, and directing them rightly.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r12.anchor: ومن الإحسان إليه إعطاؤه وإرفاقه وهدايته ورشده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r13.claim: The command concerning those held in one's right hand obliges kindness to enslaved people, as the Prophet's teaching elaborates in the following discussion.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#9/r13.anchor: أمر الله تعالى بالإحسان إلى المماليك، وبين ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r1.claim: Abu Dharr wore the same kind of garment as his servant after the Prophet rebuked him for insulting a brother's non-Arab mother; the Prophet called servants brothers, ordered equal food and clothing, forbade overburdening them, and required assistance if burdened.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r1.anchor: عن المعرور بن سويد قال: مررنا بأبي ذر بالربذة وعليه برد وعلى غلامه مثله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra once rode a mule with his servant behind him and said he would rather share two burning embers than make the servant run behind the mount.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r2.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة أنه ركب بغلة ذات يوم فأردف غلامه خلفه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r3.claim: The Prophet said to feed and clothe servants who suit their masters as the masters feed and clothe themselves; those who do not suit them may be sold, but God's creatures must not be tormented.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r3.anchor: وخرج أبو داود عن أبي ذر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains لايمكم as 'agreed with you' and الملايمة as agreement or compatibility.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r5.claim: The Prophet assigned a slave food and clothing and limited assigned work to what the slave can bear.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r5.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" للمملوك طعامه وكسوته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r6.claim: The Prophet taught masters to say 'my boy' or 'my girl' instead of 'my male slave' or 'my female slave'; al-Qurtubi points to fuller discussion in Surah Yusuf.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r6.anchor: لا يقل أحدكم عبدي وأمتي بل ليقل فتاي وفتاتي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r7.claim: The Prophet urged masters toward noble conduct, kindness, and humility instead of seeing themselves as superior: all are God's servants and property, while their differing relations serve divine favor and wisdom.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r7.anchor: فندب صلى الله عليه وسلم السادة إلى مكارم الأخلاق وحضهم عليها وأرشدهم إلى الإحسان وإلى سلوك طريق التواضع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r8.claim: A master may give servants food and clothing of lower quality or quantity than his own if he fulfills the servants' required minimum; al-Qurtubi says there is no disagreement on this.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#10/r8.anchor: فإن أطعموهم أقل مما يأكلون، وألبسوهم أقل مما يلبسون صفة ومقدارا جاز إذا قام بواجبه عليه. ولا خلاف في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r1.claim: Qurtubi reports the Muslim narration from Abd Allah ibn Amr: withholding the provisions of those one owns is sufficient sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r1.anchor: كفى بالمرء إثما أن يحبس عمن يملك قوتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r2.claim: The Prophet made freeing a slave expiation for striking or slapping the slave without a due legal punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r2.anchor:
ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من ضرب عبده حدا لم يأته أو لطمه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r3.speaker: نفر من الصحابة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r3.claim: Some Companions reportedly allowed a servant to retaliate for a child who struck him, and freed the servant when retaliation was waived.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r3.anchor: وجاء عن نفر من الصحابة أنهم اقتصوا للخادم من الولد في الضرب واعتقوا الخادم لما لم يرد القصاص

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r4.claim: The Prophet said that a person who accuses his slave of fornication will face the eighty lashes on Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r4.anchor: من قذف مملوكه بالزنى أقام عليه الحد يوم القيامة ثمانين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r5.claim: The Prophet warned that a person with bad conduct toward those under his authority will not enter Paradise.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says bad character brings ill fortune, good stewardship brings growth, kinship extends life, and charity averts an evil death.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r6.anchor: سوء الخلق شؤم وحسن الملكة نماء وصلة الرحم تزيد في العمر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r7.claim: The Prophet said that a righteous enslaved person receives two rewards; Abu Hurayra swore he would have wished to die enslaved but for jihad, pilgrimage, and honoring his mother.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r7.anchor: والذي نفس أبي هريرة بيده لولا الجهاد في سبيل الله والحج

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r8.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that a slave who advises his master and worships God well receives his reward twice over.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r9.speaker: أبو عمر يوسف بن عبد البر وأبو بكر محمد بن عبد الله العامري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r9.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr and al-Amiri favor the slave's merit: the slave is charged both with worshipping God and serving a master, and reports promise double reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r9.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب أبو عمر يوسف بن عبد البر النمري وأبو بكر محمد بن عبدالله بن أحمد العامري البغدادي الحافظ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r10.claim: The case for the free person's greater merit is independence in religious and worldly affairs; the enslaved lack autonomy, hold fewer offices and testimony roles, and face reduced penalties, while free people carry greater duties and effort and so may earn greater reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r10.anchor: استدل من فضل الحر بأن قال: الاستقلال بأمور الدين والدنيا إنما يحصل بالأحرار والعبد كالمفقود لعدم استقلاله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r11.claim: On the argument for the free, Abu Hurayra's wish to die enslaved is explained by opportunities a slave lacks, including jihad and pilgrimage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#11/r11.anchor: وقد أشار إلى هذا أبو هريرة بقوله: لولا الجهاد والحج، أي لولا النقص الذي يلحق العبد لفوت هذه الأمور

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r1.claim: Anas reports Gabriel's repeated counsel about neighbors, women, servants, using the tooth-stick, and night prayer; the Prophet says this counsel nearly led him to expect inheritance for neighbors, a limit on divorce, emancipation after a term, a sore mouth from tooth-cleaning, and sleeplessness among the best worshippers.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r1.anchor: ما زال جبريل يوصيني بالجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi glosses God's not loving as not being pleased; the warning means He will not show the person bearing these traits the effects of His favor in the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إن الله لا يحب } أي لا يرضى.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r3.claim: A mukhtal is arrogant and full of self-conceit; a fakhur boasts of his merits out of pride, and fakhr denotes extravagance and self-exaltation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r3.anchor: والمختال ذو الخيلاء أي الكبر. والفخور الذي يعدد مناقبه كبرا. والفخر: البذخ والتطاول

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r4.claim: These traits are singled out because they lead people to disdain poor relatives, poor neighbors, and others named in the verse, thereby neglecting God's command to show kindness.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r4.anchor: وخص هاتين الصفتين بالذكر هنا لأنهما تحملان صاحبيهما على الأنفة من القريب الفقير والجار الفقير

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r5.speaker: عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r5.claim: Asim, according to al-Mufaddal, reads الجار الجنب with an open jim and a still nun; al-Mahdawi explains it through an omitted genitive, 'the neighbor of the side or region.'
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فيما ذكر المفضل عنه { والجار الجنب } بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash cites the line 'People are on one side and the ruler on another' to show that جنب can mean a side or region, hence a neighbor distant from kinship.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:36#12/r6.anchor:
وأنشد الأخفش:
الناس جنب والأمير جنب

QASHANI:4:36/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36/r1.claim: Worship means turning exclusively toward God and annihilating in Him, the utmost humility.
QASHANI:4:36/r1.anchor: خصصوه بالتوجه إليه، والفناء فيه، الذي هو غاية التذلل

QASHANI:4:36/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36/r2.claim: Associating anything with God means asserting its independent existence.
QASHANI:4:36/r2.anchor: ولا تشركوا به شيئا } بإثبات وجوده

QASHANI:4:36/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36/r3.claim: The parents are spirit and soul from which the heart is born; fulfill their rights by drawing from spirit and orienting to it, and purifying and protecting the soul from worldly love, greed, and Satan while restraining appetites.
QASHANI:4:36/r3.anchor: ووفوا حقوقهما وراعوهما حق المراعاة بالاستفاضة من الأول

QASHANI:4:36/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36/r4.claim: Near kin are those like you in original preparedness and spiritual affinity.
QASHANI:4:36/r4.anchor: الذي يناسبكم في الحقيقة بحسب القرب في الاستعداد الأصلي

QASHANI:4:36/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36/r5.claim: Orphans are prepared people cut off by veiling from the holy spirit, their true father.
QASHANI:4:36/r5.anchor: المستعدين المنقطعين عن نور الروح القدسي الذي هو الأب الحقيقي

QASHANI:4:36/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36/r6.claim: The needy are righteous people without a share in knowledge, gnosis, or realities; they are still and unable to travel, ending in the Garden of acts.
QASHANI:4:36/r6.anchor: أي: لا حظ من العلوم والمعارف والحقائق، فسكنوا ولم يقدروا على المسير

QASHANI:4:36#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#2/r1.claim: The near neighbor is at a spiritual station close to yours; the distant neighbor is far; the companion by your side shares your station and accompanies you.
QASHANI:4:36#2/r1.anchor: في مقام من مقامات السلوك، قريب من مقامك

QASHANI:4:36#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#2/r2.claim: The companion by your side shares your station and travels alongside you.
QASHANI:4:36#2/r2.anchor: والرفيق الذي هو في عين مقامكم ويرافقكم في سيركم

QASHANI:4:36#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#2/r3.claim: The wayfarer travels the path of truth, estranged from the soul's home and not yet at a station of God's people.
QASHANI:4:36#2/r3.anchor: أي: السالك في طريق الحق، الداخل في الغربة عن مأوى النفس

QASHANI:4:36#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#2/r4.claim: Those under one's right hand are one's people of will and love, servants deserving kindness suited to each.
QASHANI:4:36#2/r4.anchor: من أهل إرادتكم ومحبتكم، الذين هم عبيدكم كلا بما يناسبه

QASHANI:4:36#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, near kin are high malakut spirits, orphans spiritual faculties, and needy psychic faculties; near neighbor intellect, distant neighbor imagination, companion longing and will, wayfarer thought, and owned servants acquired virtues that source good acts.
QASHANI:4:36#2/r5.anchor: وإن شئت أولت ذي القربى بما يتصل به من الملكوت العالية من المجردات

QASHANI:4:36#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#3/r1.claim: The arrogant person advances by self-reliance rather than God and admires their own deeds.
QASHANI:4:36#3/r1.anchor: يسعى في السلوك بنفسه لا بالله، معجبا بأعماله

QASHANI:4:36#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:36#3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:36#3/r2.claim: The boastful person delights in states, stations, and perfections, becoming veiled by seeing these qualities in themselves.
QASHANI:4:36#3/r2.anchor: مبتهجا بأحواله ومقاماته وكمالاته، محتجبا برؤيتها

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r1.claim: After directing spouses to treat one another well and end quarrels, God turns to ten further kinds of good conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r1.anchor: لما أرشد كل واحد من الزوجين إلى المعاملة الحسنة مع الآخر وإلى إزالة الخصومة والخشونة

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command to worship God as a command to affirm His oneness.

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r3.claim: Rāzī defines worship as every act or omission done solely in response to God's command, including deeds of the heart and body; it is not limited to monotheism.
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r3.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن كل فعل وترك يؤتى به لمجرد أمر الله تعالى بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r4.claim: The ban on associating partners commands sincerity: worshipping another alongside God is incompatible with exclusive devotion, as 98:5 says.
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r4.anchor: لأن من عبد مع الله غيره كان مشركا ولا يكون مخلصا

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r5.claim: The wording ellipses an imperative, “do good to parents”; Rāzī compares “striking the necks” in 47:4, meaning “strike them.”
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r5.anchor: واتفقوا على أن ههنا محذوفا ، والتقدير : وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r6.speaker: كثير
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r6.claim: The poet Kathīr's line using aḥsin demonstrates the Arabic construction of doing good to someone.
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r6.anchor: قال كثير : أسيئى بنا أو أحسنى لا ملومة لدنيا ولا مقلية إن تقلت

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r7.claim: God repeatedly joins kindness to parents with worship and monotheism—in this verse, 17:23, and 31:14—showing the weight of their rights.
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r7.anchor: قرن إلزام بر الوالدين بعبادته وتوحيده في مواضع : أحدها : في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r8.claim: The command includes not saying “uff,” not rebuking parents, and speaking graciously (17:23); even unbelieving parents merit good companionship, though one must not obey a call to shirk (31:15).
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r8.anchor: فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r9.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that a man from Yemen sought the Prophet's permission to join jihad; told to ask his parents, he had not, so the Prophet ordered him to return and honor them unless they permitted him to fight.
RAZI-FULL:v10p76#3/r9.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه : أن رجلا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من اليمن

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r1.claim: Kindness to parents means serving them, speaking gently without raised voices, meeting their needs and supporting them as able, and not threatening or killing them.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الإحسان إلى الوالدين هو أن يقوم بخدمتهما ، وألا يرفع صوته عليهما

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r2.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī allows killing a parent only if leaving them alive would let them kill the child; otherwise enabling one's own death is forbidden self-destruction.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي : إلا أن يضطر إلى ذلك بأن يخاف أن يقتله أن ترك قتله

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r3.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet forbade Ḥanẓala b. Abī ʿĀmir al-Rāhib from killing his unbelieving father.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r3.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى حنظلة بن أبي عامر الراهب عن قتل أبيه

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r4.claim: “Near kin” commands maintaining family ties, as the opening of the sūra also commands.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r4.anchor: وهو أمر بصلة الرحم كما ذكر في أول السورة بقوله : { والأرحام }

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r5.claim: Parents are kin too, but birth-kin are singled out before other relatives because this is the closest relation and has special rights.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r5.anchor: لما كانت مخصوصة بكونها أقرب القرابات وكانت مخصوصة بخواص لا تحصل في غيرها

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r6.claim: Orphans suffer both childhood and lack of a provider, leaving them especially helpless and deserving of compassion.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r6.anchor: واعلم أن اليتيم مخصوص بنوعين من العجز : أحدهما : الصغر ، والثاني : عدم المنفق

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to treat orphans gently, raise them and stroke their heads; a guardian should carefully protect their property.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يرفق بهم ويربيهم ويمسح رأسهم ، وإن كان وصيا لهم فليبالغ

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r8.claim: Although the poor lack wealth, an adult can present his case to others to gain benefit or avert harm; an orphan cannot, which is why orphans are mentioned first.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r8.anchor: فلهذا المعنى قدم الله اليتيم في الذكر على المسكين

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r9.claim: Kindness to a poor person may mean giving generously or refusing courteously, as the command not to rebuff a petitioner says in 93:10.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r9.anchor: والإحسان إلى المسكين إما بالإجمال إليه ، أو بالرد الجميل . كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r10.claim: One interpretation takes the near neighbor as one whose home is close and the distant neighbor as one whose home is farther away.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r10.anchor: قيل : هو الذي قرب جواره ، والجار الجنب هو الذي بعد جواره .

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r11.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r11.claim: The Prophet warns that a person whose neighbor is unsafe from his harms will not enter Paradise; neighborliness extends forty homes.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r11.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لا يدخل الجنة من لا يأمن جاره بوائقه ألا وإن الجوار أربعون دارا )

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r12.speaker: الزهري
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r12.claim: Al-Zuhrī specifies forty neighbor homes in each of the four directions: right, left, front, and behind.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r12.anchor: وكان الزهري يقول : أربعون يمنة ، وأربعون يسرة ، وأربعون أماما وأربعون خلفا .

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r13.claim: A woman who fasted and prayed but verbally harmed neighbors was condemned by the Prophet as having no good and being destined for Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r13.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قيل : يا رسول الله ان فلانة تصوم النهار

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r14.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r14.claim: A Prophetic report lists neighborly duties: support a poor neighbor, lend on request, congratulate good fortune, console hardship, visit illness, and attend the funeral; few meet these duties.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r14.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( والذي نفس محمد بيده لا يؤدي حق الجار إلا من رحم الله

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r15.claim: Another interpretation takes the near neighbor as a blood relative and the distant neighbor as a non-relative outsider.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r15.anchor: وقال آخرون : عني بالجار ذي القربى : القريب النسيب ، وبالجار الجنب : الجار الأجنبي

RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r16.claim: A reading puts dhā in the accusative as an emphatic specification, highlighting the neighbor's greater claim through both adjacency and kinship; Rāzī compares 2:238.
RAZI-FULL:v10p77/r16.anchor: وقرىء ( والجار ذا القربى ) نصبا على الاختصاص ، كما قرىء ( حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى )

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī derives al-janb from distance, opposite kinship: it describes a stranger far from home or kin; the same root names sides and ritual impurity because of separation from purity and mosque prayer until washing.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r1.anchor: الواحدي : الجنب نعت على وزن فعل ، وأصله من الجنابة

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r2.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r2.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal transmits from ʿĀṣim a reading with fatḥa on jīm and sukūn on nūn; it permits reading the phrase as a neighbor of the side or as an emphatic adjective.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r2.anchor: وروى المفضل عن عاصم : { والجار الجنب } بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r3.claim: For the variant, al-janb may mean a side, with an understood construct (the neighbor of the side), or function as an intensive adjective like generosity and munificence.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أنه يريد بالجنب الناحية ، ويكون التقدير : والجار ذي الجنب

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r4.claim: The companion at one’s side includes a travel companion, adjoining neighbor, work or study partner, or anyone who briefly sits beside one; their claim must be honored and made a means of kindness.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r4.anchor: وهو الذي صحبك بأن حصل بجنبك إما رفيقا في

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r5.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the companion at one’s side as a wife, who is with and lies beside her husband.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r5.anchor: قيل : الصاحب الجنب : المرأة فانها تكون معك وتضجع

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r6.claim: The son of the road is a traveler cut off from his home country.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r6.anchor: وهو المسافر الذي انقطع عن بلده

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r7.claim: A second reported interpretation takes the son of the road to mean a guest.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r7.anchor: وهو المسافر الذي انقطع عن بلده ، وقيل : الضيف

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r8.claim: Kindness to enslaved people is a major act of obedience; ʿUmar reports the Prophet advised replacing a servant whose temperament does not suit the purchaser’s, since people have different temperaments, and forbade tormenting God’s servants.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r8.anchor: روى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من ابتاع شيئا من الخدم

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet’s final words were to attend to prayer and those whom one’s right hand possesses.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r9.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان آخر كلامه : ( الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم )

RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r10.claim: A man stopped beating his servant when the servant invoked the Messenger; the Prophet said God had the greater right to protect a person seeking refuge, and warned the master of Hellfire before he freed the servant.
RAZI-FULL:v10p78/r10.anchor: وروي أنه كان رجل بالمدينة يضرب عبده ، فيقول العبد أعوذ بالله

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r1.claim: Kind treatment of enslaved people means not imposing what they cannot bear, avoiding harsh speech and dealing well with them, and providing the food and clothing they need.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الاحسان اليهم من وجوه : أحدها : أن لا يكلفهم ما لا طاقة لهم به

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r2.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, enslaved women were mistreated by being forced into prostitution for earnings from their sexual services.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r2.anchor: وكانوا في الجاهلية يسيئون إلى المملوك فيكلفون الاماء البغاء

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r3.claim: Some say every living creature is owned, and kindness appropriate to each creature is a great act of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كل حيوان فهو مملوك ، والاحسان إلى الكل بما يليق به

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r4.claim: Mentioning the right hand is emphatic, as in saying that one’s foot walked or one’s hand took; he also cites the maxim that a hand is responsible for what it takes and God’s reference to what His hands made.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r4.anchor: واعلم أن ذكر اليمين تأكيد وهو كما يقال : مشت رجلك ، وأخذت يدك

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the conceited person as one who is inflated in his own estimation and fails to fulfill anyone’s rights.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد بالمختال العظيم في نفسه الذي لا يقوم بحقوق أحد

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r6.claim: Fakhr is self-exaltation; the boastful person enumerates his merits out of arrogance and vaunting.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r6.anchor: ومعنى الفخر التطاول ، والفخور الذي يعدد مناقبه كبرا وتطاولا

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the boastful person flaunts before God’s servants the kinds of favors God has bestowed on him.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هو الذي يفخر على عباد الله بما أعطاه الله من أنواع نعمه

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r8.claim: The conceited person is unlikely to honor others’ rights; adding ‘boastful’ warns against honoring them merely for reputation, rather than solely in obedience to God.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r8.anchor: لأن المختال هو المتكبر ، وكل من كان متكبرا فانه قلما يقوم برعاية الحقوق

RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r9.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj notes that the derivation of ikhtiyāl was discussed in the commentary on 3:14.
RAZI-FULL:v10p79/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج : وإنما ذكر الاختيال ههنا ، وذكرنا اشتقاق هذه اللفظة عند قوله :

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r1.claim: Servanthood means embracing God's commands and avoiding what He forbids.

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r2.claim: Open association is belief in another deity; hidden association notices any existent besides God. Unity recognizes that every event exists through God, its maker, originator, and sustainer, with no creaturely share in creation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r2.anchor: الشرك جليه اعتقاد معبود سواه ، وخفيه : ملاحظة موجود سواه

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r3.claim: Subtle ostentation, flattery, self-admiration, acting for people's gaze, savoring their praise, and shrinking under criticism are all hidden shirk.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r3.anchor: دقائق الرياء وخفايا المصانعات وكوامن الإعجاب والعمل على رؤية الخلق ،

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r4.claim: The sequence begins with parents because they are one's kind and raised one; their rights are the first step toward further growth and realization of knowledge.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r4.anchor: أمرت أولا بحقوقهما لأنهما من جنسك ومنها تربيتك ،

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r5.claim: Being fit for companionship with relatives, the poor, orphans, and their peers is a stage toward becoming worthy of companionship with God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r5.anchor: إذا صلحت للصحبة والعشرة مع ذوي القربى والفقراء والمساكين واليتامى ومن في طبقتهم -

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r6.claim: Since a house neighbor deserves kindness, one must not neglect the heart, the neighbor of the self, or allow corrupt thoughts to settle there.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r6.anchor: فجار نفسك - وهو قلبك - أولى بألا تضيعه ولا تغفل عنه

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r7.claim: The spirit is the heart's neighbor and deserves protection from incompatible occupants; the secret is the spirit's neighbor and must be guarded from absence from witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r7.anchor: فجار قلبك - وهو روحك - أولى أن تحامي على حقها

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r14.claim: Their immediate punishment is exclusion from the company of God's beloved, which is itself a sufficient trial.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r14.anchor: فعقوبتهم في العاجل أنهم ليسوا من جملة محبيه ، وكفى بذلك محنة

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r15.claim: The conceited person looks at himself, while the show-off looks at other people; both bear the mark of hidden shirk.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r15.anchor: والمختال الذي ينظر غلى نفسه والمرائي الذي ينظر إلى أبناء جنسه ،

QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r16.claim: Fakhūr is likened to a camel or ewe whose udder is tied to exaggerate its milk; likewise, a pretender displays false spiritual rank and a show-off spends to be seen.
QUSHAYRI:v1p206/r16.anchor: والفخور من الإبل كالمصراة من الغنم وهو الذي سدت أخلافه ليجتمع فيها الدر

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r1.claim: The Quran repeatedly places virtue toward parents immediately after worshipping God alone and commands kindness toward parents in other verses.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r1.anchor: This is one of several verses that place virtue toward parents immediately after the command to worship none but God

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r2.claim: Iḥsān derives from a root meaning beautiful; its derivatives denote virtue, moral beauty, goodness, and doing what is beautiful and good, and toward parents it means filial piety.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r2.anchor: The Arabic word here used to denote virtuous behavior is iḥsān, which comes from a root meaning “beautiful”

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r3.claim: The list of people deserving virtue, kindness, and charity resembles lists elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r3.anchor: The list provided here of those to whom one should be virtuous, kind, and charitable is similar to other such lists in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r4.claim: The neighbor who is of kin is generally understood as a family member.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r4.anchor: the neighbor who is of kin is generally considered to refer to one’s family members

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r5.speaker: A minority tradition
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r5.claim: A minority tradition understands the kin-neighbor as Muslims, those close in religion.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r5.anchor: a minority tradition identifies it as a reference to Muslims generally, that is, those to whom one is close in religion

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r6.claim: The non-kin neighbor may mean a nonfamily member or friend, or someone geographically or religiously distant.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r6.anchor: may mean nonfamily members or friends, but also those who are distant from oneself geographically or in religion

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r7.claim: Junub relates to distance; ritual impurity after sexual relations is called junub because it distances a person from prayer until purification.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r7.anchor: The word junub relates to something that is distant; the state of ritual impurity brought about by sexual relations is also referred to as junub

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r8.claim: Virtue toward slaves may mean freeing them, a repeatedly recommended expiation, or simply treating them well.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r8.anchor: which may mean freeing them, an act repeatedly recommended as a form of expiation

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r9.claim: The companion at one’s side may be a traveling companion or, more specifically, one’s wife.
