STUDYQURAN:4:36/r9.anchor: The companion at your side may refer to one’s traveling companion or more specifically to one’s wife

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r10.claim: The verse calls for kindness to everyone, especially dependents and people with less social power, including parents, needy relatives, orphans, wives, non-Muslims, and slaves.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r10.anchor: The verse thus enjoins kindness and virtuous behavior as a rule toward all, particularly toward those over whom one might have a certain power

STUDYQURAN:4:36/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r11.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r11.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says all revealed scriptures similarly command kindness to others, a principle reason can know even without revelation.
STUDYQURAN:4:36/r11.anchor: Qurṭubī asserts that similar enjoinders to kindness toward others are found in all Divinely revealed books

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r1.claim: Worship God by obeying and humbling yourselves to Him, affirm His sole lordship, follow His commands and avoid His prohibitions, and assign Him no partner in worship or lordship.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r1.anchor: بالطاعة، واخضعوا له بها، وأفردوه بالربوبية، وأخلصوا له الخضوع والذلة

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r2.claim: Iḥsānan is accusative as an exhortation: God commands dutiful kindness to parents.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r2.anchor: وأمركم بالوالدين إحسانا، يعني برا بهما؛ ولذلك نصب الإحسان، لأنه أمر منه جل ثناؤه بلزوم الإحسان

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r3.claim: Some explain the phrase as an instruction to enjoin yourselves to treat parents well; al-Ṭabarī says this is close to his own explanation.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r3.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم: معناه: واستوصوا بالوالدين إحسانا، وهو قريب المعنى مما قلناه

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r4.claim: Relatives include maternal or paternal kin whose blood relationship is near; kindness means maintaining those kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r4.anchor: وهم ذوو قرابة أحدنا من قبل أبيه أو أمه ممن قربت منه قرابته برحمه من أحد الطرفين إحسانا بصلة رحمه

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r5.claim: An orphan is a child whose father has died.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r5.anchor: فإنهم جمع يتيم، وهو الطفل الذي قد مات والده وهلك

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r6.claim: The poor are those overcome by the abasement of want and need.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r6.anchor: وهو الذي قد ركبه ذل الفاقة والحاجة، فتمسكن لذلك

TAB-FULL:v7p5/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r7.claim: God commands care and compassion for these groups and adherence to His instruction to treat them well.
TAB-FULL:v7p5/r7.anchor: استوصوا بهؤلاء إحسانا إليهم , وتعطفوا عليهم، والزموا وصيتي في الإحسان إليهم

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the near-kinsman neighbor as a neighbor related to you.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] يعني: «الذي بينك وبينه قرابة»

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r2.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r2.claim: Qatāda and Mujāhid say this is your neighbor who is your relative.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، وابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] قال: «جارك هو ذو قرابتك»

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r3.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r3.claim: ʿIkrima and Mujāhid gloss the phrase as kinship.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة , ومجاهد، في قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] قالا: القرابة

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says this is a neighbor related to you.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] قال: «جارك الذي بينك وبينه قرابة»

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r5.claim: Qatāda says a neighbor who is also kin has two rights: kinship and neighborliness.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] إذا كان له جار له رحم، فله حقان اثنان: حق القرابة، وحق الجار

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise identifies the near-kinsman neighbor as your relative.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] قال: " الجار ذو القربى: ذو قرابتك "

TAB-FULL:v7p7/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r7.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r7.claim: Maimūn ibn Mihrān instead takes it to mean a man who invokes the neighborly bond of one of your relatives.
TAB-FULL:v7p7/r7.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران، في قوله: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] قال: «الرجل يتوسل إليك بجوار ذي قرابتك»

TAB-FULL:v7p8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects Maimūn's reading: with the definite article, dhi al-qurbā describes the neighbor; an intended possessive meaning would require wa-jāri dhi al-qurbā.
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r1.anchor: وأما والجار بالألف واللام فغير جائز أن يكون {ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] إلا من صفة الجار

TAB-FULL:v7p8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r2.speaker: نوف الشامي
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r2.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī says the near neighbor is a Muslim, understood as near through Islam.
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r2.anchor: عن نوف الشامي: {والجار ذي القربى} [النساء: 36] المسلم

TAB-FULL:v7p8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the religious-proximity reading: ordinary Arabic uses a person of kinship for a blood relative, so the phrase means kinship rather than nearness in religion.
TAB-FULL:v7p8/r3.anchor: فلان ذو قرابة، إنما يعني به: إنه قريب الرحم منه دون القرب بالدين

TAB-FULL:v7p10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد وابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and Ibn Zayd describe the distant neighbor as one without kinship or close relation to you.
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {والجار الجنب} [النساء: 36] الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة

TAB-FULL:v7p10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومجاهد والضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r2.claim: Other reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, Mujāhid, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk describe this neighbor as a stranger or someone from another people.
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {والجار الجنب} [النساء: 36] الجار الغريب يكون من القوم

TAB-FULL:v7p10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r3.speaker: نوف الشامي
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r3.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī identifies the distant neighbor as a Jew or Christian.
TAB-FULL:v7p10/r3.anchor: عن نوف الشامي، {والجار الجنب} [النساء: 36] قال: «اليهودي والنصراني»

TAB-FULL:v7p11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the distant, unrelated neighbor, whether Muslim, polytheist, Jewish, or Christian, completing the command to care for both near and distant neighbors.
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r1.anchor: لما بينا قبل أن الجار ذي القربى: هو الجار ذو القرابة والرحم، والواجب أن يكون الجار ذو الجنابة الجار البعيد

TAB-FULL:v7p11/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r2.claim: In Arabic janb can mean distant; the same root appears in ijtanaba for distancing oneself, tajannaba for withholding, and junub for being apart from prayer until washing.
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r2.anchor: وبعد فإن الجنب في كلام العرب البعيد

TAB-FULL:v7p11/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r3.speaker: الأعشى من بني قيس
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā's phrase ʿan janāba means from a distance or in estrangement, supporting the lexical sense of janb as distant.
TAB-FULL:v7p11/r3.anchor: أتيت حريثا زائرا عن جنابة … فكان حريث في عطائي جامدا يعني بقوله: عن جنابة: عن بعد وغربة

TAB-FULL:v7p12/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p12/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
TAB-FULL:v7p12/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī identify the companion at one's side as a travel companion; Mujāhid adds that lodging, food, and journey are shared.
TAB-FULL:v7p12/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {والصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] الرفيق في السفر

TAB-FULL:v7p12/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p12/r2.speaker: علي وعبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p12/r2.claim: ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh describe the companion at one's side as a righteous companion.
TAB-FULL:v7p12/r2.anchor: عن علي، وعبد الله، قال: {الصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] الرفيق الصالح

TAB-FULL:v7p14/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also interprets the companion at one's side as a travel companion.
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {والصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] قال: «الرفيق في السفر»

TAB-FULL:v7p14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r2.speaker: علي وعبد الله وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى وإبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r2.claim: ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, and Ibrāhīm identify the companion at one's side as one's wife; Ibn ʿAbbās says it is the person with you at home.
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r2.anchor: عن علي، وعبد الله: {والصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] قالا: هي المرأة

TAB-FULL:v7p14/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the phrase as the person who is with you in your home.
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {والصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] يعني الذي معك في منزلك

TAB-FULL:v7p14/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r4.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the phrase includes someone who stays attached to you and accompanies you.
TAB-FULL:v7p14/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {والصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] الملازم. وقال أيضا: رفيقك الذي يرافقك

TAB-FULL:v7p16/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the companion as someone close beside you who stays with you hoping for benefit.
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد: {والصاحب بالجنب} [النساء: 36] الذي يلصق بك

TAB-FULL:v7p16/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the phrase literally as a companion at one's side, encompassing a travel companion, spouse, or attached dependent; God commands kindness to all because a companion has a right upon the person accompanied.
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r2.anchor: الصاحب إلى الجنب، كما يقال: فلان بجنب فلان وإلى جنبه

TAB-FULL:v7p16/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r3.speaker: رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet gave his companion the straight branch and took the crooked one, explaining that every companion is accountable for the companionship, even for an hour of a day.
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r3.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان معه رجل من أصحابه وهما على راحلتين

TAB-FULL:v7p16/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r4.speaker: رسول الله عن عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r4.claim: The Prophet says the best companions before God are those best to their companions, and the best neighbors are those best to their neighbors.
TAB-FULL:v7p16/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن خير الأصحاب عند الله تبارك وتعالى خيرهم لصاحبه، وخير الجيران عند الله خيرهم لجاره»

TAB-FULL:v7p18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r1.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والربيع
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r1.claim: Qatāda and Mujāhid define the son of the road as a passing traveler; al-Rabīʿ adds that the traveler qualifies even if originally wealthy.
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، وابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {وابن السبيل} [النساء: 36] هو الذي يمر عليك وهو مسافر

TAB-FULL:v7p18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r2.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the son of the road is a guest; Mujāhid says a guest has rights both while traveling and at home.
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وابن السبيل} [النساء: 36] قال: «الضيف له حق في السفر والحضر»

TAB-FULL:v7p18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the literal wayfarer: when traveling lawfully, a needy stranded traveler should be helped, hosted, and transported as needed.
TAB-FULL:v7p18/r3.anchor: أن ابن السبيل: هو صاحب الطريق , والسبيل: هو الطريق، وابنه: صاحبه الضارب فيه

TAB-FULL:v7p19/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r1.claim: The phrase means those whom you own as slaves; ownership is attributed to the hands because they are under one's control and are fed, clothed, and directed through one's hands.
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r1.anchor: فكذلك قوله: {وما ملكت أيمانكم} [النساء: 36] لأن مماليك أحدنا تحت يده

TAB-FULL:v7p19/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r2.claim: Expressions such as your mouth spoke, your foot walked, and your hand struck attribute a person's action to the body part customarily used; the ownership phrase works similarly.
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r2.anchor: لأنه بذلك يكون في المتعارف في الناس دون سائر جوارح الجسد

TAB-FULL:v7p19/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r3.claim: Mujāhid says slaves are among what God has bestowed and that God commanded kindness toward all the listed groups.
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وما ملكت أيمانكم} [النساء: 36] مما خولك الله , كل هذا أوصى الله به

TAB-FULL:v7p19/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says God commanded benevolence to all those groups and that people must preserve God's and His Messenger's instructions concerning them.
TAB-FULL:v7p19/r4.anchor: فأوصى ربنا جل جلاله بجميع هؤلاء عباده إحسانا إليهم، وأمر خلقه بالمحافظة على وصيته فيهم

TAB-FULL:v7p21/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r1.claim: Mukhtāl means haughty or vainglorious and derives from khāla, with forms yakhūlu, khawlan, and khālan; the cited verses use khāl and al-khāl in this word family.
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r1.anchor: وللمختال المفتعل من قولك: خال الرجل فهو يخول خولا وخالا، ومنه قول الشاعر

TAB-FULL:v7p21/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r2.speaker: العجاج
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r2.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's line calls al-khāl a garment of fools, as lexical evidence for the cited word family.

TAB-FULL:v7p21/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r3.claim: A boaster flaunts God's blessings and bounty over His servants without gratitude, becoming arrogant and self-exalting over others.
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r3.anchor: فهو المفتخر على عباد الله بما أنعم الله عليه من آلائه , وبسط له من فضله، ولا يحمد على ما آتاه

TAB-FULL:v7p21/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as arrogant and boastful: such a person counts what he has received but does not thank God.
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r4.anchor: قال: " متكبرا فخورا قال: يعد ما أعطي، وهو لا يشكر الله

TAB-FULL:v7p21/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن واقد أبو رجاء الهروي
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r5.claim: Abū Rajāʾ al-Harawī says bad treatment of slaves accompanies arrogance and boasting, while disobedience to parents accompanies tyranny and wretchedness, citing Maryam 19:32.
TAB-FULL:v7p21/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن واقد أبي رجاء الهروي، قال: لا تجد سيئ الملكة إلا وجدته مختالا فخورا

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r1.claim: True servanthood means cutting away attachments and partners associated with shirk.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان رحمه الله : حقيقة العبودية قطع العلائق والشركاء عن الشرك

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r2.claim: The first thing to which one turns for help in distress is one's object of worship.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : إذا أحزنك أمر فأول خاطر تستغيث به فهو معبودك

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r3.claim: Shirk includes seeing one's own fault and stumble as one's own, then blaming oneself for it.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r3.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : الشرك رؤية التقصير والعثرة من نفسه والملامة عليها

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r4.claim: Shirk is turning one's gaze to another besides God or seeing any other as a source of harm or benefit.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : الشرك أن تطالع غيره أو ترى من سواه ضرا ونفعا

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r5.claim: Complete worship rests on six stations: reverence, modesty, fear, weeping, love, and awe.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم رحمه الله : العبادة أصلها ستة : التعظيم والحياء والخوف والبكاء والمحبة ، والهيبة

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r6.speaker: الطيب البصري
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r6.claim: Servanthood is not pure unless its fulfillment is placed within the majesty of lordship.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r6.anchor: وقال الطيب البصري رحمه الله : من لم يدرج وفاء العبودية في عز الربوبية ، لم تصف له العبودية

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r7.claim: Servanthood is shedding lordly claims, a jewel through which lordship appears without cause.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم رحمه الله : العبودية خلع الربوبية وهي جوهرة تظهر الربوبية من غير علة

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r8.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r8.claim: God first tendered and then subdued people so that tenderness would teach their need for servanthood and subjection would reveal the honor of lordship.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r8.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله : دللهم ثم ذللهم ليعرفوا بالدل فاقة العبودية ، وبالذل عز الربوبية

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r9.claim: Servanthood means relinquishing choice and abiding in abasement and need.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : العبودية ترك الإختيار وملازمة الذل والإفتقار

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r10.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r10.claim: Servanthood entails leaving choice, keeping covenants and limits, accepting what is present, and bearing what is lost.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r10.anchor: وقال أيضا : العبودية ترك الإختيار وهي جامعة لأربع خصال : الوفاء بالعهود والحفظ للحدود

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r11.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r11.claim: Servanthood is relinquishing one's will; whoever leaves the claim of servanthood is treated like a runaway slave.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r11.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : العبودية ترك المشيئة ومن خرج من قال بالعبودية صنع به ما يصنع بالآبق

SULAMI:v1p146#2/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r12.claim: Six qualities structure servanthood: reverence with sincerity, modesty with an unsettled heart, love with longing, fear that leaves sins, hope that follows the Prophet, and awe that relinquishes choice.
SULAMI:v1p146#2/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم رحمه الله : العبودية بناؤها على ستة خصال : التعظيم وعنده الإخلاص

SULAMI:v1p147/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p147/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p147/r1.claim: Sahl reads the near neighbor as the heart, the distant neighbor as the self, the companion by one's side as the intellect shaped by Sunna and law, and the traveler as obedient bodily limbs.
SULAMI:v1p147/r1.anchor: قال سهل رحمه الله : الجار ذي القربى هو القلب ، والجار الجنب هي النفس ، والصاحب بالجنب وهو العقل

TABATABAI:4:36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r1.claim: These seven verses urge kindness and spending for God, promise a beautiful reward, and condemn withholding or spending for show.
TABATABAI:4:36/r1.anchor: آيات سبع فيها حث على الإحسان والإنفاق في سبيل الله ووعد جميل عليه وذم على تركه

TABATABAI:4:36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r2.claim: Worship and nonassociation here mean practical monotheism: doing good deeds, including kindness, to please God and seek the afterlife reward.
TABATABAI:4:36/r2.anchor: هذا هو التوحيد غير أن المراد به التوحيد العملي وهو إتيان الأعمال الحسنة

TABATABAI:4:36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r3.claim: The following condemnation of stingy and showy spenders, and the question about believing and spending, show that practical association is failure to believe truly in God and the Last Day.
TABATABAI:4:36/r3.anchor: وعلله بقوله { إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا فخورا } وذكر أنه البخيل بماله

TABATABAI:4:36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r4.claim: Ṣād 38:26 says following desire diverts from God's path and leads to punishment through forgetting the reckoning; every association is misguidance.
TABATABAI:4:36/r4.anchor: إن الذين يضلون عن سبيل الله لهم عذاب شديد بما نسوا يوم الحساب

TABATABAI:4:36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r5.claim: He cites al-Jāthiya 45:23: taking desire as one's god is worship of desire and association with it.
TABATABAI:4:36/r5.anchor: فبين أن اتباع الهوى عبادة له وشرك به

TABATABAI:4:36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r6.claim: Practical monotheism means working for God's reward while mindful of Judgment; practical association means forgetting the afterlife and acting for desire, wealth, or people's praise.
TABATABAI:4:36/r6.anchor: أن يعمل الإنسان ابتغاء مثوبة الله وهو على ذكر من يوم الحساب

TABATABAI:4:36/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r7.claim: Sincere worship seeks God's approval and reward rather than following desire.
TABATABAI:4:36/r7.anchor: فالمراد بعبادة الله والإخلاص له فيها أن يكون طلبا لمرضاته وابتغاء لمثوبته لا لاتباع الهوى

TABATABAI:4:36/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r8.claim: Iḥsānan is an absolute object for an implied command, as if the text said to do good to parents.
TABATABAI:4:36/r8.anchor: قوله إحسانا مفعول مطلق لفعل مقدر تقديره وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا

TABATABAI:4:36/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r9.claim: The verb aḥsana takes both bi and ilā, as in the usages aḥsantu bihi and aḥsantu ilayhi.
TABATABAI:4:36/r9.anchor: والإحسان يتعدى بالباء وإلى معا يقال أحسنت به وأحسنت إليه

TABATABAI:4:36/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r10.claim: The kin group and the following categories are coordinated with the parents; dhū al-qurbā means relatives.
TABATABAI:4:36/r10.anchor: وقوله { وبذي القربى } هو وما بعده معطوف على الوالدين وذو القربى القرابة

TABATABAI:4:36/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r11.claim: The contrast in the neighbor descriptions indicates a nearby neighbor by residence and a distant, nonrelative neighbor.
TABATABAI:4:36/r11.anchor: قرينة المقابلة في الوصف تعطي أن يكون المراد بالجار ذي القربى الجار القريب دارا

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r1.claim: The preceding segment attributes this neighbor-distance report to the Prophet: one version says forty cubits, another forty houses; no grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r1.anchor:
تحديد الجوار بأربعين ذراعا "
وفي رواية أربعون دارا

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r2.claim: He suggests the two reported ranges may correspond respectively to the nearby and distant neighbors.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r2.anchor: ولعل الروايتين ناظرتان إلى الجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r3.claim: The companion at one's side is anyone who stays alongside, including a travel companion or someone accompanying one at home.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r3.anchor: هو الذي يصاحبك ملازما لجنبك وهو بمفهومه يعم مصاحب السفر من رفقة الطريق ومصاحب الحضر

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r4.claim: Ibn al-sabīl is someone known only as a traveler, as though the road were his sole affiliation; poverty or lack of provisions is not built into the phrase.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r4.anchor: هو الذي لا يعرف من حاله إلا أنه سالك سبيل كأنه ليس له من ينتسب إليه إلا السبيل

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r5.claim: The phrase refers to male and female slaves, as the context lists people to be treated well and the Qur'an commonly uses this expression for them.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r5.anchor: المراد به العبيد والإماء بقرينة عده في عداد من يحسن إليهم

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r6.claim: Mukhtāl is a strutting, self-deluded person, related to the prancing horse called khayl; fakhūr means one who boasts much.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r6.anchor: المختال التائه المتبختر المسخر لخياله ومنه الخيل للفرس لأنه يتبختر في مشيته والفخور كثير الفخر

TABATABAI:4:36-40/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r7.claim: Arrogance and boasting follow attachment to wealth and status; God dislikes hearts attached to anything besides Him, as shown by the two groups described next.
TABATABAI:4:36-40/r7.anchor: من لوازم التعلق بالمال والجاه والإفراط في حبهما ولذلك لم يكن الله ليحب المختال الفخور

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r1.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits through Salām al-Juʿfī and Abān ibn Taghlib from al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq that the verse was revealed concerning the Prophet and Ali; another report via Ibn Jabala is similar. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r1.anchor: عن سلام الجعفي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام وأبان بن تغلب عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام نزلت في رسول الله

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet calls himself and Ali the two fathers of this community; al-ʿAyyāshī, al-Baḥrānī citing al-Fāʾiq, and Ibn Shahrāshūb also transmit the inward interpretation. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r2.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنا وعلى أبوا هذه الأمة

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r3.claim: In the inner sense, a teacher who raises a person's soul toward perfection is a father; the Prophet and Imam are truer fathers to guided believers than bodily parents, so parental injunctions inwardly include them while outwardly retaining their bodily sense.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r3.anchor: فمعلم الإنسان ومربيه للكمال أبوه فمثل النبي والولي عليهما أفضل الصلاة أحق أن يكون أبا للمؤمن المهتدي به

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r4.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī reports from Abu Ṣāliḥ from Abu al-ʿAbbās that the neighbor described as distant is one with no kinship to you; the wording could refer to both neighbor categories. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح عن أبي العباس في قول الله { والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب } قال الذي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r5.claim: The same report glosses the companion at one's side as a travel companion; the author treats this as one example, not an exclusive referent. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r5.anchor: وقوله { الصاحب في السفر } لعله من قبيل ذكر بعض المصاديق

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r9.claim: Reports from the Prophet and his family on kindness to parents, relatives, orphans, and the other listed groups are too numerous and familiar to reproduce; their specific contexts are better treated elsewhere.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r9.anchor: فوق حد الإحصاء على معروفيتها وشهرتها وهو الموجب للإغماض عن إيرادها ها هنا

TUSTARI:4:36/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:4:36/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:4:36/r1.claim: Outwardly, the distant neighbor is a foreigner or stranger.
TUSTARI:4:36/r1.anchor: أما ظاهرها فالجار الجنب: البعيد الأجنبي

TUSTARI:4:36/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:4:36/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:4:36/r2.claim: Outwardly, the companion by one's side is a travel companion.
TUSTARI:4:36/r2.anchor: والصاحب بالجنب: هو الرفيق في السفر

TUSTARI:4:36/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:4:36/r3.speaker: قيل
TUSTARI:4:36/r3.claim: An alternate reported outward interpretation identifies the companion by one's side as one's wife.

TUSTARI:4:36/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:4:36/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:4:36/r4.claim: Outwardly, the wayfarer is a guest.
TUSTARI:4:36/r4.anchor: وقد قيل الزوجة، وابن السبيل: الضيف، أما باطنها

TUSTARI:4:36/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:4:36/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:4:36/r5.claim: Inwardly, the near neighbor is the heart, the distant neighbor the natural self, the companion reason following sacred law, and the wayfarer the limbs obedient to God.
TUSTARI:4:36/r5.anchor: أما باطنها فالجار ذو القربى هو القلب، والجار الجنب هو الطبيعة

AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r1.claim: Some gloss الجنب as الجنب meaning the side or direction; a rajaz line uses it this way, for the neighbor detached from kinship; جانب is another form.
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم {الجنب} وقال الراجز: [وهو الشاهد الخامس والسبعون بعد المئة]

AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r2.claim: The distant neighbor is one separated from kinship, and الجنب can also mean someone alongside or apart.
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r2.anchor: وهذا هو المتنحى عن القرابة فلذلك قال "جنب" و"الجنب" أيضا: المجانب للقرابة

AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p256#2/r3.claim: الصاحب بالجنب means the companion at your side, as in saying someone is beside or next to you.

TABRISI:4:36/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r1.claim: Neighbor is linked to deviation: one turns toward and lives beside another; seeking God’s protection asks Him to turn one away from the Fire.
TABRISI:4:36/r1.anchor: الجار أصله من العدول. يقال: جاوره يجاوره مجاورة وجوار

TABRISI:4:36/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r2.claim: The near neighbor is a relative, and the distant neighbor is a stranger.
TABRISI:4:36/r2.anchor: { والجار ذي القربى } القريب، { والجار الجنب } الغريب.

TABRISI:4:36/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:4:36/r3.claim: Abu Ali parses جنب as an adjective on the faʿl pattern; it means far from one’s family, as shown by contrast with the near neighbor.
TABRISI:4:36/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الجنب صفة على فعل مثل ناقة أجدو مشي سجح

TABRISI:4:36/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r4.claim: Qurba derives from nearness just as yusra derives from ease.
TABRISI:4:36/r4.anchor: والقربى: من القرب كاليسرى من اليسر

TABRISI:4:36/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r5.claim: Mukhtal comes from imagining: the person’s bearing makes him seem boastfully exuberant; horses are called khayl because they prance, and khawal are attendants.
TABRISI:4:36/r5.anchor: وأصل المختال من التخيل وهو التصور لأنه يتخيل بحاله مرح البطر

TABRISI:4:36/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r6.claim: A boastful person counts achievements out of pride; someone who recounts them in recognition of blessing is thankful, not boastful.
TABRISI:4:36/r6.anchor: والفخور الذي يعد مناقبه كبرا أو تطاولا، وأما الذي يعددها اعترافا بالنعمة

TABRISI:4:36/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r7.claim: Ihsanan is a cognate accusative with an implied do good, or an object of an implied enjoin goodness.
TABRISI:4:36/r7.anchor: إحسانا نصب على المصدر كما تقول ضربا لزيد وتقديره احسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا

TABRISI:4:36/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r8.claim: After commands about orphans, spouses, and dependents, the verse adds conduct gathering core principles and good deeds, beginning with worship of God.
TABRISI:4:36/r8.anchor: لما أمر سبحانه بمكارم الأخلاق في أمر اليتامى والأزواج والعيال

TABRISI:4:36/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r9.claim: Worship means affirming God’s oneness and magnifying Him; only God merits worship because only He bestows the foundational blessings.
TABRISI:4:36/r9.anchor: أي وحدوه وعظموه ولا تشركوا في عبادته غيره فإن العبادة لا تجوز لغيره

TABRISI:4:36/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r10.claim: Treat both parents with goodness, beneficence, kindness, and honor; a view supplies an implicit God enjoined you.
TABRISI:4:36/r10.anchor: أي فاستوصوا بهما برا وإنعاما وإحسانا وإكراما. وقيل: إن فيه إضمار فعل

TABRISI:4:36/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r11.claim: Show goodness to relatives generally, protect and manage orphans’ property, and provide the poor with needed food, clothing, and necessities.
TABRISI:4:36/r11.anchor: معناه احسنوا بالوالدين خاصة وبالقرابات عامة. يقال: أحسنت إليه وأحسنت به

TABRISI:4:36/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن زيد
TABRISI:4:36/r12.claim: One view is a neighbor related by blood and a foreign neighbor with no kinship.
TABRISI:4:36/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن زيد وقيل المراد به الجار ذي القربى

TABRISI:4:36/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36/r13.claim: Another view is a neighbor near through Islam and a polytheist neighbor distant in religion.
TABRISI:4:36/r13.anchor: وقيل المراد به الجار ذي القربى منك بالإسلام، والجار الجنب المشرك البعيد في الدين

TABRISI:4:36/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:4:36/r14.claim: A Prophetic report divides neighbors into one with three rights of neighborhood, kinship, and Islam; one with neighborhood and Islam; and a scriptural polytheist with the right of neighborhood.
TABRISI:4:36/r14.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:4:36#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:4:36#2/r1.claim: The Prophet divides neighbors into one with three rights of neighborhood, kinship, and Islam; one with neighborhood and Islam; and a scriptural polytheist with the right of neighborhood.
TABRISI:4:36#2/r1.anchor: الجيران ثلاثة: جار له ثلاثة حقوق، حق الجوار، وحق القرابة

TABRISI:4:36#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:4:36#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines the near neighbor as someone who comes close to you and whom you know, and who comes close to and knows you.
TABRISI:4:36#2/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: { والجار ذي القربى } الذي يقاربك وتقاربه

TABRISI:4:36#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:4:36#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines the distant neighbor simply as one far away.

TABRISI:4:36#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#2/r4.claim: A report sets the limit of neighborhood at forty houses; another version says forty cubits.
TABRISI:4:36#2/r4.anchor: وروي أن حد الجوار إلى أربعين دارا، ويروى إلى أربعين ذراعا

TABRISI:4:36#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#2/r5.claim: Although kin were already mentioned, a nearby relative who is also a neighbor has both kinship and neighborly rights, unlike a relative who is not a neighbor.
TABRISI:4:36#2/r5.anchor: لأن الجار إذا كان قريبا فله حق القرابة والجوار

TABRISI:4:36#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:4:36#3/r1.claim: One view takes the companion as a travel companion, owed support and good fellowship.
TABRISI:4:36#3/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه الرفيق في السفر عن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وجماعة

TABRISI:4:36#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى والنخعي
TABRISI:4:36#3/r2.claim: A second view takes the companion as one’s wife.
TABRISI:4:36#3/r2.anchor: وثانيها: أنه الزوجة عن عبد الله بن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى، والنخعي

TABRISI:4:36#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
TABRISI:4:36#3/r3.claim: A third view takes the companion as someone attached to you hoping for a benefit.
TABRISI:4:36#3/r3.anchor: وثالثها: أنه المنقطع إليك يرجو نفعك عن ابن عباس في إحدى الروايتين، وابن زيد

TABRISI:4:36#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#3/r4.claim: A fourth view identifies a servant; al-Tabrisi prefers including all four interpretations.
TABRISI:4:36#3/r4.anchor: ورابعها: أنه الخادم الذي يخدمك، والأولى حمله على الجميع

TABRISI:4:36#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد والربيع
TABRISI:4:36#3/r5.claim: One view identifies the person of the road as a traveler.
TABRISI:4:36#3/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنه المسافر عن مجاهد والربيع

TABRISI:4:36#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:4:36#3/r6.claim: Another view identifies the person as a guest; Ibn Abbas says hospitality is for three days and further hosting is kindness.
TABRISI:4:36#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو الضيف عن ابن عباس. قال: والضيافة ثلاثة أيام وما فوقها فهو معروف

TABRISI:4:36#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#3/r7.speaker: جابر
TABRISI:4:36#3/r7.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet’s teaching that every good deed is charity, including a cheerful greeting and sharing water from one’s bucket.

TABRISI:4:36#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#4/r1.claim: The phrase refers to male and female slaves; mentioning the right hand emphasizes ownership, as in saying one’s foot walked or hand struck.
TABRISI:4:36#4/r1.anchor: يعني به المماليك من العبيد والإماء وذكر اليمين تأكيدا كما يقال

TABRISI:4:36#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#4/r2.claim: Ma is genitive by coordination with the preceding items, making this part of the command to treat those under one’s ownership well.
TABRISI:4:36#4/r2.anchor: ما ملكت أيمانكم جر بالعطف على ما تقدم، أي: وأحسنوا إلى عبيدكم

TABRISI:4:36#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#4/r3.claim: Good treatment includes maintenance and housing and not imposing work beyond their ability.
TABRISI:4:36#4/r3.anchor: بالنفقة والسكنى ولا تحملوهم من الأعمال ما لا يطيقونه

TABRISI:4:36#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#4/r4.claim: God’s not loving someone means He does not approve of that person.
TABRISI:4:36#4/r4.anchor: أي لا يرتضي { من كان مختالا } في مشيته { فخورا }

TABRISI:4:36#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:4:36#4/r5.claim: The conceited person struts and the boastful person is proud of wealth; such people disdain poor relatives and neighbors.
TABRISI:4:36#4/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس وإنما ذكرهما لأنهما يأنفان من أقاربهم وجيرانهم إذا كانوا فقراء

TABRISI:4:36#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:36#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:36#4/r6.claim: The verse gathers Islam’s pillars and good character; reflection can replace many sermons and guide one to extensive scholarly knowledge.
TABRISI:4:36#4/r6.anchor: تضمنت بيان أركان الإسلام، والتنبيه على مكارم الأخلاق

FARRA:v1p265/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p265/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p265/r11.claim: The command requires kindness to parents, as in the parallel command in 17:23.
FARRA:v1p265/r11.anchor: أمرهم بالإحسان إلى الوالدين. ومثله وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا

FARRA:v1p265/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p265/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p265/r12.claim: إحسانا is accusative with an understood verb; raising it with the preposition bi would also be valid if the verb were left unexpressed.
FARRA:v1p265/r12.anchor: كان صوابا كما- تقول في الكلام: أحسن

THALABI:v3p304/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r1.speaker: العامة وابن أبي عبلة
THALABI:v3p304/r1.claim: The common reading puts the near kin-neighbor in the genitive, coordinated with what precedes; Ibn Abi Abla reads the neighbor and what follows in the accusative.
THALABI:v3p304/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بالخفض عطفا على الكلام الأول، وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: والجار وما يليه نصبا.

THALABI:v3p304/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p304/r2.claim: Al-jar dhi al-qurba is a neighbor related by kinship; al-jar al-junub is the distant neighbor, described here as one connected by kinship.
THALABI:v3p304/r2.anchor: والجار ذي القربى ذو القرابة والجار الجنب البعيد الذي بينك وبينه قرابة

THALABI:v3p304/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r3.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v3p304/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies al-jar al-junub as a stranger from another people.
THALABI:v3p304/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو الغريب من قوم آخرين، وقرأ الأعمش والفضل

THALABI:v3p304/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r4.speaker: الأعمش والفضل
THALABI:v3p304/r4.claim: Al-A'mash and al-Fadl read al-junub with an open jim and still n, noting several Arabic forms for a non-relative or stranger.
THALABI:v3p304/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والفضل: (والجار الجنب) بفتح الجيم وسكون النون، وهما لغتان: رجل جنب وجنب

THALABI:v3p304/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r5.speaker: الأعشى
THALABI:v3p304/r5.claim: Al-A'sha's poem uses janaba to mean foreignness without kinship, supporting the sense of a stranger in al-jar al-junub.
THALABI:v3p304/r5.anchor: وقال الاعشى: أتيت حريثا زائرا عن جنابة … فكان حريث في عطائي جامدا

THALABI:v3p304/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p304/r6.claim: The root denotes distance: one avoids someone by keeping away, and a ritually impure person is called junub because he abstains from prayer and the mosque until washing.
THALABI:v3p304/r6.anchor: ومنه يقال: اجتنب فلان فلانا، إذا بعد منه، ومنه قيل للمجنب: جنب لاعتزاله الصلاة

THALABI:v3p304/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r7.speaker: نوف البكالي
THALABI:v3p304/r7.claim: Nawf al-Bikali identifies the al-jar al-junub as a non-Muslim neighbor.
THALABI:v3p304/r7.anchor: وقال نوف البكالي: الجار الجنب هو الكافر، والصاحب بالجنب يعني الرفيق في السفر

THALABI:v3p304/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وعكرمة وقتادة
THALABI:v3p304/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Ja'far, Ikrima, and Qatada identify the companion by one's side as a travel companion.
THALABI:v3p304/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وعكرمة وقتادة، عن سعيد بن معروف بن رافع، عن أبيه، عن جده قال

THALABI:v3p304/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r9.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p304/r9.claim: The Prophet advises choosing the neighbor before the home and the travel companion before setting out.
THALABI:v3p304/r9.anchor: عن جده قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «التمسوا الجار قبل الدار، والرفيق قبل الطريق»

THALABI:v3p304/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r10.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v3p304/r10.claim: Some say al-jar al-junub is the adjacent neighbor whose house is next to yours.
THALABI:v3p304/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الجار الجنب هو الجار اللاصق داره بدارك، فهو إلى جنبك

THALABI:v3p304/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r11.speaker: علي وعبد الله وابن أبي ليلى والنخعي
THALABI:v3p304/r11.claim: Ali, Abd Allah, Ibn Abi Layla, and al-Nakha'i identify the companion by one's side as one's wife.
THALABI:v3p304/r11.anchor: وقال علي وعبد الله وابن أبي ليلى والنخعي: هو المرأة تكون معه إلى جنبه.

THALABI:v3p304/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r12.speaker: ابن زيد وابن جريج
THALABI:v3p304/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jurayj say it is someone who stays with a person hoping for his generosity and support.
THALABI:v3p304/r12.anchor: ابن زيد وابن جريح: هو الذي يلزمك ويصحبك رجاء برك ورفدك.

THALABI:v3p304/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p304/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is ashamed if someone visits his home three times without seeing a sign of his kindness.
THALABI:v3p304/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إني لأستحي أن يطأ الرجل بساطي ثلاث مرات لا يرى عليه أثر من بري.

THALABI:v3p304/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r14.speaker: المهلب
THALABI:v3p304/r14.claim: Al-Muhallab says a person who comes and goes to one's home is already a sufficient reminder of his need.
THALABI:v3p304/r14.anchor: وقال المهلب: إذا غدا عليكم الرجل وراح، فكفى به مسألة وتذكرة بنفسه.

THALABI:v3p304/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r15.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p304/r15.claim: The Prophet says the best companion and neighbor in God's sight is the one who treats his companion or neighbor best.
THALABI:v3p304/r15.anchor: وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن خير الأصحاب عند الله عز وجل خيرهم لصاحبه، خير الجيران عند الله خيرهم لجاره»

THALABI:v3p304/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p304/r16.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p304/r16.claim: The Prophet says faith is incomplete if a neighbor fears one's harm, then lists neighborly duties: answer invitations, aid and lend, share joy, visit illness, console loss, attend funerals, avoid blocking air or causing offense, and share fruit.
THALABI:v3p304/r16.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ليس بمؤمن من لا يؤمن جاره بوائقه، فأيما رجل أغلق أبوابه دون جاره

THALABI:v3p305/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p305/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p305/r1.claim: The Prophet assigns three rights to a Muslim relative-neighbor, two to a Muslim neighbor, and the right of neighborliness to a polytheist neighbor.
THALABI:v3p305/r1.anchor: ثم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الجيران ثلاثة: فمنهم من له ثلاثة حقوق، ومنهم من له حقان

THALABI:v3p305/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p305/r2.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p305/r2.claim: The Prophet says harming a neighbor harms him and God, while warring against a neighbor is warring against him and God.
THALABI:v3p305/r2.anchor: أبو هشام القطان، عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من آذى جاره فقد آذاني، ومن آذاني فقد آذى الله

THALABI:v3p305/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p305/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p305/r3.claim: The phrase about those whom your right hands possess refers to enslaved people.
THALABI:v3p305/r3.anchor: وابن السبيل وما ملكت أيمانكم يعني المماليك

THALABI:v3p305/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p305/r4.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p305/r4.claim: The Prophet tells Abu Dharr to feed and clothe an enslaved boy as he does himself; after Abu Dharr shares his only garment, the Prophet advises him to free the boy, and Abu Dharr does so.
THALABI:v3p305/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دفع إلى أبي ذر غلاما، فقال: «يا أبا ذر أطعمه مما تأكل واكسه مما تلبس»

THALABI:v3p305/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p305/r5.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v3p305/r5.claim: The Prophet describes sheep as blessing, camels as honor, and horses as carrying good, then says an enslaved person is one's brother and should be helped when unable.
THALABI:v3p305/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الغنم بركة، والإبل عز لأهلها، والخيل معقود في نواصيها الخير

THALABI:v3p305/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p305/r6.speaker: علي
THALABI:v3p305/r6.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet's last words concerned prayer and fearing God regarding those under one's authority.
THALABI:v3p305/r6.anchor: وعن علي (رضي الله عنه) قال: «كان آخر كلام رسول إله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة واتقوا الله فيما ملكت أيمانكم»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the command as God enjoining both worship of Him and kindness to parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى: أوصاكم الله بعبادته، وأوصاكم بالوالدين إحسانا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ expands the wording as an imperative: “and treat parents kindly.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا. أمرهم بالإحسان (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas describes filial kindness as gentle treatment: humble one's voice and gaze, answer softly, and stand before parents in loving humility like a servant before a harsh master, as in 17:24.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد البر بهما مع اللطف ولين الجانب، ولا يغلظ لهما الجواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r4.claim: Qurbā is a verbal noun like qarāba, as bushrā and rujʿā are verbal nouns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r4.anchor: القربى مصدر كالقرابة (¬1)، ومثله البشرى والرجعى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says to maintain relations with and show affection to one's relatives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يصله ويعطف عليه (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God commands kindness to relatives after parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p501#2/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أمر الله: عز وجل بالإحسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says to treat orphans gently, draw them close, and stroke their heads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يرفق بهم ويدنيهم ويمسح رأسهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recommends giving the poor what one can readily spare or returning them a kind response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r2.anchor: يريد: بذل يسر، أو رد جميل (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r3.speaker: عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r3.claim: Most exegetes identify the near neighbor as a neighbor related by blood, who is owed kinship, neighborly, and Islamic rights.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r3.anchor: قال عامة المفسرين: يعني القريب في النسب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes nearness to mean a nearby home and familiarity; the nearby neighbor knows you, unlike the distant stranger mentioned next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r4.anchor: ودل كلام الزجاج على أنه أراد بالقربى ههنا قرب الدار والمعرفة والاختلاط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r5.claim: The author prefers the majority's kinship interpretation; he also notes that the contrast with the distant neighbor supports a proximity reading of al-jār dhī al-qurbā.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r6.claim: Junub is an adjective on the fuʿl pattern, like aḥad in nāqa aḥad, ghalq, and fatḥ; it derives from janāba, the opposite of closeness, and means distance. ʿAlqama and al-Aʿshā use janāba in this sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r6.anchor: فلا تحرمني نائلا عن جنابة ... فإني امرؤ وسط القباب غريب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r7.claim: The root denotes removal and distancing; the author links it to Abraham's prayer that God keep him and his sons far from worshipping idols in 14:35.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r7.anchor: وأصل الجنب التنحية والإبعاد، ومنه قوله: {واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام} [إبراهيم: 35].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r8.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r8.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal reports from ʿĀṣim a reading with fatḥ on jīm and sukūn on nūn; it can mean a neighbor from a distant side with the genitive noun omitted, or simply a distant stranger as an adjective.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r8.anchor: وروى المفضل عن عاصم (¬5): {والجار الجنب} بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r9.claim: On the first reading, junub may mean “side,” with “possessor of a side” understood because a neighbor cannot itself be a side; alternatively it is an adjective like ḍarb, nadb, and fisal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r9.anchor: أحدهما: أن يريد بالجنب الناحية، ويكون المعنى على هذا: ذي الجنب، فحذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r10.claim: A further cited line calls a stranger “a man junub” and pluralizes the adjective as ajnūb; junub is based on being removed and far away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r10.anchor: ورجل جنب، إذا كان غريبا متباعدا عن أهله. وقوم أجناب، ورجل أجنب وأجنبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r11.claim: An anonymous poet describes noble people approached from afar as lenient to a neighboring guest, illustrating junāba as distance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p502/r11.anchor: وقال آخر: كرام إذا ما جئتهم عن جنابة ... أعفاء عن جار الخليط المجاور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والحسن والسدي والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak identify the companion at one's side as a travel companion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والحسن والسدي والضحاك: هو الرفيق في السفر (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r2.claim: ʿAtaʾ, quoting Ibn Abbas, says the travel companion beside you has both the right of neighborliness and the right of companionship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد صاحبك في السفر، وهو جارك إلى جانبك، فله حق الجوار وحق الصحبة (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ, al-Zajjaj, and Ibn Qutayba choose the travel-companion interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r3.anchor: وهذا اختيار الفراء (¬5) والزجاج (¬6) وابن قتيبة (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r4.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى وإبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r4.claim: Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Abi Layla, and Ibrahim identify the companion at one's side as one's wife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r4.anchor: وقال علي وابن مسعود وابن أبي ليلى (¬8) وإبراهيم: هو زوجتك تكون معك إلى جنبك (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r5.speaker: ابن جريج وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd understand it as someone who stays close to you hoping for your help and benefit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وابن زيد: هو الذي يلزمك ويصحبك رجاء خيرك ونفعك (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r6.claim: The son of the road is a guest, whom one must host until he reaches his intended destination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r6.anchor: {وابن السبيل}. هو الضيف، يجب قراه إلى أن يبلغ حيث يريد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والربيع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Rabiʿ identify him as a passing traveler, whom one should give water and food until he leaves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والربيع: يريد عابر السبيل، ترويه وتطعمه حتى يرحل عنك (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r8.claim: The phrase refers to enslaved people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says to feed an enslaved person well, bear mistakes, and forgive; if temperaments do not fit, sell him so he may suit another owner and you avoid wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد المملوك، تحسن رزقه وتحتمل مساوئه وتعفو عنه فيما يخطئ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r10.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r10.claim: Umar reports the Prophet's instruction to sell a servant whose disposition does not suit the owner, keep looking until finding a match, and not torment God's servants because people have different temperaments.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p506/r10.anchor: وروى عمر بن الخطاب أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "من ابتاع شيئا من الخدم فلم يوافق شيمته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r1.claim: Mukhtāl means a person possessed by conceit and arrogance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the conceited person as self-important and failing to fulfill God's rights.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد بالمختال العظيم في نفسه، الذي لا يقوم بحقوق الله (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that conceit is mentioned because an arrogant person disdains poor relatives and neighbors and therefore treats them badly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: وإنما ذكر الاختيال ههنا، لأن المختال يأنف من ذوي قراباته إذا كانوا فقراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r4.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier discussion of the derivation of khaylāʾ at 3:14.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r4.anchor: وذكرنا اشتقاقه في اللغة عند قوله: {والخيل المسومة} [آل عمران: 14].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r5.claim: Fakhr means boasting and overreaching; a fakhūr magnifies his merits out of arrogance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r5.anchor: ومعنى الفخر في اللغة هو البذخ والتطاول، والفخور الذي يعدد مناقبه كبرا وتطاولا (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the boastful person flaunts before God's servants the honor and blessings God has granted him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p507/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو الذي يفخر على عباد الله بما خوله الله من كرامته

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r1.claim: The near neighbor is the neighbor who is a relative.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r2.claim: Al-janb means distant; the neighbor described this way is a stranger.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r3.claim: The companion by one's side is a travel companion.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r4.claim: The son of the road refers to a guest.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r4.anchor:
وابن السبيل} الضيف.
و (المختال) ذو الخيلاء والكبر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p126#3/r5.claim: Mukhtāl is a person characterized by pride and conceit.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r1.claim: Kindness to parents means treating them well with gentleness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r1.anchor: أحسنوا بهما إحسانا، وهو البر مع لين الجانب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r2.claim: A relative is to be visited and treated with affection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r2.anchor: وهو ذو القرابة يصله ويتعطف عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r3.claim: Orphans should be treated gently and brought near.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r4.claim: The poor should receive a modest gift or a kind response.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r4.anchor: ببذل يسير، أو رد جميل { والجار ذي القربى }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r5.claim: The near relative neighbor has both the right of kinship and the right of neighborhood.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r5.anchor: وهو الذي له مع حق الجوار حق القرابة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r6.claim: The distant neighbor is unrelated to one in lineage.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r6.anchor: البعيد عنك في النسب { والصاحب بالجنب }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r7.claim: The companion by one’s side is a traveling companion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r7.anchor: هو الرفيق في السفر { وابن السبيل }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r8.claim: The wayfarer is a traveler passing along the road.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r8.anchor: عابر الطريق. [وقيل: الضيف] يؤويه ويطعمه حتى يرحل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r9.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r9.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the wayfarer to mean a guest, whom one shelters and feeds until departure.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r10.claim: Those possessed by the right hand are enslaved people.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r11.claim: A mukhtāl is self-important and neglects duties owed to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r11.anchor: عظيما في نفسه لا يقوم بحقوق الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r12.claim: A fakhūr boasts over God’s servants about the blessings God has bestowed on him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:36-37/r12.anchor: على عباده بما خوله الله من نعمته

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r5.claim: After resolving family life, the passage turns to general moral instruction and lays down ten duties.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r5.anchor: aile terbiyesinde umûmî bir ilmihal olarak esas ittihaz edilmesi lâzım gelen ahlâk-ı haseneye geçilerek

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r6.claim: The first duty is to worship God alone and sincerely, associating nothing with Him.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r6.anchor: birincisi, Allah’a ibadet ve ubûdiyet ve O’na hiçbir şey şerîk koşmayıp ihlas ile ibadet etmek

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r7.claim: The second duty is to treat one's mother and father with benevolence.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r7.anchor: ikincisi anaya babaya ihsan ile muâmele etmek

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r8.claim: The third duty is benevolence toward relatives.

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r9.claim: The fourth duty is benevolence toward orphans.

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r10.claim: The fifth duty is benevolence toward the poor.

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r11.claim: The near neighbor is one whose home is nearby or who is a relative.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r11.anchor: yakın komşuya ihsan ki hânesi yakın olur veya akrabadan bulunur

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r12.claim: The distant neighbor may live farther away, be unrelated, or be non-Muslim.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r12.anchor: veya akrabadan olmaz veya gayrimüslim bulunur

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r13.claim: A Prophetic hadith distinguishes neighbors with three rights (neighbor, kinship, Islam), two rights (neighbor, Islam), and one right (neighbor only), including People of the Book and polytheist neighbors.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r13.anchor: üç hakkı vardır; hakk-ı civar, hakk-ı karâbet, hakk-ı İslâm. İkincisinin iki hakkı vardır; hakk-ı civar

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r14.claim: The companion at one's side is a companion in a good activity such as study, business, craft, or travel; the meaning includes spouses.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r14.anchor: musâhabet eden arkadaş ve yoldaş demektir. Bu mefhum zevc ve zevceye dahi şâmil olur

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r15.claim: The wayfarer is an arriving traveler, or more generally a guest.

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r16.claim: Those under one's hand are people in one's custody, such as male and female slaves.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r16.anchor: köle ve cariye gibi[^22] el altında bulunanlara ihsan

ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r17.claim: Muhtal means arrogant; fahur means boastful and vainglorious.
ELMALILI:4:34-40#2/r17.anchor: tefâhur eden demektir ki Allah bunları sevmez, hele o bahil mütekebbirler

MAJAZ:v1p125/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p125/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p125/r6.claim: The phrase is elliptical, as Arabic often is; its full sense is ‘enjoin care of parents with kindness.’
MAJAZ:v1p125/r6.anchor: وبالوالدين إحسانا» (35) : مختصر، تفعل العرب ذلك، فكان فى التمثيل: واستوصوا بالوالدين إحسانا.

MAJAZ:v1p125/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p125/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p125/r7.claim: Al-jār dhū al-qurbā is the close or related neighbor.
MAJAZ:v1p125/r7.anchor: والجار ذي القربى» (35) القريب، «والجار الجنب» (35) الغريب،

MAJAZ:v1p125/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p125/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p125/r8.claim: Al-jār al-junub is a distant or foreign neighbor; the root is ijtināb, and ʿAlqama and al-Aʿshā use janāba for distance.
MAJAZ:v1p125/r8.anchor: ما تأتينا إلا عن جنابة، أي من بعيد، قال علقمة بن عبدة:

MAJAZ:v1p125/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p125/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p125/r9.claim: The companion at one’s side is someone who travels with and stays beside you.
MAJAZ:v1p125/r9.anchor: والصاحب بالجنب» (35) أي: يصاحبك فى سفرك، ويلزمك، فينزل إلى جنبك:

MAJAZ:v1p126/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p126/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p126/r1.claim: Ibn al-sabīl means a stranger or traveler away from home.

MAJAZ:v1p126/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p126/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p126/r2.claim: Mukhtāl is one characterized by pride and conceit; khayāl can also be a verbal noun, as the poems of al-ʿAjjāj and al-ʿAbdī illustrate.
MAJAZ:v1p126/r2.anchor: المختال، ذو الخيلاء والخال، وهما واحد، ويجىء مصدرا، قال العجاج:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r1.claim: These seven verses promote social order through constructive ties, kindness from near to far, material and spiritual help for God's sake, and worship of the one God in communal life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r1.anchor: Buradan itibaren yedi âyette, sûrenin ana konuları arasında bulunan cemiyet düzeni, bu düzenin harcı durumundaki yapıcı sosyal ilişkiler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r2.claim: Shirk occurs in belief by treating another being as divine or as possessing God's attributes, and in practice by directing worship to others alongside God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r2.anchor: Allah’a başkasını ortak koşmak (şirk) birisi inançta, diğeri amelde ve davranışta olmak üzere iki çeşittir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r3.claim: Arrogance, miserliness, and ostentation bear traces of both kinds of shirk and draw people toward polytheist traits without necessarily making them polytheists.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r3.anchor: Bu âyetlerde kınanan kibir, cimrilik, gösteriş yapma duygu ve eylemlerinde iki çeşit şirkin de izleri vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r4.claim: The arrogant person acts as though independent before God and worships the self.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r4.anchor: Kibirlenen kimse Allah karşısında bağımsızlığını ilân ediyor ve nefsine tapıyor demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r5.claim: The miser is ungrateful for God's favor and distrustful of it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r5.anchor: Cimrilik eden kimsede ise Allah’ın lutfuna karşı nankörlük ve güvensizlik vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r6.claim: Doing good to win people's notice and praise adds motives besides God's approval to worship and servitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r6.anchor: İyiliği insanlar görsün ve kendisini övsünler diye yapanlar ibadet ve kulluğa Allah rızâsından başka unsurlar katmaktadırlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r7.claim: Lying, breaking one's word, and betraying trusts approach hypocrisy without making one a technical hypocrite; the condemned traits similarly approach shirk without making one a polytheist.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r7.anchor: Yalan söylemek, sözünde durmamak, emanete hıyanet etmek nasıl kişiyi –terim anlamında münafık kılmasa bile– münafıklığa yaklaştırıyorsa

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r8.claim: Placing the command to treat parents well immediately after the prohibition of shirk, as in many verses, underscores its importance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r8.anchor: ana-babaya iyi davranma emrinin gelmesi anlamlıdır; işin önemini göstermektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r9.claim: Many verses and hadiths strongly recommend kindness to relatives, orphans, and the poor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r9.anchor: Akrabaya, yetimlere ve yoksullara iyilik etmek birçok âyet ve hadiste hararetle tavsiye edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r10.claim: The verse also includes neighbors, companions, travelers, and people under one's authority among those owed kindness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r10.anchor: Burada komşu, arkadaş, yolcu ve el altında bulunanlar da iyilik (ihsan) edilecekler arasına alınmışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r11.claim: The word jārr derives from terms for nearness and usually denotes people or families in nearby homes; it also applies to other kinds of proximity, such as work or land.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r11.anchor: câr kelimesi, “yakın olma, yakınlık” anlamındaki civâr ve mücâvere masdarlarından isim olup genellikle birbirine yakın meskenlerde yaşayan kişilerin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r12.speaker: Evzâî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r12.claim: Al-Awza'i is reported to count the forty homes on each side of a house as its neighbors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r12.anchor: Evzâî’nin, bir evin farklı yönlerinde bulunan kırkar evi o eve komşu saydığı belirtilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r13.claim: A report counting every home audible from a shout as a neighbor has doubtful authenticity, so the commentary does not rely on that view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r13.anchor: bir evden bağırıldığında sesin duyulabildiği bütün evlerin komşu sayılması gerektiği söylenmişse de bu rivayetlerin sıhhati tartışmalı olduğundan bu görüşe itibar edilmemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r14.speaker: âlimler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r14.claim: Many scholars prefer letting customary usage determine who counts as a neighbor, since Qur'an and sound hadith set no clear boundary and the boundary-setting reports are doubtful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r14.anchor: kimlerin komşu sayılacağını örfün belirlediği görüşünü tercih etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r15.claim: The common interpretation takes the near neighbor as one living closest and the distant neighbor as one living relatively farther away.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r15.anchor: Yaygın yoruma göre âyette geçen “yakın komşu” ile evleri en yakında bulunan komşular, “uzak komşu” ile de nisbeten daha uzakta oturan komşular kastedilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r16.claim: Other reported interpretations distinguish a related from an unrelated neighbor, or a Muslim from a non-Muslim neighbor; the commentary cites al-Zamakhshari and al-Shawkani.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r16.anchor: İlkiyle akrabalık bağı bulunan, ikincisiyle akraba olmayan komşuların veya ilkiyle müslüman, ikincisiyle gayri müslim komşuların kastedildiği gibi daha başka yorumlar da yapılmıştır (Zemahşerî, I, 267-268; Şevkânî, I, 521).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r17.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r17.claim: Al-Qurtubi regards the interpretation that the distant neighbor is non-Muslim as sound.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r17.anchor: Kurtubî, bu son yorumu da sahih bir yorum olarak değerlendirir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r18.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r18.claim: Al-Qurtubi says ihsan can include sharing a neighbor's happiness and sorrow, friendly coexistence, avoiding harm, and protecting the neighbor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r18.anchor: Kurtubî, bu son yorumu da sahih bir yorum olarak değerlendirir; ayrıca âyetteki “ihsân” kelimesinin, yerine göre komşunun mutluluğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r19.claim: A hadith says Gabriel stressed neighbor rights so much that the Prophet thought a neighbor might be made an heir to another neighbor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r20.claim: Hadiths say that a person whose neighbor fears their harm does not have complete faith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r20.anchor: komşusunun, kötülük yapmasından korktuğu kimsenin tam olarak iman etmiş olamayacağı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r21.claim: A hadith says that the best neighbor before God is the one who does the most good for neighbors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r21.anchor: Allah katında en hayırlı komşunun, komşularına en çok iyilik eden kimse olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r22.claim: Hadiths advise neighbors to exchange gifts, starting with those closest by.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r22.anchor: komşuların, en yakın olanlardan başlamak üzere birbiriyle hediyeleşmeleri de öğütlenmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r23.claim: Neighbors form the social circle after family, and every religion and culture has rules for neighborly relations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r23.anchor: Sosyal hayatın aileden sonraki halkasını komşular oluşturduğundan her din ve kültürde komşuluk ilişkileriyle ilgili kurallar bulunur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r24.claim: Islamic sources treat neighbor rights under human rights, whose commands and prohibitions also govern neighborly relations, and discuss neighbor rights specifically as well.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r24.anchor: komşu hakları genel olarak kul hakları (hukuk-ı ibâd) veya insan hakları (hukuk-ı âdemiyyîn) denilen haklar çerçevesinde ele alınır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r25.claim: The evidence rejects as unjust and immoral the Jewish conception that teaches hatred and abasement of outsiders; it also regards the Gospel command to love enemies as unrealistic.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r25.anchor: İslâm’da, yabancılara karşı nefret telkin eden ve onları aşağılayan yahudi telakkisinin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r26.speaker: author
