KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r26.claim: The commentary cites the command not to let anger at a people lead to injustice as clear evidence for fair treatment of disliked groups.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r26.anchor: Bir topluluğa duyduğunuz kızgınlık sizi adaletsizlik yapmaya itmesin. Adaletli olun; bu, takvâya daha uygundur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r27.speaker: âlimler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r27.claim: Scholars who note that hadiths use neighbor without a religious distinction agree that non-Muslim neighbors also have neighborly rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r27.anchor: gibi hadislerde komşuluk kavramının din ayırımı yapılmaksızın mutlak olarak kullanılmasını dikkate alan âlimler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r28.claim: A report assigns related Muslim neighbors kinship, faith, and neighbor rights; unrelated Muslim neighbors faith and neighbor rights; and non-Muslim neighbors neighbor rights. Its authenticity is uncertain, but it fits sound hadiths and general Islamic understanding.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r28.anchor: özellikle komşuları üç gruba ayırarak akraba olan müslüman komşuların akrabalık, dindaşlık ve komşuluk hakları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r29.claim: Helping travelers mattered especially when transport and communication were difficult; it remains needed for travelers in distress, people seeking directions, and those facing language barriers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r29.anchor: Günümüzde de yolculuk esnasında yardıma muhtaç hale gelen, yer ve yol soran, dil bilmediği için iletişimde güçlük çeken kimselere yardım gereği devam etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r30.claim: The verses and hadiths imply a Muslim duty to establish public and civic institutions that help travelers and provide travel guidance for God's sake.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r30.anchor: Allah rızâsı için yolculara yardım eden, seyahat rehberliği yapan resmî ve sivil kurumlar oluşturmanın müslümanlara düşen kulluk vazifeleri arasında bulunduğu ortaya çıkmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r31.claim: Before slavery was abolished, people under one's authority primarily meant slaves; Islam insisted they be treated well and that master-slave relations follow ihsan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r31.anchor: kimseler, kölelik kaldırılmadan önce birinci derecede köleler idi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r32.claim: Though slavery has ended, the powerful still control many vulnerable people; believers should remember all power comes from God and use it for service rather than oppression or exploitation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:36/r32.anchor: Günümüzde kölelik kaldırılmıştır, ancak güçlülerin elleri altında eskiden olduğundan daha çok zayıflar bulunmaktadır.

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r1.claim: A report warns that Qur’anic passages slip from people’s hearts more quickly than tethered camels escape; it rebukes saying “I forgot” and urges review.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r1.anchor: القرآن فلهو اشد تفصيا فى صدور الرجال من النعم فى عقالها

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r2.claim: Reciters should use a toothstick, clean their mouths and bodies, wear perfume and presentable clothes, and honor recitation as speech before the Benefactor.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r2.anchor: يستحب الاستياك وتطهير فمه والطهارة للقراءة باستياكه وتطهير بدنه بالطيب المستحب تكريما لحال التلاوة

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r3.claim: Reciters should sit facing the qibla; Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib sat upright when asked about a hadith because he disliked reporting from the Prophet while reclining, and God’s speech deserves this even more.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r3.anchor: ويستحب أن يكون جالسا مستقبل القبلة سئل سعيد بن المسيب عن حديث وهو متكىء فاستوى جالسا

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r4.speaker: إمام الحرمين وغيره
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r4.claim: Al-Juwaynī and others say recitation in minor ritual impurity is permitted, not disliked; the Prophet recited in every state except major impurity, which is compared to menstruation and postpartum bleeding.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r4.anchor: قال إمام الحرمين وغيره لا يقال إنها مكروهة فقد صح أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ مع الحدث وعلى كل حال سوى الجنابة

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r5.speaker: الشافعى
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r5.claim: In an older position, al-Shāfiʿī allows a menstruating woman to recite if she fears forgetting.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r5.anchor: وللشافعى قول قديم فى الحائض تقرأ خوف النسيان

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r6.speaker: أبو الليث
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Layth permits a menstruating or major-impurity person to recite less than a verse; for instruction, a menstruating student may be prompted half a verse at a time, not a whole verse in one recitation.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الليث لا بأس أن يقرأ الجنب والحائض أقل من آية واحدة قال وإذا أرادت الحائض التعلم فينبغى لها أن تلقن نصف آية

BURHAN:v1p458#2/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r7.claim: Recitation while passing wind is disliked; other minor invalidators such as touch may not be disliked because they are not ordinarily considered impure.
BURHAN:v1p458#2/r7.anchor: وتكره القراءة حال خروج الريح وأما غيره من النواقض كاللمس والمس ونحوه فيحتمل عدم الكراهة لأنه غير مستقذر عادة

NAHHAS:v1p454/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p454/r4.claim: The command is an imperative, with its plural nūn omitted; lā tushrikū is a prohibition.
NAHHAS:v1p454/r4.anchor: أمر فلذلك حذفت منه النون ( ولا تشركوا به شيئا ) نهي

NAHHAS:v1p454/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p454/r5.claim: Iḥsānan is a verbal noun; al-Farrāʾ also allows nominative iḥsān with the bāʾ when its governing verb is unexpressed.
NAHHAS:v1p454/r5.anchor: مصدر قال الفراء ويجوز وبالوالدين إحسان ترفعه بالباء لأن الفعل لم يظهر

NAHHAS:v1p454/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p454/r6.claim: Dhī al-qurbā is genitive after bāʾ, and the orphans, needy, and neighbor are coordinated with it. A Kufan codex wording would require naṣb of “the neighbor of kin” and what follows after an implied verb.
NAHHAS:v1p454/r6.anchor: خفض بالباء ( واليتامى والمساكين والجار ذي القربى ) عطف كله قال الفراء وفي مصاحف أهل الكوفة

NAHHAS:v1p454/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r7.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p454/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash explains al-jār al-junub as a neighbor with no kinship, distant from one’s family; the poetic line uses junub for “to the side.”
NAHHAS:v1p454/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش الجار الجنب المجانب للقرابة أي ليس بينك وبينه قرابة وحكى والجار الجنب وأنشد ( الناس جنب والأمير جنب )

NAHHAS:v1p454/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r8.speaker: أبو مكوزة
NAHHAS:v1p454/r8.claim: Abū Makūza says al-ṣāḥib bi-l-janb is the person beside you; al-Akhfash agrees and cites expressions for someone being at your side.
NAHHAS:v1p454/r8.anchor: سألت أبا مكوزة الأعرابي عن الصاحب بالجنب فقال هو الذي بجنبك وكذا قال الأخفش هو الذي بجنبك

NAHHAS:v1p454/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r9.speaker: أبو مكوزة
NAHHAS:v1p454/r9.claim: Abū Makūza also explains al-jār al-junub as someone who comes and lodges wherever you lodge, within sight.
NAHHAS:v1p454/r9.anchor: سألت أبا مكوزة عن الجار الجنب فقال هو الذي يجيء ويحل حيث يحل تقع عليه عينك

NAHHAS:v1p454/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p454/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p454/r10.claim: The phrase is genitive by coordination: show kindness to those your right hands possess.

ITQAN:v1p279#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r1.claim: Wudu is recommended before Quran recitation because reciting is a superior form of remembrance, and a hadith says the Prophet disliked remembering God except in purity.
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r1.anchor: يستحب الوضوء لقراءة القرآن لأنه أفضل الأذكار وقد كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكره أن يذكر الله إلا على طهر

ITQAN:v1p279#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r2.speaker: إمام الحرمين
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r2.claim: Al-Juwayni says recitation is not disliked for a person in minor ritual impurity, citing an authentic report that the Prophet recited while not in ablution.
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r2.anchor: قال إمام الحرمين ولا تكره القراءة للمحدث لأنه صح أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ مع الحدث

ITQAN:v1p279#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r3.speaker: شرح المهذب
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r3.claim: The commentary says to pause recitation during an ongoing passing of wind; a person in major impurity or menstruating may not recite but may look at the codex or recite inwardly.
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r3.anchor: وأما الجنب والحائض فتحرم عليهما القراءة نعم يجوز لهما النظر في المصحف وإمراره على القلب

ITQAN:v1p279#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r4.speaker: شرح المهذب
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r4.claim: The commentary says recitation with an impure mouth is disliked; another view makes it forbidden, by analogy with touching the codex with an impure hand.
ITQAN:v1p279#3/r4.anchor: وأما متنجس الفم فتكره له القراءة وقيل تحرم كمس المصحف باليد النجسة

DAMGHANI:v1p261/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p261/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p261/r8.claim: Shirk with God means setting another beside Him; the cited warnings concern those who assign Him partners.
DAMGHANI:v1p261/r8.anchor: الشرك بالله تعالى وهو أن يعدل به غيره قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r1.claim: The root sense of worship is humility; a road called muʿabbad is leveled and made easy.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r1.anchor: الأصل في العبادة : الذل . يقال : طريق معبد ، أي : مذلل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r2.claim: Worshiping God means humbling oneself through obedience to His commands and avoiding what He prohibits.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r2.anchor: وعبادة الله تعالى : الذل له بالانقياد لما أمر والانتهاء عما نهى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r3.claim: Some define worship as actions reaching the utmost possible humility and submission, beyond one servant’s submission to another.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r3.anchor: وحد بعضهم العبادة فقال : هي الأفعال الواقعة على نهاية ما يمكن من التذلل والخضوع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r4.claim: Worship can mean affirming God’s oneness, as in commands to worship God alone and the prophets’ calls to their peoples.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p431#2/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن العبادة في القرآن على وجهين : أحدهما : التوحيد

BURHAN:v2p131/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p131/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p131/r7.claim: The saying to honor one's guest is connected to Abraham's honored guests and Qur'anic duties toward neighbor, companion, and traveler.
BURHAN:v2p131/r7.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليكرم ضيفه فى قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v2p131/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p131/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p131/r8.claim: Good conduct means guarding secrets and others from harm, speaking good or staying silent, treating neighbors well, and honoring guests; a believer may enter Paradise if given a good end.
BURHAN:v2p131/r8.anchor: وهذه الأربع كلمات جمعن حسن الصحبة للخلق لأن من كف سره وأذاه وقال خيرا أو صمت عن الشر

DAMGHANI:v1p274/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r2.claim: A ṣāḥib can mean a travel companion or fellow traveler.
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r2.anchor: والصاحب بالجنب يعني الرفيق في السفر

DAMGHANI:v1p314/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r3.claim: ʿIbādah can mean worshipping God alone or affirming His oneness.
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r3.anchor: اعبدوا يعني وحدوا قوله تعالى في سورة هود

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r12.claim: Al-ṣāḥib bi-l-janb can mean a traveling companion; the source also reports that it may mean a wife at home.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r12.anchor: الثاني الجنب السفر قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r14.claim: Janb can mean distant or remote, as in seeing Moses from afar and the neighbor who is far off.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r14.anchor: الرابع الجنب البعيد قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r1.claim: Sahib means companion; its plural forms include sahb, sihab, and ashab, and it can also describe a master, slave, scholar, or student through association.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r1.anchor: الصاحب : القرين ، والجمع صحب وصحاب وأصحاب . ويقال للسيد : صاحب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r9.claim: Sahib denotes a bondservant in the source's gloss of 4:36.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الصاحب في القرآن على تسعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r5.claim: The broadest Qur'anic sense is associating another with God, illustrated by commands against shirk and the declaration of disavowal from polytheists.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الشرك في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p83/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p83/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p83/r1.claim: An-Nisa repeats ب with ذي القربى because the surah’s broader subject is kinship, adding emphasis and detail; Baqara omits it for concision because that is not its context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p83/r1.anchor: ذكر الباء مع ذي القربى في هذه الآية من سورة النساء كان لمراعاة التفضيل والتوكيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p533/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p533/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p533/r2.claim: Al-Baqara omits the preposition before kin for brevity because kinship is not its context; Al-Nisāʾ retains it to emphasize kin, a topic sustained through that sūra.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p533/r2.anchor: وذلك لأن السياق في سورة النساء والكلام عن القرابات من أول السورة إلى آخرها

NASHR:v1p299/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p299/r7.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v1p299/r7.claim: Yaqub joins Abu Amr in assimilating bāʾ in the single phrase wa-l-sahibi bil-janb.
NASHR:v1p299/r7.anchor: ووافقه يعقوب على إدغام الباء في موضع واحد، وهو والصاحب بالجنب في النساء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.claim: The Qur'an's commands and recommendations about goodness, prayer, and care speak of الوالدين, not الأبوين; he illustrates this with 17:23, 4:36, and 6:151.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.anchor: لا تجد في القرآن الكريم البر أو الدعاء أو التوصية إلا بذكر الوالدين لا الأبوين
